
# API Endpoints

Any node with the `ingress` role (`api.port > 0` in Tier A) serves the Crewlet API. A node has every role by default and runs it beside the agents in one process; a node with `-roles data,ingress` serves only these routes and reaches the rest of the fleet over the event stream. The routes are identical either way.

A node **without** `ingress` still binds `api.port`, and serves the network only its two probes there, `/health` and `/ready`: see [Probes on a node without ingress](#probes-on-a-node-without-ingress). An executor run in a box that does not share its node's loopback reaches its tools through an ingress node's [tool bridge](#routes), which relays each call to the node holding the seat; a `direct` run on its own host dials it on loopback, where it serves the bridge to its own host alone.

Nothing to install: the API is compiled into the binary, with the dashboard and the WebSocket that is the dashboard's data plane (see [`WS /ws/stream`](#ws-wsstream)).

---

## Which listener serves what

Every route is served on `api.port`, unless the node's Tier A sets `api.public.port`. Then the routes **outside parties** call (authenticated by a provider signature or a signed per-run token, never an operator credential) move to that listener and are served nowhere else:

| Prefix | Who calls it | Without `api.public` | With `api.public` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/webhooks/*` | Vendors (deliveries, the MCP sign-in's client metadata document) and a person's browser returning from a vendor's app flow or sign-in (`/webhooks/slack-oauth`, `/webhooks/github-app`, `/webhooks/mcp-oauth`) | `api.port` | `api.public` only |
| `/otlp/{token}/v1/{signal}` | A box exporting its executor's telemetry | `api.port` | `api.public` only |
| `/mcp/{token}` | A seat's executor run, in its box, calling the seat's tools, each of its MCP servers (`/mcp/{token}/server/{server}`), polling its turn's notes (`/mcp/{token}/steer/{notes,read}`) and reporting each skill it loads (`/mcp/{token}/skill`) | `api.port` | `api.public` only |
| `/box/git/*` | A box's git, with its run's own token as git's Basic password ([Coding boxes](../concepts/gitlet.md#coding-boxes)) or its check's ([Check boxes](../concepts/gitlet.md#check-boxes)); mounted where `gitlet` is among the node's roles | `api.port` | `api.public` only |
| `/box/gitlet/*` | A check's box reading the commit its check measures, with its check's token ([Check boxes](../concepts/gitlet.md#check-boxes)); mounted where `gitlet` is among the node's roles | `api.port` | `api.public` only |
| `/git/*`, `/gitlet/*` | A person's git client, with their own token; the CLI | `api.port` | `api.port` only, never published: the credential is a person's own token ([Gitlet](#gitlet-git-and-gitlet)) |
| Everything else: `/health`, `/ready`, `/`, `/dashboard`, `/favicon.ico`, `/static/*`, `/auth/*`, `/iam/*`, `/ws/stream`, `/query/*`, every REST read, `/config`, `/secrets`, `/setup`, `/operator/*`, `/backup`, the `/worklet/*` and `/fleet/*` gestures | People, the dashboard, the CLI, orchestrators | `api.port` | `api.port` only |

A public route asked of `api.port` answers `404` `no_route` with a `hint` naming `api.public` (the caller is on the operator's own network, likely a vendor with the wrong port). Every other route asked of the public listener answers exactly what an unserved path answers (the same `404 no_route`, the same generic hint), so the published socket reveals nothing of the admin routes. It decides before the guard runs and asks for no credential, so a guarded route there is that `404` whatever credential is sent. The probes are deliberately **not** public (`/health` describes the node to whoever runs it): point every health check at `api.port`. A node without `ingress` serves the network only its [probes](#probes-on-a-node-without-ingress) on `api.port`, on either listener, plus the routes its own boxes dial on its host's loopback; with `api.port` `0` it serves nothing. See [Deployment → Exposing webhooks without the admin API](../guides/deployment.md#exposing-webhooks-without-the-admin-api).

---

## Request timeouts

Three deadlines bound a request on **every** route, each covering a phase the others do not. None is configurable.

| Phase | Bound | What it stops |
|---|---|---|
| Request line and headers | 10 s | A connection opened and left silent. |
| Reading the request body | 30 s | A client that *dribbles* a body under every size cap a few bytes at a time (a cap alone stops only the other failure). 30 s carries the largest other body, a 25 MiB webhook delivery, at about 7 Mbit/s. A project file's upload is the one exception: it streams up to a gibibyte, so it is held to thirty seconds for each mebibyte (see [Project files](#project-files)). |
| Between keep-alive requests | 60 s | A client that finished a request and went quiet while holding its connection slot. |

A body that misses its deadline fails like any truncated delivery: `400` `unreadable_body` (logged as `webhook_body_unreadable` on a webhook path). There is **no** whole-request timeout: it would have to fit the largest body on the slowest link, bounding nothing on a small one. Long-lived responses, [`WS /ws/stream`](#ws-wsstream) above all, bound themselves.

---

## Every refusal is one envelope

A refused request, on any route and surface and whatever the status, is one JSON object with the same three parts:

```json
{
  "error": "no_external_url",
  "message": "No external address is set. Set `api.external_url` in this node's config file and restart.",
  "config_path": "api.external_url",
  "hint": "Set the HTTPS address third-party apps reach this deployment on; without it the pass can register no webhook."
}
```

- **`error` is the code, and the only thing to branch on.** One closed vocabulary (`internal/api/httpjson`) is shared by every surface, so a failure has one name everywhere: a `413` is `body_too_large` for a config document, a secret value or a webhook delivery, and an unserved query is `unknown_query` over the WebSocket and its REST twin. Never parse the message.
- **`message` is one sentence for a person**, product copy the dashboard renders verbatim. It belongs to the *code*, not the call site; a route with more to say puts it in the detail. A code whose refusals have different remedies picks its sentence by the facts the detail carries: `unauthorized` says the rule its `reason` names ([below](#which-permission-a-route-needs)); a `503` `unavailable` or `identity_unavailable` with no `Retry-After` says waiting won't change it, and under a `Retry-After` says to try again in a moment (a write whose `outcome` is `unknown` keeps the code's own sentence, since it may have landed). Never match on it: the wording can change. Every refusal carries one, `/config`, `/secrets`, `/setup` and every `/webhooks/*` route included (no `invalid signature` code with a space, no `{"status": "unavailable", "reason": …}` shape; see [Webhook refusals](#webhook-refusals)).
- **Everything else is the detail**: machine-readable facts about *this* refusal as typed JSON beside the two reserved keys, not nested: `config_path` and `hint` above, `fields` on an integration missing values, `current_revision_id` on a lost update, `problems` on a refused configuration document. Values keep their types (a count is a number, located problems a list). The text keys `detail` (what happened) and `hint` (what to do) are sentences: a capital first letter, unless the text opens with a field name, flag, path, address or Go package prefix (`statelog: …`), and a full stop. The WebSocket's error frames write `detail` the same way.
- **A `503` says when, or says it will not help.** A `503` that waiting clears (a node behind its log, an unreachable coordination store, a write whose outcome is unknown, an integration another pass holds: `surface_busy`) carries a `Retry-After` in seconds, derived from the refusal where it knows (a node behind its log estimates from its backlog) and a few seconds otherwise. A `503` no wait changes carries NONE, and the detail names what to do instead. That is a state-log refusal waiting cannot clear on THIS node: a node evicted from the fleet, one holding a record it cannot decode, a log at its byte ceiling (`log_full`), a record larger than the broker takes in one message (`record_too_large`), one the broker refused for its own reason (`broker_refused`), a deleted object. It applies on every surface that answers one with a `503` (`/worklet`, `/doclet/pages`, `/chatlet`, `/artifacts` with its datastore's `/artifacts/{id}/data`, `/artifact-folders`, `/brand`, `/operator/act`, `/iam`, `/auth`, `/config`, `/setup`, `/secrets`, `/assistant`, and every question the query registry answers, `/query/{what}` and its named read routes). The same request is refused however often sent: ask another node, split the change, or have an operator readmit, upgrade or resize; never poll this one. The detail says which, in a sentence for the reader (asking them to try again in a moment exactly where a `Retry-After` is sent), never in the refusal's own text (positions, settings, the broker's words), which goes to the node's log. `/operator/act`, and the human write surface's tool-backed routes and tool-less verbs, carry no detail (ADR-0060): the code's `message` stands alone beside the header. [Read consistency](../guides/consistency.md#a-writes-refusals) says what each asks of whom.
- **A write that may have landed is not a refusal, and says so as a field.** A `503` about a write this node cannot account for carries **`"outcome": "unknown"`** and the **`op_id`** to retry under, on every surface that writes through a state log (`/worklet`, `/doclet/pages`, `/chatlet`, `/artifacts` with its datastore's `/artifacts/{id}/data`, `/artifact-folders`, `/brand`, `/operator/act`, `/iam`, `/auth`, `/assistant`). A `503` without `outcome` is a refusal and wrote nothing: a gesture refused partway lists what landed before it as `landed`, and a `/setup` submission the credentials it sealed first (below). The two send a client opposite ways: retry the unknown under the **same** `op_id`, never a fresh one, which would make the change twice if the first landed. Branch on the field, not the sentence. The routes that read no `Idempotency-Key` (a token's mint, every `/auth` gesture) are the exception the `detail` names: there the `op_id` finds the attempt in the trail, and the retry is the gesture asked again. Where this node's operation ledger cannot vouch for the operation it also carries **`"unvouched": true`** and **no** `Retry-After`: the same request here answers the same way until the change reaches this node, so send it, with the same `op_id`, through another node. `outcome`, `op_id` and `unvouched` are the answer's own and no route's detail displaces them. The config surface and a [`/setup`](#supplying-them) submission carry no operation, so their unknown has no `op_id`: it names the revision stored and the `node` whose history alone holds it, and the pointer says whether it landed; it is not sent again either (see [`/config`'s status codes](#status-codes)). A `/setup` `503` **without** `outcome` left the company document as it was, but names the credentials it sealed before the refusal as `wrote_secrets`, and the one whose write the store did not answer (it may have landed) as `unanswered_secret`. Its remedy is the plain `503`'s: send the submission again as it stands, which rewrites every credential in it by name.
- **A `500 internal_error` carries no reason.** Its sentence says the reason is in this node's log: a fault's own words are a store's or driver's (a database path, a connection string), and holding a permission does not make a caller someone they are meant for. A route may say what the request carried and what already landed (`/iam` does, beside the code), never what failed underneath.

`error` and `message` are RESERVED: a route's detail can never displace them.

Two shapes sit outside this envelope. A **WebSocket query answer** is a frame, `{"kind": "error", "id", "what", "error"}`, with no `message`: the client switches on the value and the dashboard holds each code's sentence (see [`WS /ws/stream`](#ws-wsstream)). A refusal on **authority** is the exception: its frame carries the same `reason` and `grants` as the REST envelope, under the same keys. And routes that are not JSON at all (the dashboard shell, the Slack OAuth landing) answer as what they are.

---

## While a node is starting

`crewlet run` binds `api.port` (and `api.public` and `api.artifacts`, where served) as soon as it has read and checked its Tier A, before it opens its store, and logs `api_bound`. A port someone else holds fails the boot at once, naming the address. Until the node's own surface takes the socket over (logged as `api_listening`, or `api_probes_listening` on a node without `ingress`), it answers its probes and tells a caller to come back for any route it will serve, and only for one it will serve:

| Request | While the node starts | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /health`, on `api.port` | `503` while the node recovers what it holds, then `200`, `status: "starting"` both times | The `503` is what a startup probe sized for the node's store (and, on a fleet's data node, for the join it may make) bounds; nothing after the recovery holds it. See the phases below. |
| `GET /ready`, on `api.port` | `503`, `reason: "starting"` | The node takes no traffic until it serves, so no load balancer or rollout counts it. |
| A route this listener will serve | `503 starting`, with `Retry-After: 10` | The caller is told to come back instead of meeting a refused connection, which reads as a node that is not there. On an `ingress` node that is every route of [Which listener serves what](#which-listener-serves-what) on its listener; a node without `ingress` serves the network no route but its probes, and one that runs seats tells a caller on its own host's loopback to come back for `/mcp/` and `/otlp/`, the routes its boxes dial (a `direct` run outlives its node's restart and calls back while it starts). |
| A request on the artifact origin (`api.artifacts`) | An empty `503` with `Retry-After: 10` for a ticketed path, the runtime or the kit, and the empty `404` or `405` the origin gives anything else | The origin's refusal under its own inert headers, never a JSON body an artifact page could read. |
| Anything else | The `404` that listener answers once the node serves | A socket says no more while starting than afterwards, and nobody waits for a route this node never serves. On `api.public`: the router's `404 no_route`, probes included. On `api.port` of an `ingress` node with `api.public` set: the `404` naming `api.public` for a route outside parties call. On `api.port` of a node without `ingress`: the router's `404` for every path but the two probes and, from its host's loopback on a node that runs seats, its boxes' two routes (once serving, its guard answers `401` for a path that asks for a credential). |

Nothing here asks for a credential, since nothing served could be unlocked. Every answer carries the node's security headers, and on an `ingress` node its CORS permission, so a dashboard on an origin `api.auth.allowed_origins` lists reads `starting` rather than a network error; a path with a dot segment is refused `400 non_canonical_path` as always.

`/health` names how far the boot has got:

```json
{
  "status": "starting",
  "node": "core-1",
  "version": "v0.4.0",
  "phase": "recovering"
}
```

| `phase` | `/health` | What the node is doing |
|---|---|---|
| `recovering` | `503` | Opening and recovering what it holds: its store and that release's schema migrations, the embedded broker's file store and listeners, JetStream catching up with peers (or, on a node without `data`, its leaf link to a member), the streams and buckets it provisions, the batches of a stateless node's events its event log left unsettled, the replicated estate and its state logs, and a joining node's snapshot. It takes as long as the store is large, and on a fleet's data node whose rows the logs can no longer bring level, as long as fetching a peer's snapshot of the whole replicated estate takes (budgeted by `stream.tracker_retention.rejoin_window`, projected by `crewlet retention status`; a lone data node never fetches one). The deployment bounds it with a startup probe: see [Sizing the startup probe](../guides/deployment.md#sizing-the-startup-probe). A join logs `statelog_join_progress` every ten seconds while it transfers. It ends with `engine_recovered` in the log. Applying the state logs is not part of it: that catches up in the background, and what waits for it is the node's first seat, never `/health`. |
| `preparing` | `200` | Bringing up what its company configures: the snapshot of the company's secrets its `${VAR}` references resolve from, the company built from its document, shared MCP servers, sandboxes, Worklet, Doclet and Chatlet, the harnesses' credential bundles, the first apply of the revision it boots on, and the dashboard's projection. None holds a probe. A part that waits on something else is bounded by its own setting (a tool server by its `startup_timeout_seconds`), but the first apply has no deadline beyond its parts', so a part that never returns leaves the node here with `/ready` naming `starting`, and nothing restarts it: watch for a node that stays unready (see [Sizing the startup probe](../guides/deployment.md#sizing-the-startup-probe)). So does a secret store that does not answer: the node builds no company from the environment alone, and asks again, logging `secret_store_unreadable`, until it answers. A value its keyring cannot open ends the boot instead, naming the secret. |

Every field of that body is a field of [the health envelope](#the-health-envelope) under the same name, so a script reads one shape whichever answered. It omits every fact about a running engine (queue, seats, posture, applied epoch, `started_at`), since a zero would be a fiction. The envelope carries no `phase`: the node answering it is serving.

`/ready` says the same in its own shape:

```json
{
  "ready": false,
  "node": "core-1",
  "configured": false,
  "draining": false,
  "posture": "",
  "reason": "starting"
}
```

`configured` is `false` because no revision is active in this process yet, whatever its store holds, and `posture` is empty because nothing has concluded one. A route the node will serve is refused in the engine's envelope:

```json
{
  "error": "starting",
  "message": "This node is still starting and is not serving yet. Try again in a moment.",
  "detail": "This node is recovering what it holds (its store, its broker and its copy of the estate) and serves nothing until it has started.",
  "hint": "Retry after the Retry-After: once the node serves, /health stops answering status \"starting\" and /ready stops naming reason \"starting\"."
}
```

A node told to stop before it serves (a signal during the boot) answers a drain's answers as far as it can: `/health` says `status: "shutting_down"` but keeps its phase's status code (`503` while it recovers, since a stop does not cut a recovery short and the startup probe still bounds it, `200` after), `/ready` answers `reason: "draining"` and `draining: true`, and every route it would have served answers `503 draining` with the drain's `Retry-After` of 30 seconds.

---

## During a drain

A node told to stop (SIGTERM, or `Ctrl+C` once) keeps serving HTTP for the whole of its [drain](../concepts/agent-runtime.md#graceful-shutdown) and closes its listener only once the drain completes. From the drain's first moment it takes only some requests:

| Request | During a drain | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /health` | `200`, `status: "shutting_down"` | Liveness. An orchestrator that could not reach the node would kill it mid-turn. |
| `GET /ready` | `503`, `reason: "draining"` | Takes the node out of rotation so traffic moves to a peer. |
| Every other read (`GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`): the dashboard, the REST reads, `/query/*`, `/ws/stream`, a check's box's reads of its commit (`/box/gitlet/*`) | Served | A read starts nothing, and it is how the drain is watched. |
| `/mcp/{token}` (its MCP servers, notes route and skill route included) and `/otlp/{token}/v1/{signal}` | Served | They carry the tool calls, notes and spans of executors launched before the drain. An [executor in its box](../concepts/code-sandbox.md) outlives the turn segment that launched it, so the drain never waits on one; refusing these would shorten no drain and only break an executor mid-flight. A tool call whose executor's seat is held by another node is relayed there, as outside a drain. |
| A git fetch already begun: `POST /git/{repo}/git-upload-pack` | Served, and finished before the listener closes | The upload `POST` continues a fetch whose advertisement was answered before the drain, on this node or a peer (git keeps no state between an exchange's requests); refusing it would break the fetch half done. It is the one request under `/git/` a draining node serves. A box's `POST /box/git/{repo}/git-upload-pack` (a coding box's or a check's) is the same request, served the same. |
| A new git fetch: `GET`/`HEAD /git/{repo}/info/refs` asking for `git-upload-pack` (or no service) | `503`, `text/plain` | The advertisement begins every fetch, and a fetch runs git's upload-pack here after syncing the repository from the object store: new work the shutdown would wait out. Refused at its first request, a clone fails at once and is retried against a peer rather than cut part way. A box's under `/box/git/` (a coding box's or a check's) is the same. |
| A download: `GET /git/{repo}/-/raw`, `GET /git/{repo}/-/archive.zip` | `503`, `text/plain` | New work: a sync and a git process on the transfer lane. One begun before the drain finishes before the listener closes. |
| A git push: `GET`/`HEAD /git/{repo}/info/refs` asking for any other service, `POST /git/{repo}/git-receive-pack`, and every other path under `/git/` but the two downloads | `503`, `text/plain` | Every request of a push is refused, its advertisement included, because the `GET` is where git prints the reason (`remote: this node is draining …`); on the `POST` it prints only `RPC failed; HTTP 503`. In git's own form, not the JSON below, which git prints as nothing. A coding box's push under `/box/git/` is refused the same. |
| Every `/webhooks/*` route, whatever its method | `503` | A delivery is new work, and one of the two `GET` landings acts: the GitHub App return seals a credential and writes a config revision, and an install arrival asks the reconcile loop for a pass. The Slack OAuth landing only renders a page and is refused with the rest, since a per-route carve-out is what refusing by default avoids. |
| Every other write: `/config`, `/secrets`, `/setup`, `/backup`, the `/worklet/*` writes, `POST /operator/mcp`, `POST /operator/act/{tool}` | `503` | Each starts work or changes the company the drain is leaving. Refusing by default keeps a later write route from slipping through. `POST /secrets/reveal` rides with them although it changes nothing (it is a `POST` so the names travel in a body), and the CLI run asking it is told to try another node, as for a write. |

`/operator/mcp` serves only `POST`: it is served [statelessly](#every-call-is-decided-by-the-request-that-carries-it) with no session, so there is no `GET` stream to open or session to end. Every JSON-RPC call it carries, reads and a new listening stream included, is refused with the writes (telling a listing from a filed task would mean reading the body, the per-route carve-out refusing by default avoids). An assistant asking a draining node is told to retry elsewhere, like the dashboard. A stream an assistant opened BEFORE the drain is kept for the whole drain and goes on hearing every other node's rebuild of its tools ([`/operator/mcp`](#operatormcp--your-own-assistant)), since ending it would cut off, for the drain's whole length, a client that opens no new stream (the Go SDK's does not). It is answered, and so ends, as the listener starts to close, so it never holds the listener's five seconds. `/mcp/{token}` is not split: the whole prefix is served, since an executor's tool calls are the one thing on this listener the node must not break.

A refusal is `503` with a `Retry-After` of 30 seconds, long enough for a load balancer following `/ready` to have moved traffic to a peer, and a body the CLI and dashboard both render, everywhere but `/git/*`, whose refusal is the one `text/plain` line `this node is draining for a shutdown and begins no new fetch or push: retry in 30 s, against another node or once it has restarted` (a download's says `begins no new download`):

```json
{
  "error": "draining",
  "message": "This node is shutting down and is not taking new work. Try another node, or this one once it has restarted.",
  "detail": "This node is draining for a shutdown: the turns already running finish, and nothing new is started here.",
  "hint": "Retry against another node, or once this one has restarted; /ready answers 503 for as long as the drain lasts."
}
```

A write still needs its token first: an unauthenticated write answers `401` whether or not the node is draining. A request already running when the drain began is cut only if still running five seconds after the listener starts to close; except an assistant's listening stream, answered the moment the listener starts to close, and a connection that has sent no request, closed then, so `api_shutdown_failed` keeps meaning a request was stuck.

**A git request is finished, not cut.** A clone or push cut part way restarts from nothing against a peer, so every rolling restart would pay twice, and five seconds is a REST read's grace, not a transfer's. So once the turns have finished, and before the listener starts to close, the node waits for every git request it is serving: a push, fetch or download running when the drain began, and a fetch's upload `POST` served during it. Because git keeps no state between an exchange's requests, it then goes on listening five seconds after the last of them ends (git's own keepalive interval, many times the pause between two requests of one exchange), so a fetch between rounds does not face a closed port. The drain begins no fetch or push, but serves every upload `POST` that reaches it (a fetch begun on a peer, which a load balancer keeps sending here until it acts on `/ready`, or under Kubernetes until the pod leaves its Service's endpoints), so the wait can grow and ends once that traffic has moved and what was running is done. The deployment guide's [`preStop` sleep](../guides/deployment.md#separate-processes-a-split-deployment) shortens that window. The node logs `git_draining` with the count when there is something to wait for and `git_drain_complete` when done. Like the wait for the turns, it has no deadline of its own: the supervisor's kill grace or a second interrupt bounds it (see [Graceful shutdown](../concepts/agent-runtime.md#graceful-shutdown) for sizing the grace).

A node with a [public listener](#which-listener-serves-what) drains both by this one table (webhooks refused on `api.public`, sandbox endpoints served there), and closes `api.public` first, then `api.port`, each with its own five seconds, so `/health` answers until the very end even while an open bridge session holds the public listener for its whole grace.

---

## A request nothing serves, and an answer with no code

The [envelope](#every-refusal-is-one-envelope) covers a request nothing serves as well as a route's refusal: `404 no_route` for a path this build does not have or this node does not serve now (such as `POST /worklet/items/{key}/purge` on a company that does not run Worklet), and `405 method_not_allowed` for a path this build's routes take under other methods. Both carry a `detail` naming the method and path; the 405 carries an `Allow` header naming the methods this build's route table holds for the path, which does not promise this node serves them now: a route it does not serve now still answers a wrong method `405`, and then `404 no_route` under the methods `Allow` named.

The CLI and dashboard rely on it. A non-2xx answer with no code was written by something **in front of** the node (most often a reverse proxy's read timeout) and says nothing about what the node did, so a write that meets one is reported as *unknown*, with the operation id to finish it under, not as refused. A refusal from the node means nothing was done.

**Every answer the node's API writes carries `X-Crewlet-Engine: 1`**: a route's answer, every refusal, the router's own `404` and `405`, the canonical-path refusal and the `503 starting`. A body alone cannot say whose answer it is (a proxy can answer JSON with an `error` field); nothing in front of the node sets this header. The dashboard and CLI read an answer as the node's only when it carries both the header and a code, so a proxy's `401`, `403` or `413` is never read as a refused token, a grant to ask for or a smaller document. A proxy must pass the header through unchanged; one that strips it makes every answer read as one the node never gave, so a write's outcome is reported unknown, never refused. A dashboard on another origin (`api.auth.allowed_origins`) reads it because the node exposes it to permitted origins (`Access-Control-Expose-Headers`, beside the `ETag`, `Retry-After` and `X-Request-Id` it reads too); a proxy that rewrites that header must keep `X-Crewlet-Engine` in it.

**Except under `/git/*`, where the node answers in git's form.** A git client prints a refusal's body only when it is `text/plain` (each line as `remote: …`) and prints the API's JSON as nothing, so every refusal the node writes there is one `text/plain` line, no envelope: the guard's `401` Basic challenge ([the auth note under Routes](#routes)); its `403` for a credential acting as a seat the org chart no longer holds as a human seat, or a session that may only enrol a second factor, and its `503` for a node that cannot tell who the credential is (`Retry-After: 2`), each the envelope's sentence; a refusal of the route's own authority verb, its sentence with the code in brackets after it; a node that serves none of Gitlet now, likewise ([git's smart HTTP](#gits-smart-http)); and the drain's `503` ([During a drain](#during-a-drain)). So the inference above (no code means something in front of the node wrote it) holds on every route but `/git/*`, where the node's refusal is told from a proxy's by its own `text/plain` sentence (`authentication required: …`, `this node is draining …`), which git prints to the person who ran the command. `/gitlet/*`, Gitlet's REST reads, answers JSON with a code like every other route.

---
## Routes

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/health` | Liveness + the engine-health envelope (see [below](#the-health-envelope)). Stays `200` through a drain (see [During a drain](#during-a-drain)); use `/ready` to steer traffic. Before the node serves it answers a shorter body: `503` while recovering, `200` after (see [While a node is starting](#while-a-node-is-starting)) |
| `GET` | `/ready` | Readiness for a load balancer: `503` with `reason: "starting"` before the node serves (see [While a node is starting](#while-a-node-is-starting)), then `503` while draining, before the first config revision applies, on a `shed` or `stuck` posture, or while this node can no longer route the estate's reads and writes; `200` otherwise. A `503` names why in `reason`: `draining`, `unconfigured`, `shed` or `stuck`, then `estate_behind`, in that order of precedence. `estate_behind` also gives a node's seats back ([`unserviceable`](../concepts/seat-ownership.md#a-copy-that-is-behind-and-a-copy-that-is-wrong)): its calls need another data node (its own copy is out of service) and its view of who serves the estate has been unreadable over 60 seconds. A copy that is merely behind never takes a node out of rotation. The deciding term is logged at debug (`ready_withheld_for_the_estate`), never in the body. It never reads the fleet's presence or alarm counts. A node without the `ingress` role answers a different question here, whether it is doing its work: see [Probes on a node without ingress](#probes-on-a-node-without-ingress) |
| `GET` | `/agents` | List agent roles, each merged with live state from the in-memory projection (including the in-flight `live_calls`). [Human seats](../concepts/humans-in-the-org.md) are excluded; they appear only in `/org` with `"kind": "human"` |
| `GET` | `/agents/{id}` | Single agent: `handle`, `agent_id`, `role` (its name), the live overlay (incl. `live_calls`), and `llm_history`, the seat's finished phases newest first, capped at 50. `{id}` is the seat's **handle** (every roster row's `id`); a role name is NOT accepted (two seats may share one). A handle no agent seat answers to is `404` |
| `GET` | `/agents/{id}/memory` | Durable memories (personal, episodic, counterparty, synthesized skills). `{id}` is the seat's handle, resolved to the derived agent id the diary is keyed by |
| `GET` | `/agents/{id}/memory/episodes/{episode}` | One episode **whole**, ask and account complete (the memory listing carries only their openings; see [below](#get-agentsidmemoryepisodesepisode)) |
| `GET` | `/agents/{id}/sessions` | The seat's **executor sessions**, latest begun first, paged: each turn whose executor captured its harness's session or read its conversation, how it ended, what it was asked, whether its session is still kept, and whether a relaunch of it (or, once ended, its conversation's next turn) would continue it. The seat's trail, `audit.seat.read` (see [below](#get-agentsidsessions)) |
| `GET` | `/agents/{id}/sessions/{turn_id}` | One turn's session and a page of its **transcript**, read from its sealed object as its harness recorded it, redacted; an object that is gone or does not open is an answer saying so (see [below](#get-agentsidsessionsturn_id)) |
| `GET` | `/org` | The company's charter and its seat and unit tree, in a public shape with no contact identity, email, credential or deployment setting (see [below](#get-org)). Human seats appear with `"kind": "human"` |
| `GET` | `/tools` | Registered tools, each with its `source` (`builtin` or `mcp:<server>`; see [Where a tool comes from](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#where-a-tool-comes-from)), behavioural `annotations`, where it `delivers`, and its `input_schema` (see [below](#the-tool-catalogue)) |
| `GET` | `/events` | Recent engine events from the event store (`limit` caps at 400; keyset-paged, see below) |
| `GET` | `/events/{event_id}` | Single event incl. payload, within the 30-day history (`event_history_seconds`) like every read of the log: an older event answers `not_found`, since every data node floors its lookup at the serving node's horizon (see [coverage](#reading-the-fleets-history-coverage)) |
| `GET` | `/events/trace/{trace_id}` | All events in one trace, oldest first, capped at 500 |
| `GET` | `/tokens/breakdown` | Token-spend rollup by phase / model / provider entry / worker / seat: the live 24 hours, or any window of up to 90 company days from the replicated usage domain (see [below](#token-spend-breakdown)) |
| `GET` | `/tokens/series` | The same spend **with a time axis**: one bucket per company day or ISO week, split into bands (see [below](#get-tokensseries)) |
| `GET` | `/tokens/turn-outcomes` | Over the same window as `/tokens` (`days`, `since` and `until`, `previous`, `seat`), each agent's started turns by what woke them (`wake`, as the turn ledger keys it: `schedule:<name>`, `work_item:<reason>`, `chat_message:<reason>` and the like), with `turns` and `tokens` (input, output and auxiliary calls'; the prompt cache is a share of the input, never added), and `nothing` and `nothing_tokens` for turns that committed nothing. An executor turn's outcome and tokens settle when its run is collected, the run's own writes and model tokens included |
| `GET` | `/agents/activity` | Every seat's turns over a window of company days: counts, first-pass rate over reviewed turns, turn-duration quantiles and a day-by-day series (see [`seat_activity`](#queries)) |
| `GET` | `/schedules` | Configured role/unit schedules + next-run + the company's recent fires and what became of each |
| `GET` | `/fleet` | Every live node, its roles and labels, seat ownership, singleton duties, the fleet's activation, each node's config record (revision last attempted, how that went, revision it runs), and where the company's files are kept with what the object store's collector last found. **Always needs a credential carrying `admin`** (session or bearer): it describes the deployment, not the company, and the dashboard locks its screen (see [below](#get-fleet)) |
| `GET` | `/executors` | Every seat's [executor](../concepts/code-sandbox.md) the engine still holds a record of, from the executors' durable record in the [coordination store](../concepts/coordination.md) (see [below](#get-executors)) |
| `GET` | `/budgets` | Token caps, the durable shared counter they are enforced against (per calendar window), and which scopes are being refused (see [below](#get-budgets)) |
| `POST` | `/backup` | Copy this node's store and stream estate into `?dir=` **on the engine's host**. **Takes `admin`**: it writes every credential the company holds to a path the caller names (see [below](#post-backup)) |
| `GET` | `/fleet/broker` | The fleet broker's membership: every live node's broker kind as its presence advertises it, the JetStream metadata group as a member reports it, and every disagreement (a member gone for good first). **Takes `admin`** (see [The broker's membership](#the-brokers-membership)) |
| `POST` | `/fleet/broker/remove/{node}` | Remove a member from the metadata group through a live member's system account. `?confirm=` repeats the node id; refused while the node holds a live presence lease as a member unless `?force=true`. **Takes `admin`** and a [recent proof](#some-gestures-ask-how-recently-you-proved-who-you-are) |
| `POST` | `/fleet/broker/remove-peer/{peer}` | The same removal by the raft peer id `GET /fleet/broker` shows, for a voter whose name no member has heard. `?confirm=` repeats the peer id. **Takes `admin`** and a recent proof |
| `GET` | `/feeds/dead-letters` | Every wake feed's dead letters (records no node could read in the hour each was handed back), by feed, each entry by the id a discard names and what its feed kept of the record, never its frame; a feed that could not be listed is named with its error. **Takes `admin`** (see [The wake feeds' dead letters](#the-wake-feeds-dead-letters)) |
| `POST` | `/feeds/dead-letters/{id}/discard` | Give one entry's wake up for good, whichever feed's subject holds it. `?confirm=` repeats the id; an id no wake feed holds is `404 no_dead_letter`. **Takes `admin`** and a [recent proof](#some-gestures-ask-how-recently-you-proved-who-you-are) |
| `GET` | `/integrations` | Every inbound surface, how it is wired, whether a signing secret is present, and what has arrived through it (see [below](#get-integrations)) |
| `GET` | `/link-hosts` | Where the company's own apps live in a browser: one `{kind, url}` per configured GitHub, GitLab, Mattermost, Jira and Confluence, and on a code host its `owners`. **Everybody's**: no repository, project, team, credential or health, and each `url` is reduced to scheme, host, port and path. `owners` are the organizations or top-level groups the company works in (GitHub's `provisioning.org`, GitLab's `provisioning.group`, and the owner part of every repository or project the integration and the seats name), lower case and sorted, never the repositories. The dashboard uses it for an app's mark beside a link, to link a bare `owner/repo#14`, and to read a bare `owner/repo` as a repository only under one of the owners. A Jira or Confluence on a cloud id with no `site_url` has no browser address and adds no row |
| `GET` | `/advisor/access` | The change that grants an agent one access it asked for (`seat=` the agent's handle, `access=` the grant's key), built from the redacted company for that agent alone ([ADR-0118](../../adr/0118-an-agent-asks-for-access-as-one-grant-a-person-previews-and-sends.md)). **Takes `admin`**. Refused in its own words for a key the catalogue does not name, a grant the agent holds, or one it has nothing to add to |
| `GET` | `/delegated-decisions` | What [delegates](../guides/delegated-decisions.md) decided, under which rules ([ADR-0125](../../adr/0125-a-delegate-decides-a-request-only-within-rules-the-engine-enforces.md)): `enabled`; `rules` (`rule`, `kinds`, `delegates`, `escalate_to`, `sample_one_in`, `always_escalate_paths`, `required_checks`, each `{repo, branch, checks}`); `limits` (the three limits every delegate is held to, as rows of the `limits` question's shape: `key`, `group` `delegated`, `unit`, `value`, `default`, `off`, `default_off`, `settable`, `range`; keys `delegated_decisions.deadline_seconds`, `allows_per_hour`, `server_allows_per_hour`, each the document's value or the engine's default); `sample` (`{default, min, max}`, the spot-check rate a rule's `sample_one_in` may set); and for one company day (`day=`, `2026-11-09` or `today`; default the last whole day, which Home's digest reads; a day not begun is `400 bad_params`) its `since`, `until`, `complete` (false for the running day, whose list grows) and `decided` (every request a delegate or the engine settled that day), then `spot_checks` (the week's decisions chosen for a spot-check) and `flagged` (the week's high-confidence denials). Each list holds up to 100 rows, `*_more` saying the log holds more; each row has `request`, `kind`, `rule`, `seat`, `by`, `by_kind` (`agent`, `person` or `engine`), `through`, `asked`, `confidence`, `verdict`, `overruled`, `sampled`, `host`, `item`, `at` and the opened `subject`, `reason`, `findings`, redacted as [every view shows them](../guides/delegated-decisions.md#what-you-still-see) (`subject_unopened` where they do not open on this node). **Takes `admin`, or a person a rule names in `escalate_to`** |
| `GET` | `/delegated-decisions/repositories` | What a [rule's required checks](../guides/delegated-decisions.md#checks-a-rule-requires) can name on the company's GitHub: `connected` (false for a company with no GitHub) and `repos`, every repository an agent's own app covers under an owner the company names, each once, `{repo, default_branch, archived}` with `repo` as `owner/name`. Read through the agents' apps when asked; `unread` says why nothing could be listed (no agent's app installed, or GitHub not answering). **Takes `admin`** |
| `GET` | `/delegated-decisions/branches` | One of those repositories' branches, `repo=owner/name`: `{repo, branches, more, unread?}`, the first 300 in GitHub's order, `more` saying GitHub holds more. A `repo` that is not `owner/name` is `400 bad_params`; one under an owner the company's GitHub does not name, or no agent's app covers, answers no branches and `unread` saying so. **Takes `admin`** |
| `GET` | `/delegated-decisions/checks` | The check names a rule can require of one branch, `repo=owner/name&branch=`: `{repo, branch, checks, unread?}`, each name once from the check runs on the branch's newest commit, leaving out any an agent's own app or no app reported, since neither passes a declared check. An app without Checks (Read-only) answers no checks and `unread` naming the permission; a `branch` that is not a branch name is `400 bad_params`. **Takes `admin`** |
| `GET` | `/growth/changes` | What agents changed on the company's growth accounts ([ADR-0171](../../adr/0171-spend-public-and-admin-acts-are-held-for-an-administrator-never-a-delegate.md)), newest first: every step of a call that was not a read, off the access log. `product=` narrows to one integration kind; `cursor=` and `limit=` (1 to 100, 25 when unset) page it; a `product` that is no kind, or a `cursor` no page answered, is `400 bad_params`. Each row is `{seat, turn, act, held, product, connection, account, target, tool, class, step, answered_by, answerer, operation, before, changes, money, failure, at}`: `act` is the held call's id where `held`, else the call's; `step` is `made` (an operate call made at once), `failed` (with `failure`, a closed word), or a held call's `asked`, `allowed`, `denied`, `lapsed` (the engine's, a day after the ask), `applied` or `void` (allowed, but the target moved and nothing was sent); `answered_by` is `person` (with `answerer`, their human seat) or `engine`; `operation` and `before` are SHA-256 hex of the exact vendor operation and the target's before-state; each change is `{field, label, before, after, money, text}`, a published text (`text: true`) as `before_sha256`, `before_bytes`, `after_sha256` and `after_bytes` alone; `money` is null or `{currency, delta_micros, daily_micros, daily_after_micros, per_change_cap_micros, daily_cap_micros}` as decimal strings. Each page is `{rows, next, complete}`. **Takes `admin`** (`audit.read`) |
| `GET` | `/advisor/review` | What each agent may do and where it runs, as its next turn is told: per agent (`seat`, `name`), its `access`, the integrations with their levels and permissions, the MCP servers with the tools at each level, and the boxes its runs use with their memory and, once a run has read the box, its browser and container runtime. The go-live check's review. **Takes `admin`** |
| `GET` | `/advisor/findings` | The [Advisor](../guides/advisor.md)'s findings as its duty keeps them: `state=open` (the default) every live one, the most costly first, then the most hours a week, then the longest standing; `state=closed` the closed ones, the newest first; both narrowed by `severity=`, `area=` and `class=`, a page of `limit=` (1 to 100, 50 by default) at `cursor=`. Answers `{findings, next_cursor, counts, last_run}`: `counts` the owner's open findings neither snoozed nor applied, by severity (an `engine` finding is the engine's own work and not counted), and `last_run` the latest run, as `GET /advisor/runs/latest` answers it. Each finding is `{id, key, class, source, actor, area, severity, subject, title, why, item, names, path, entries, explanation, state, close_reason, ineffective, snoozed_until, opened_at, last_confirmed_at, closed_at, effect_due_at, confirmed, revision, seen_before, impact, evidence, fix, headline, stats, chart, seats, actions, premise_checked_at}`, every field always sent, `null` where it has no value: `id` the episode and `key` its class and subject across episodes; `state` `open`, `applied`, `resolved`, `retired`, `expired` or `dismissed`; `confirmed` `stale` once its class has not run for three of its intervals; `evidence` `{window, facts, records}`, each fact `{key, label, value, unit}`; `entries` what an `atlas_act` fix acts on, for a caller holding `atlas` and `null` for any other ([what the atlas shows](../guides/advisor.md#what-the-atlas-shows)); `headline` one line carrying the finding's number (its class's from its facts where the finding states none, its title only for a document's own warning), `close_reason` among them `duplicate` (a rule's finding says it with its numbers) and `replaced` (its premise moved while a rule's finding is about the same work), `stats` the numbers behind it (`{key, label, value, unit, was, better}`, `was` the same number over the range before where the finding read it), `chart` a chart as `GET /advisor/snapshot` draws them or `null`, `seats` the seats it is about (`{handle, name, value, unit}`), `actions` `{primary, secondary}`, each action `{kind, label, option, items, to, page, target, setting, url, question}` with `kind` `apply` (re-check and send fix option `option`), `reassign` (move `items` to the seat `to`, a fix's `reassign`), `open` (`page` and `target`, or `setting`), `step`, `ask` or `fix`, every key sent and `null` where its kind does not use it; `premise_checked_at` when the fact it rests on last held, `null` until re-checked. **Takes `admin`** |
| `GET` | `/advisor/findings/{id}` | One finding, with its `history` (`{at, event, by, moved}`, `by` the engine or a person, `{kind, handle, name}`, `name` the name the company gives their seat (the handle where it no longer holds one), `moved` each fact or field that moved, was and now) and its key's earlier `episodes`. `404` for an id the log does not hold. **Takes `admin`** |
| `GET` | `/advisor/runs/latest` | The latest run: `{run_id, trigger, by, started_at, ended_at, status, classes_run, unread, opened, resolved, model, deep_skipped, deep_kept_from}`, `status` `running` for a Run now the duty has not taken yet, `done`, `failed`, `ceiling`, or `interrupted` for a deep run whose server stopped during it (it concluded nothing, `model.reason` says so, and its `budget` is `null`), `unread` the sources it could not read by their words, `model` the model pass's `{status, tokens, listed, dropped, reason}` or `null`; `kind` `rules` or `deep`; `progress` a deep run's steps `{at, text, step, state, detail, why}`, oldest first: `step` `note`, `read` (the snapshot's included), `verdict`, `question` or `checks` (a press's checks), a line from before steps a `note`; `state` `done`, `failed`, or `running` for the newest note, read or checks of a run in flight; `detail` the read's call or the verdict's item and question, `why` a failed step's reason, each `""` where none; a read that failed is one step, its failure folded into the read it ended; read while it runs (a deep run in flight is the latest run, `status` `running`, until a later run ends after its last line or it goes unheard for longer than any investigation lasts), and after it ends its whole trail, every read it asked and the verdict on each agenda item, from its progress record (up to 400 lines; the last three its record keeps once its lines are past their retention), `[]` for a rules run; `budget` a deep run's `{tokens, tokens_ceiling, minutes, minutes_ceiling}` and `stopped_by` the bound it stopped at, both `null` for a rules run; `agenda` a deep run's `{items, answered}`, how many questions it has to answer and has answered, in flight (from its checkpoint) or ended, `null` for a rules run or one that kept none; `classes` what the run concluded about each class, `{class, status, reason}` with `status` `found`, `clear`, `silent` (it read its sources and still could not judge all of the company, `reason` saying what and why) or `unread`. `deep_skipped` is why a run's deep part did not run, `kept` (the investigation from `deep_kept_from` stands) or `no_model`, `null` where it ran or the run has none; `model.repaired` counts the findings its model proposed that were listed after a repair (`fix_not_built`, `reworded`, `worded_by_engine`, `subject_widened`), beside `model.dropped`. **Takes `admin`** |
| `GET` | `/advisor/notices` | The platform notices that reach every administrator's Inbox, `{notices, unread}`: an open finding that blocks the company and is the owner's to fix, an alarm standing on any node past the deferral grace and a conversation the engine holds, each `{class, subject, since, nodes, finding}`, `finding` the finding whose fix ends it (`{id, title, fix}`) or `null`; `unread` what the latest run could not read, `findings` where this node could not read the Advisor's own list. **Takes `admin`** |
| `GET` | `/advisor/reports` | The Advisor's weekly reports, the newest week first, a page of `limit=` (1 to 52, 12 by default) at `cursor=`: `{reports, next_cursor}`, each `{week, period, written_at, opened, resolved, applied, dismissed, headline}`, `week` the ISO week (`2026-W47`), `period` its `{from, to}`, Monday to Monday on the company's clock, and `headline` the week's turns, turns that committed nothing, tokens and hours work waited for a seat, those it measured, each as a report's `metrics` are. A week the company did not exist through all of has no report. **Takes `admin`** |
| `GET` | `/advisor/reports/{week}` | One week's report, written on the Monday after it and kept as written: the summary's fields with `metrics` (each `{key, label, value, unit, was}`, `was` the week before's value or `null`), `unread` (the sources whose numbers are left out), `top` (the open findings that cost the most when it was written, of those the week opened and notes left out, `{id, class, severity, title, subject, item}`) `summary` (`null` where none was written) and `days` (the week day by day, Monday first, each `{day, turns, turns_nothing, tokens}` counted as the week's totals are; `[]` for a report written before its days were kept, or whose turn ledger could not be read day by day). `404` for a week with no report. **Takes `admin`** |
| `GET` | `/advisor/snapshot` | The company's numbers over `range=` `7d` (the default), `14d` or `30d`, company days ending now, today included: `{as_of, run_id, range, stats, charts, unread}`. `stats` `{key, label, value, unit, was, better}`, `was` the range before's value or `null`, `better` `up`, `down` or `null`; `charts` `{id, title, unit, kind, x, series, note}`, `kind` `columns`, `stacked_columns` or `bars`, `x` `{kind, keys, labels}` (`day`, `seat`, `entry`, `reason` or `state`), each series `{id, label, values}` aligned with `x`; `unread` the sources that could not be read, whose numbers are left out. Charts today: `flow_by_seat`, `open_work`, `capacity_lost`, `wasted_wakes`, `tokens_per_turn`. **Takes `admin`** |
| `GET` | `/advisor/capacity` | The hours each model entry was out on its usage limit over `range=` `7d` (the default), `14d` or `30d`: `{range, days, entries}`, `days` the company days (`YYYY-MM-DD`), each entry `{entry, out_hours, total_hours, hits, hits_by_day, seats}`, `out_hours` and `hits_by_day` aligned with `days`, `hits` how many separate stretches it was out, `seats` `{handle, name, hours}` the seats it held, the most first. Read from the seats' park and release records, each stretch's first park naming the entry. **Takes `admin`** |
| `POST` | `/advisor/runs` | Run the Advisor now, with no body (or `{}`); a body naming anything else is `400`. The run is one: every check at once, its findings recorded as they are found, then the deep investigation on the Advisor's model under the same run, unless one concluded within the last six hours or no model is assigned, which the run records (`deep_skipped` on `GET /advisor/runs/latest`). `202 {run_id}`, the duty's holder taking it within a minute; `409 conflict` with the run asked for while one waits. **Takes `advisor.run`**, an administrator's at any recency and Ask Crewlet's only on the person's approval: it spends tokens and changes no config |
| `POST` | `/advisor/findings/{id}/decision` | A person's decision on a finding, `{"decision": "snooze", "reopen", "useful" or "dismiss", "reason"}`: a snooze holds it off the list for 7 days; a dismissal names its `reason`, `wont_fix` (the key held quiet 90 days), `known` (30) or `wrong` (for good, and the model pass is told); `reopen` lifts a snooze, or a dismissal's hold and asks for a run now, so a condition that still stands opens again as a new finding within a minute (the dismissed one stays as it was). Answers the finding as it now reads; `409 conflict` where it moved since it was read. **Takes `advisor.run`**. A fix is never applied here: its change is sent through its own route by the person |
| `POST` | `/advisor/findings/{id}/recheck` | Re-check an open finding before its fix is sent, `{"option": n}` (the fix's option, 0 by default), or before the work it moves is moved, `{"action": "reassign"}`: its class runs again now and answers `{outcome, finding, moved, previous_fix, preview, send, sends, moves, digest, checked_at, expires_at, refusal}`. `outcome` is `holds` (the same verdict and change), `changed` (the condition stands with another change, recorded as a new revision: `moved` says what moved and `previous_fix` the fix it replaced), `resolved` (the condition ended: the finding closes and nothing is sent) or `not_applicable` (its subject left or its change no longer builds: it is retired). On `holds` and `changed` a configuration fix carries `send`, the one request to send from the person's session (`PUT /config/{entity}/{id}` with the entity as it would become and `If-Match` the entity's tag as the re-check read it, its `dry_run_path` first), a `preview` of each field it writes, before and after, and `digest`; an option that changes several seats (its `change` and its `also`) carries every request in `sends`, in the order to send them, `send` the first, and its preview rows name each change; a reassignment answers `moves` instead (`send` null), each `{item, from, to, version, reason}`: an item the seat the finding is about still holds and nobody has started, read now, written by the person's session through `update_work_item` (`assignee` the seat, which they may change, `if_match` its `version`, and `reason`), its preview a row per item, and `applied` with its `digest` marks the finding applied once that seat holds none of them; send it before `expires_at` (10 minutes), else re-check again. `refusal` says who can make a change this server may not send (a configuration managed elsewhere); the finding stays open. `409 {outcome, state, detail}` for a finding no longer open, in words: `applied` (another window applied it, with `applied_at` and `effect_due_at`, until when its effect is checked) or `closed` (with `closed_at`). `503` when what the finding is read from could not be read just now, or was read only in part without it (an integration's findings record that may have dropped it, [Integration reconcile](../concepts/integration-reconcile.md#what-a-surfaces-records-keep)). **Takes `advisor.run`** |
| `POST` | `/advisor/findings/{id}/applied` | Report that a re-checked change was sent, `{"digest"}`: the finding is marked `applied`, its effect checked by its class's runs until `effect_due_at` (an hour for the setup's classes, a week for a pattern of the week's), once the configuration holds the change. `409 {"outcome": "recheck"}` where the finding moved since the re-check or the configuration does not hold the change, and the re-check's `409` for a finding no longer open (`applied` or `closed`). **Takes `advisor.run`** |
| `GET` | `/diagnostics/issue-reports` | The company's [engine issue reports](../guides/engine-issue-reports.md): whether they are on, the relay, every report sent with its status, the bytes it sent and the issue the relay named, and what a report of each class would say. **Takes `admin`**. The setting itself is `diagnostics.issue_reports.enabled`, written under `/config` |
| `GET` | `/diagnostics/insights` | The company's [operating insights](../guides/operating-insights.md): the consent (`share`, `accepted`, and `always`, the classes sent without review), this build's catalogue schema and catalogue, the relay, and every record the fleet keeps with its status (`observed`, `queued`, `scheduled`, `sending`, `sent`, `failed` or `declined`), when it is due, the relay's last status code (`answer`) and the record itself. A send that never settled reads as `failed` after an hour. **Takes `admin`**. The setting itself is `diagnostics.insights`, written under `/config` |
| `POST` | `/diagnostics/insights/decisions` | An administrator's answer to a queued insight record, `{"class", "week", "choice": "send" or "decline"}`: send schedules it at its own random time within a day. **Takes `admin` and a step-up**. Refused `409` when the record is not waiting for a decision (sharing is not in review mode, or it was decided) |
| `GET` | `/backups` | What the fleet has backed up: each node's newest point and the operator's newest acknowledgement of each log, as each log's trim reads them, and every backup a person asked a node for, failures included. **Takes `admin`** (see [below](#get-backups)) |
| `GET` | `/mcp-catalogue` | What an MCP server is added from: the curated catalogue whole, and with `q=` the company's community registry (`mcp_registry.url`) searched, each listing marked as not reviewed. **Takes `tools.read`**, everybody's: a member reads the curated half alone (see [below](#get-mcp-catalogue)) |
| `GET` | `/mcp-servers` | What each configured MCP server is doing on each live node (serving, failed, tools served, first failure), from every node's status record, beside what the configuration declares (never a credential), and the engine's built-in tools by group, each naming who may call it. **Everybody's**, in two readings: a member's names no launch line, failure sentence or wait (see [below](#get-mcp-servers)) |
| `GET` | `/mcp-servers/{name}` | One MCP server whole: its `/mcp-servers` row, every tool the fleet's live nodes list for it (per-agent servers included) with hints, risk and arguments, what the server said of itself in its handshake, and what removing it would take with it. **Takes `tools.read`**, everybody's, in two readings (see [below](#get-mcp-serversname)) |
| `POST` | `/mcp-servers/{name}/retry` | Restart one MCP server now: every instance on every node, or with `seat` one agent's instance on the node holding the seat. **Takes `tools.retry`**, an administrator's at any recency (see [below](#post-mcp-serversnameretry)) |
| `POST` | `/mcp-servers/{name}/check` | Test one MCP server where it runs, calling no tool: on every node, or with `seat` one agent's instance on the node holding the seat; recorded as the server's latest test. **Takes `tools.check`**, an administrator's at any recency (see [below](#post-mcp-serversnamecheck)) |
| `POST` | `/mcp-checks` | Test a draft MCP server entry before it is saved, as a write would leave it. **Takes `tools.check`**, and `config.write` and `secrets.write` on top, decided before the body is read (see [below](#post-mcp-checks)) |
| `POST` | `/mcp-probe` | Check an address before an MCP server is added at it: what answers there, and the sign-in it asks for, from its OAuth metadata. **Takes `tools.check`**, and `config.write` on top (see [below](#post-mcp-probe)) |
| `PUT` | `/mcp-servers/{name}/values/{key}` | Store one header or variable of an MCP server, tested first by default, sealed write-only and read through a `${VAR}` the key is pointed at. **Takes `secrets.write`**, and `config.write` on top, both at a recent step-up and decided before the body is read; never the assistant (see [below](#put-mcp-serversnamevalueskey)) |
| `PUT` | `/mcp-servers/{name}/tools` | Set the level each tool of an MCP server runs at (`allow` or `blocked`), as one revision of the company document; `?dry_run=true` checks it. **Takes `config.write`**, at a recent step-up for a write (see [below](#put-mcp-serversnametools)) |
| `POST` | `/mcp-servers/{name}/oauth` | Start signing the company in to a remote MCP server with OAuth: answers the address the person's browser is sent to, once. **Takes `secrets.write`**: an administrator, a [recent proof](#some-gestures-ask-how-recently-you-proved-who-you-are), never Ask Crewlet (see [below](#post-mcp-serversnameoauth)) |
| `GET` | `/mcp-sign-ins/{id}` | Where a sign-in is: `pending`, `completing`, `approved` or `failed`, and why. **Takes `config.read`** (see [below](#get-mcp-sign-insid)) |
| `DELETE` | `/mcp-servers/{name}/oauth` | Sign the company out of an MCP server: the grant is revoked at its vendor where it offers that, forgotten here, and the server stopped on every node. **Takes `secrets.write`**, as the start does (see [below](#delete-mcp-serversnameoauth)) |
| `POST` | `/mcp-servers/{name}/changes` | Accept, or keep blocked, tools an MCP server changed since their levels were decided, each by the digest of the definition reviewed. **Takes `config.write`**, at a recent step-up (see [below](#post-mcp-serversnamechanges)) |
| `GET` | `/worklet` | Worklet: a filtered listing of work items, plus the last key number minted per project. Served only where `tracker.backend` is `worklet`; a company on Jira gets `404 unknown_query`, not an empty board (see [below](#worklet-and-doclet)) |
| `GET` | `/worklet/retention` | What the state log is holding, what the trim concluded and which term is stopping it, every data node's position, and what this node costs to replace. **Takes `admin`, reads included** (see [below](#get-workletretention-what-the-log-is-holding)) |
| `POST` | `/worklet/retention/ack` | Publish an operator backup floor, for `backup_floor: operator` |
| `POST` | `/worklet/retention/evict/{node}` | Install the eviction gate on a node on every log the trim counts nodes on (every log that claims identity: all but the vector changelog and the usage log), so the trim can pass a floor it is pinning. Refused `409` while the node holds a live presence lease; answers per log (see [below](#the-three-retention-gestures-that-write)) |
| `POST` | `/worklet/retention/readmit/{node}` | Lift it on every one of those logs: the inverse commit, not a delete. Refused `409` while the node still lacks records a trim floor lets the log delete |
| `POST` | `/worklet/retention/capacity` | Drive a log's byte-ceiling change as far as this node's mode allows |
| `GET` | `/worklet/retention/maintenance` | Where that window stands and what is holding it |
| `POST` | `/worklet/retention/maintenance/abandon` | Change what the operation is trying to reach, never the barrier it must cross |
| `POST` | `/worklet/retention/maintenance/exclude` | Record that a participant's process is stopped and holds no outstanding request |
| `POST` | `/worklet/retention/maintenance/retire` | Record that no process will run under a node id again, so no capacity window counts it while the retirement stands; `?confirm=` repeats `?node=` |
| `GET` | `/worklet/retention/reanchor` | The live stream's own `created_at`, which a reanchor's confirmation has to echo, and the case a reanchor would answer |
| `POST` | `/worklet/retention/reanchor` | Adopt a recreated stream, or a broker restored from an older copy, at the next generation |
| `GET` | `/worklet/views` | One container's **view strip**: the six every container has, and whatever was saved beyond them. `?container=` takes the query grammar's spelling (`workspace`, `project:ENG`, `unit:engineering`, `person:ana`): a project key is upper-cased and a unit resolves by any key it answers to or by its name, so a team's strip is one strip under every spelling. Ordered by **the caller's own** personal views and pins; no parameter names whose. The caller's own is their [own record](#whose-record-a-personal-question-answers-for): the seat a person holds, or the login of a Tier A token or service account bound to none |
| `GET` | `/worklet/views/saved` | **Every saved view** the caller can see, in EVERY container: shared ones and their own personal ones, pinned first, each row carrying its `container`. What the dashboard's view inventory and sidebar pinned group read, since a view saved on a project board is in no workspace strip. No parameter names whose, as `/worklet/views`. `?counts=true` counts each pinned view in its own container, and is `400 bad_params` for a credential that names no record of its own, since only a record has pins |
| `GET` | `/worklet/catalogue` | The company's **vocabulary**: the task types a create may name and the workspace's custom-field declarations. `?archived=true` also lists what was retired. The types are the EFFECTIVE set: the six this build ships plus whatever the company declared, a declaration replacing a builtin of the same slug |
| `GET` | `/worklet/projects` | Every **project** work is filed into, with its `task_counts` (`{todo, active, done, closed}`, one per status group; there is no `open`, so add `todo` and `active` for every unfinished item), its `target_date` (`YYYY-MM-DD` on the company's clock; omitted when none), its `last_change` (when the project's work last changed and who changed it; ABSENT for a project nothing has been filed into), its chart-owned unit and its lead. `?q=` narrows by a word in the key, name or purpose; `?unit=` to the projects one unit owns, **named by the unit's key or by its name where exactly one unit carries it, in any case**. `?archived=` SELECTS a set: `false` (default) live projects, `only` retired alone, `true` both. `?sort=` orders the whole selected set before the page is taken: one of `key`, `name`, `unit`, `todo`, `active`, `done`, `closed`, `last_change`, `target`, each optionally with a leading `-` for descending, default `key`, the key breaking every tie; a project with no `last_change` or no `target_date` sorts last in both directions. An `archived` or `sort` value that is neither is a **400** naming the parameter and what it accepts. `?limit=` caps at 200, also the default. The answer carries a `census` (`{active, archived}`, the same question under the same `q` and `unit` MINUS its archival term), so a caller that selected one set can tell an empty set from an empty company; `total` is the census of the mode asked for. A set read, so it carries `complete` and its `incomplete` beside the read level |
| `GET` | `/worklet/projects/{key}` | One project in **full**: the six statuses with labels, groups and descriptions; the effective types; the custom fields grouped by the type they apply to, required first, with the workspace ids this project **shadows** named; its tags; its default assignee, lead and owning unit. `?for_type=` narrows the fields to one type plus those that apply to every type. Unknown key answers 404 naming the nearest three; a `for_type` the company does not file answers 400 `bad_params`, not 404 |
| `GET` | `/worklet/files` | One project's **files**, in path order: `?project=` (required), `?folder=` to narrow to the paths under one folder, `?removed=true` to include removed files, `?limit=` (default 200, capped at 1000: a larger one is answered a page of 1000) and `?after=`, the `next` the previous page answered. An unknown project is `404 no_project`, never an empty page (see [below](#project-files)) |
| `GET` | `/worklet/files/{project}/{path...}` | One file's **bytes**, streamed, with its version as the `ETag`. `503 content_unavailable` where the file is listed and its content could not be read right now (see [below](#project-files)) |
| `PUT` | `/worklet/files/{project}/{path...}` | Write a file: the request body is its content, `Content-Type` its type, `If-Match` the version it replaces and an `Idempotency-Key` how an `unknown` answer is retried. **Takes `worklet`**; the write is attributed to whoever the request resolved to (see [below](#project-files)) |
| `DELETE` | `/worklet/files/{project}/{path...}` | Remove a file. `If-Match` and `Idempotency-Key` as the write. **Its project's lead, or `admin`**, either with `worklet`, as removing a work item is |
| `GET` | `/worklet/activity` | The **activity feed**: one durable row per applied commit, quiet ones included, at any age with no live/archive boundary. Ordered by the COMPOSED LOG POSITION, not any clock: `?since=` and `?cursor=` are positions written `<stream>@<generation>:<sequence>`, so a cursor spans a reanchor with no gap and no repeat. Filters: `?task=` (key, id or a FORMER key), `?container=`, `?kinds=`, `?actor=`, `?assignee=`, `?notified=`, `?from=`/`?to=` (RFC3339, bounding the AUTHORED instants), `?limit=` ≤200. `?q=` is an escaped `LIKE` over the excerpt, REFUSED unless it names a task, or a project **and** a `since` inside 90 days. Each record carries `fields`, what MOVED, as `{"<field>": {"from": …, "to": …}}`, and for a SET (`tags`, `watchers`, `muted`, `collaborators`, each link kind, `blocking`, a catalogue's or tag set's declarations, a person's favorites) the members that joined and left, as `{"<field>": {"from": "", "to": "", "added": […], "removed": […]}}`, each sorted and every member whole. That holds for every kind, not only task kinds: a project reconcile names the name, purpose, unit or epoch that changed, a view save the query parameters, a priorities write the order before and after, a dependency the item it now waits on. A task's own row draws on twenty-nine names: `title`, `status`, `assignee`, `priority`, `project`, `type`, `tags`, `due`, `due_all_day`, `start`, `wait_reason`, `estimate`, `points`, `reporter`, `watchers`, `muted`, `collaborators`, `parent`, `routing_unit`, `archived`, `removed_with`, `waiting_on`, `linked`, `duplicates`, `page`, `blocking`, `checklists`, `fields` and `body`. Values are the STORED form (a status slug, a whole RFC3339 instant, an item's id), not a rendering. Nothing is cut: an ordered list (`priorities`, `pinned_views`, `checklists`) is carried whole, free text past 600 bytes (a project's `purpose`, say) is described as `<N> bytes`, and every field a change moved is on the row; only a notification card stops at 32, saying how many it left off (`fields_omitted`). The two largest are MARKED: `body` is `<N> bytes` on each side (empty where there was none), never the prose, and `checklists` is `<list>: <done> of <total> done` per named list. `fields` names each custom value by its SLUG (resolved by the node applying the change, so a NOTIFICATION carries every other delta and not this one), a choice as its option's slug, a multi-valued field's members joined with `/`, a value past 150 bytes as `<N> bytes`, and a count of any whose field the project no longer declares. The ANSWER also carries `keys`, an id-to-item-key map for the tasks those deltas point at (`waiting_on`, `linked` and `duplicates` but never `page`, which names a knowledge-base page; the `blocking` mirror; a person's `priorities` queue; and the scalars `parent` and `removed_with`), resolved on the answering node; a delta records another task by its ID. An id this node holds no row for is absent, not empty, and a renderer falls back to the id |
| `GET` | `/worklet/my-work` | Everything one person is expected to look at, in eight bounded lists: `priorities` in the stored order, `assigned`, `asked_of_me` (each with the literal call that answers it, whether it is `open`, and the `decision` it carries when it asks somebody to choose; see [Asking for a decision](../guides/worklet.md#asking-for-a-decision)), `checklist_items` (which live on other people's tasks and no assignee filter reaches), `collaborating`, `watching_recent`, `unblocked_recent` and `holding_up` (the open work they hold that other open work waits on, assigned to them or held by an open question to them, most waited on first, each row with `blocks`, `holders`, `held_since`, `agent_waiting` and, for an item held by a question, `asked`; beside it `holding_agents`, the held items agent items wait on and the distinct agent items waiting; see [Worklet](../guides/worklet.md)). `?handle=` is whose, **defaulting to the caller's own record** (see [Whose record a personal question answers for](#whose-record-a-personal-question-answers-for)). Naming somebody else's takes whoever leads them, or `admin`, and `worklet` either way |
| `GET` | `/worklet/inbox` | One person's **inbox**: the notices a change wrote to them, each naming the ONE [reason](../guides/worklet.md) of nineteen it found them under, whether it **asks** something or merely informs, whether it arrived only because nobody better was found, and their own read and snooze marks, plus the comment and turn the change came from, and the `ask` it is about, as it stands now. Same scope rule as `/worklet/my-work`. `?unread=`, `?primary_only=`, `?snoozed=` (`exclude`, the default, since a snooze means *not now*; `include` or `only`; anything else refused naming the three), `?reasons=` (comma-separated, refused naming the nineteen); each narrows the SCAN, so a page is full whenever the scope holds 50 notices and `next_cursor` is never a cursor past an empty page. Also `?limit=` ≤50, `?cursor=`, and `?since=`, a LOG POSITION written `<stream>@<generation>:<sequence>` (what `seen_through` reports back), never a bare sequence: the comparison is on the packed `(generation << 40) | seq`, so a sequence with no generation re-delivers everything after a reanchor |
| `GET` | `/worklet/people/{handle}` | One human's **own state**: their inbox (unread, read, snoozed, and which snoozes are now **due**), the order they mean to work in and who set it, and their pinned views. Same scope rule as `/worklet/my-work`, the handle always named here as it is the path: your own seat's is yours, anybody else's takes the owner-or-lead rule. A person nobody has written yet answers the EMPTY state with `held: false`, not a 404: the first write creates the record |
| `GET` | `/worklet/{id}` | One item with its description, thread, history and links. `{id}` is the key (`ENG-42`) or the id: a person holds the first and every internal link the second |
| `GET` | `/worklet/comments` | One page of an item's thread, walking back from the newest: `?item=` (key or id), `?cursor=`, `?limit=` (default 20, at most 50), `?thread=` (one comment's conversation) and `?with_root=`; see [`work_comments`](#queries) |
| `GET` | `/worklet/turns` | One page of the agent turns charged to an item, newest first: `?id=` (key or id), `?cursor=`, `?limit=` (default 20, at most 50); see [`work_item_turns`](#queries) |
| `GET` | `/doclet/pages` | Doclet: a filtered listing of its pages. Served only where `knowledge.backend` is `doclet` |
| `GET` | `/doclet/pages/{id}` | One page with its body, comments, revision metadata, children and ancestor breadcrumb. `{id}` is the id, or `CONTAINER/Title`: the title matches as the fleet CLAIMED it, ignoring case and runs of whitespace, so `ENG/deploy runbook` reaches "Deploy  Runbook" |
| `GET` | `/doclet/pages/{id}/revisions/{version}` | One revision of a page: its own body, message and author at that version, the newest included. Decided as reading the page; see [`page_revision`](#queries) |
| `GET` | `/containers` | Every knowledge container this node knows about, with how many pages each holds. The engine materialises one per `space:` the org chart names, plus the two reserved ones, on every config apply and boot; each carries `chart_epoch`, the activation its name and purpose were last written from (Unix milliseconds), so an earlier-activated configuration never overwrites them. Beside the list, `skills` is the key of the container tool skills are written in (`knowledge.skills_container`), absent on a company that turned tool skills off |
| `GET` | `/chatlet/channels` | The company's own **chat**: the caller's rooms, newest activity first, each with its unread count against the caller's own read cursor and whether they muted it, plus their whole read state: every room (at most 256), or with `?limit=` the most recently active that many, and with `?unread=true` only those with something unread. Served only where `chat.backend` is `chatlet`, to a principal holding `chatlet` **and acting as a seat** (see [Chatlet](#chatlet)) |
| `GET` | `/chatlet/channels/{channel_id}` | One room's metadata and membership. On this route and the two below, `{channel_id}` is the room's id or its name (`launch`, or `%23launch` for `#launch`), so a room the caller is not in is reached by its name. A room the caller may not read answers `404`, by name as by id, exactly as one that does not exist |
| `GET` | `/chatlet/channels/{channel_id}/messages` | One page of a room's transcript, newest first: `?cursor=` (the last answer's `next_cursor`), `?limit=` (default 50, at most 500) |
| `GET` | `/chatlet/channels/{channel_id}/threads/{root_id}` | One thread from its root, oldest first, with who has spoken in it; paged as the transcript, the other way |
| `GET` | `/chatlet/activity` | What waits for the caller across the rooms they may read, newest first: mentions of them (and of a whole room they are in), replies in the threads they follow, and reactions to their messages.
