`GET /health` always returns **200** once the node serves, including when `status` is `unconfigured` or a diverged posture: the code is liveness, and an engine waiting for configuration is alive. Before then it answers `503` only while the node recovers what it holds ([While a node is starting](#while-a-node-is-starting)). Steer traffic with [`GET /ready`](#routes), which answers `503` and names the reason.

### Probes on a node without ingress

A node whose `node.roles` leave out `ingress` (a [satellite](../guides/satellite-nodes.md), or the seats and workers half of a split deployment) serves no API, dashboard or webhook, but an orchestrator must still probe it to restart a wedged node or wait on a rollout. So it binds `api.port` for exactly two routes the network can reach, and binds no [public listener](#which-listener-serves-what). An executor in a box that does not share its node's loopback reaches its tools through an ingress node's [tool bridge](#routes), which relays each call here. The guard stands in front as on an ingress node: `401` to a request presenting no credential (everything outside the guard's exemptions is guarded, `/agents` say), and `404 no_route` for an exempt path this node does not serve (`/dashboard`) and for anything once a credential is presented. The node logs `api_probes_listening`, with the address its own boxes dial in `box_host_url`. `api.port: 0` binds nothing, here as anywhere.

**A node that runs seats serves its own boxes beside the probes.** A `direct` box is a process of the node's host and dials the node that launched it on loopback: the [tool bridge](#routes) under `/mcp/{token}` (its MCP servers, notes route and skill route included) and, where the node forwards to `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, the telemetry receiver under `/otlp/{token}/v1/{signal}`. Both are the routes an ingress node serves, but only to a caller on this host's loopback, read from the connection's own address. A token the fleet did not sign answers `401`; a call for a seat this node has since handed on is relayed to its holder. A caller off the host meets `404 no_route` under both prefixes, whatever its method. While the node starts, a loopback caller of either gets `503 starting` with a `Retry-After`, as every starting node answers a route it will serve. The node hands its boxes this address only where loopback reaches the listener (an `api.host` of every interface or a loopback address); one bound to a single other address leaves its `direct` boxes to `CREWLET_MCP_BRIDGE_URL`.

`GET /health` is liveness: `200` while the process is alive, through a drain and a down broker link, once the node serves (before then, see [While a node is starting](#while-a-node-is-starting)). Its body is the node's half of [the health envelope](#the-health-envelope) under the same field names, plus the node's `roles`, and leaves out what describes a dashboard this node does not serve (`clients`, `event_history_seconds`, `spend_history_seconds`, `seeded_from`):

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "node": "sat-eu-1",
  "roles": ["seats"],
  "configured": true,
  "version": "v0.4.0",
  "started_at": "2026-04-01T11:58:03Z",
  "queue": "jetstream-embedded",
  "in_flight": 1,
  "shutting_down": false,
  "posture": "serve",
  "applied_epoch": 41,
  "identity_duty_seconds": {},
  "seats": ["eu-support"],
  "nodes": 4
}
```

`GET /ready` answers whether the node is **doing its work**; it takes no traffic for the probe to steer, and what waits on it is a rollout that must not replace the next node until this one has joined. `200` once every condition below holds; otherwise `503`, with the first that fails in `reason`, in this order:

| `reason` | The node is not ready because |
|---|---|
| `starting` | It has not started yet; its probes are still the boot's ([While a node is starting](#while-a-node-is-starting)). |
| `draining` | It is stopping. |
| `broker_unlinked` | It cannot reach the fleet's broker: a leaf whose link to every member is down, a connection to an external cluster that is reconnecting, or the fleet's JetStream not answering across its data path or its lease link. `detail` names which, and the cause. Ahead of what follows, since each of those is what a lost broker looks like. |
| `unconfigured` | Its engine runs no company revision. |
| `shed`, `stuck` | Its [config posture](../concepts/control-plane.md#operator-surface) is diverged. `wait` and `isolated` stay ready, as on an ingress node. |
| `no_presence` | It does not hold its presence lease (its last renew is older than the TTL), so no peer counts it and nothing routes to it. |
| `admission_withheld` | It runs seats and its latest placement pass was not admitted to claim: no data node has yet answered that a copy of the estate admits a seat (a stateless node), its own copy is behind (a data node), or it cannot serve the seats it holds. Not judged on a node running no seats or started in a [maintenance mode](../guides/retention.md#the-three-modes). |

```json
{
  "ready": false,
  "node": "sat-eu-1",
  "configured": true,
  "draining": false,
  "posture": "serve",
  "reason": "broker_unlinked",
  "detail": "the data path: jetstream: this leaf has no link to any member of the fleet, so every stream and bucket it uses is out of reach"
}
```

An ingress node's `/ready` answers whether traffic should come to it, on `draining`, `unconfigured`, `shed`, `stuck` and `estate_behind` alone. Both share one judgement (`judgeReadiness`, `internal/api/health.go`) and one precedence, so a shared reason means the same on both.

### What a line names

A line the engine writes (an event's `summary`, a trigger's `summary` on a phase record and a live call, a wake's subject) says what it names that a person can open, beside the words: `refs`, each `{kind, id, text}`. `kind` is one of `work_item` (a Worklet task by its id or key), `code_change` (`<repository>!<number>`), `commit` (`<repository>@<object id>`), `repository`, `page` (a Doclet page by its id), `artifact`, `turn`, `schedule` (`<scope type>/<scope id>/<name>`), `a2a_channel`, `seat` (a handle) or `chat_room`; a kind a newer engine adds arrives as itself. `text` is the words the line spells it with, a run of the line: a reader finds each ref's words left to right, each search starting where the last match ended, and a ref whose words a cut summary lost is not drawn. The words are unchanged, so a reader ignoring `refs` reads the same line. Whether the reader may open what a ref names, and what it is called now, is the `references` question's.

### Paging the event history

`GET /events` and the `events` query return rows ordered by `(timestamp, id)` **descending** and accept an exclusive keyset cursor:

```
GET /events?limit=100&before_time=2026-04-01T12:00:00Z&before_id=<event_id>
```

Pass the oldest row you hold to get the page beneath it. The id half is not optional: burst writes share a timestamp at microsecond resolution, and a cursor over a non-unique key skips or repeats what collided.

**The end of the history is `exhausted: true`, `next: null`**, and only that. A page SHORTER than `limit` is not the end: the page is merged from every node's store ([Reading the fleet's history](#reading-the-fleets-history-coverage)) and stops at the newest point any node's page stopped at, so a node whose reply was cut to fit the transport shortens the page without ending it. The `agent` filter adds another reason: it also pulls in every event sharing a trace with a direct match, from every data node, so a caller must dedupe by id.

`agent` is the **related** filter: every event involving one agent seat, named by any **handle** it answers to: the events that are its own and every one naming it as a party (an A2A channel it asked or was asked on, a message it sent or was sent there, a vendor delivery addressed to it), plus the trigger that caused its work, by trace. Both sides are keyed on the seat's **agent id**, never a name: the handle is resolved through the org chart the answering node holds, as each event's participants were when it was written, so a namesake is never listed as the seat, and a handle the seat has given up still finds it rather than whoever took it next. A handle no agent seat answers to (a human seat's, or nobody's) is refused `bad_params`, since no id could match and an empty page would read as an agent that did nothing; a person's events are the ones they acted in, under `actor`. The index was keyed on names before node migration `0038`, so a counterpart or delivery recipient named before it is not in the related view for the rest of the retention window.

The persistent store retains 30 days, and [`event_history_seconds`](#the-health-envelope) is that floor on the wire: read it rather than restating the number, which is the store's own constant. Once a cursor crosses it every page is empty, so a client must distinguish that from quiet rather than draw the gap as silence.

`seat` narrows the log to the events ONE agent seat published, named by its handle and resolved on the server to the derived agent id every seat-level event carries and every row names as its own `agent_id` (the live `event` push and a stored row alike, so a client merging the two filters both by the same id). It is what a seat's "all activity" asks by, never `actor` (who acted, as prose: a seat's name there matches every seat carrying it).

`category` filters server-side because filtering a paged list client-side silently excludes (a 100-row page holding 2 matches reads as "only 2 exist"). Its vocabulary is a closed set of eight values; which event type lands under which is in [Deployment § What gets stored](../guides/deployment.md#what-gets-stored-and-under-which-category).
### Reading the fleet's history: `coverage`

A data node's event store holds what that node published, plus the events of a node without `data`, kept in
[custody](../guides/deployment.md#custody-the-rows-of-a-node-without-data). So the history questions (`events`, `event`, `event_series`,
`trace`, `turn`, `turns`, `phases`, a seat's `llm_history` on `agent`, the
delivery and outcome counts on `integrations`, the live projection's boot
seed) are answered by **every live data node at query time**: the
node you asked reads its own store, scatters the question to its
peers, merges the answers and says which nodes it heard from. Each answer carries:

```json
"coverage": {
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "node-a", "answered": true,  "error": ""},
    {"id": "node-b", "answered": false, "error": "no answer within the 2s fleet read budget"}
  ],
  "complete": false
}
```

- `nodes` is every node asked or heard from, sorted by id. The node you
  asked is always one and always answered (serving the API takes the `data` role); a failure of its own store is an error, not a gap.
- `complete` is true only when the node roster could be read **and** every
  node on it answered. A node that did not is named with why: no answer
  inside the two-second fleet read budget, a build speaking another scatter protocol version, an unreadable reply, or its own read
  failing.
- **Every node answers in its own protocol version only** and refuses a
  question in any other: a node on another build is named with that
  reason on every answer, and nothing it holds is merged. No node
  is asked to answer around a filter it would drop, a count it would never
  send or the instant it would ignore, so every merged part was read
  exactly as asked: the axis's window is cut alike on every node, a window
  the history clips goes down to the bucket the horizon falls in, and the serving
  node drops that partial first bar after the sum (see [the time
  axis](#the-event-logs-time-axis)).
- It sits at the top of each answer, beside the record's own fields on
  `event` and `event_series`, and is `null` on `agent` and `integrations`
  when the history could not be read at all.
- **A node that has left the fleet is not asked** (not live): its turn-level detail left with it. Its spend and turn counts are answered by the replicated `usage` domain.
- **A stateless node's row is listed and counted once**, though for a moment
  two data nodes can hold it: a
  [custody](../guides/deployment.md#custody-the-rows-of-a-node-without-data)
  batch the second keeper wrote before the first settled it. A listing
  holds it once by its `(timestamp, id)`. Every count (`event_series`'s bars,
  `total`, `failed` and `by_category`, `trace`'s and `turn`'s `total`, a
  `turns` row's tokens, `phases` and `duration_ms`, the outcome counts on
  `integrations`) counts it once: each node counts the rows it keeps
  and names the ones it has not settled, and the serving node asks which node
  keeps each named row before adding it.
- **`event` not found** answers `not_found` naming any node that did not
  answer, since a silent node differs from a dead one. An event older than the 30-day history is not found
  either: it is past the horizon every read of the log stops at, and a row a
  node's sweep has not yet deleted is not served; every node
  floors its lookup by id at the serving node's horizon.
- **Every question is asked at one instant**, the serving node's clock
  when it arrived, which travels with it. Every node floors the 30-day history at the serving node's horizon, not its
  own, and one node's part of an answer (a turn's rows, count, ending
  and traces) is read at that instant throughout. A node answering late or with a fast clock therefore holds back nothing
  the others include. A question carrying no instant is refused.

`turns` merges in two passes: every data node's page, then every data node's share of
exactly the turns any page listed, so a turn resumed on another node after a
restart is one row folded from both halves. The window is pinned to the asker's clock
(the instant travels with the question, so every node floors the
window and its share of each turn at the asker's 30-day horizon), and the merged turn is held to it whole: a node's half of a resumed
turn can start inside the window while the turn began before it elsewhere.

A turn is **paged where a node lists it**: at the earliest start at which any
node's own page lists it, which each node says of its share in the second
pass. That is not always its `started_at` (where the turn began): a
turn resumed across nodes is selected by each node on its own half, so under
a filter the whole turn passes but the half where it began may not (the clean
half of a turn that failed later, under `failed=true`; the half that names no
item of a turn charged to an item only by its later records, under
`work_item=`). Paged at its `started_at`, such a turn could fall behind the cursor and
on no page of the walk.
Walking `next` lists every turn exactly once, even two turns starting at one
microsecond: the cursor is that position and the turn's id, and every node resumes after exactly the turn
the last page ended on. Rows are newest first by that position, the higher
`turn_id` first within one microsecond, so a row whose `started_at` is earlier
than where it is listed can sit above rows that began after it.
`next` is the fleet's cursor:
it can be present on an empty page, where a node's page stopped before any
turn above it could be shown. With `sort=-tokens` the page ranks each node's
top turns by their MERGED totals and carries no cursor (`before=` is refused
`bad_params`): a ranking has no position to resume from, and it can miss a
turn split across nodes whose every half fell below every node's cut.

### The runtime audit: `source=operator`

Every change a person makes through a running node leaves one event, whether
or not it went through:

| Event type | Written for |
|---|---|
| `operator_acted` | Every [operator tool](#operatormcp--your-own-assistant) call that is not a proven read and not a person's own bookkeeping (`own_record_marked`, below), on **all three** transports: a dashboard button (`/operator/act`), a person's own assistant (`/operator/mcp`) and a script on the [human write surface](#the-human-write-surface) (`/worklet`, `/doclet/pages`), whose verbs with no tool behind them are recorded too. A write Ask Crewlet sent after you approved it is recorded under the transport `assistant`, its credential `assist:<grant>`, with an `assistant` reference (`conversation_id`, `turn_id`, `grant_id`, `session`, `proposal_id`) and `conversation_id` beside it as a listing field |
| `own_record_marked` | Every such call to a tool that keeps only the caller's OWN bookkeeping: `mark_chat_read`, `mark_inbox`, the code inbox's marks and `set_pins`, each taking no name. Same fields as `operator_acted`, under a type the activity feed leaves out ([stored, not in the activity feed](../guides/deployment.md#what-gets-stored-and-under-which-category)): reading one's rooms is not something the company did. A write to a person's record BY NAME (`PUT /worklet/people/{handle}/inbox` and `/pins`) is `operator_acted`, whoever's record it names |
| `backup_requested` | Every [`POST /backup`](#post-backup) that began copying, finished or not |
| `assistant_conversation_read` | Every administrator's compliance read of a person's Ask Crewlet conversation: the reader, `conversation_id`, `owner_id` and the reason given, and `file_id` for a compliance download of one file. The conversation itself is never copied here |
| `assistant_turn_completed` | Every segment of a person's Ask Crewlet turn: answered, stopped, failed, out of budget, or parked on a proposal. It names the conversation, the turn (`assistant_turn_id`, never a seat's `turn_id`), how it ended and every step's tool, route pattern, outcome, HTTP status and bytes read; never an argument, an answer or the person's question |

Each carries `source: "operator"` on the envelope, so
`GET /events?source=operator` is the runtime audit alone. Who acted is
[the one attribution](#who-a-write-is-attributed-to): `actor` (the seat's handle for a person, or for a token or
service account bound to one, and the login otherwise), `actor_kind` (`human`, `operator` or `system`) and
`operator_id` (the credential: `session:<lineage>`, `pat:<id>`, or a Tier A
token's login), resolved once for the call so a directory rebind landing
meanwhile never makes the record name a different person. All are filed
under `lifecycle`.

```json
{"type": "operator_acted", "source": "operator",
 "actor": "jane-founder", "actor_kind": "human",
 "operator_id": "session:0192f0aa-61c2-7d1e-9b40-3c5d7e8f9a01",
 "transport": "act", "tool": "update_work_item",
 "request_id": "0192f1a4-9b2d-7c03-a4e1-5f3b9d0c7a12.k3f9a1c0d2e4b6a88",
 "outcome": "applied", "position": "CREWLET_TRACKER_LOG@1:4711"}
```

`outcome` is one of five: `applied`, `pending` and `unknown` are the write's own
answer as the call returned it (a call interrupted before answering is `unknown`: whether it landed is what nobody
knows); `refused` names the tool's refusal class in `refusal`; `failed` is a
node fault (`internal_error`) or a failure the tool did not classify,
and carries no `refusal`. The last two also carry `failed: true`, so
the log's failure filter finds the row. `request_id`
is the operation the call was made under: the request's `Idempotency-Key` as
the caller's own operation on the act and write surfaces, absent over MCP, so
every retry of one gesture reads as the same request. A backup's record names the `dir` and the number of
`streams` the manifest covers; the node whose disk it was written to is the
envelope's `node` (the queue stamps it on every event with the publishing node; the backup route publishes from the node that took the copy).

**The arguments are never recorded.** A page body or comment is the
company's content and already lives in the history of the object it changed;
the audit says who called what, and what became of it.

**A listing carries what a row needs without its payload.** `GET /events`
never returns payloads, so the store promotes the audit's dimensions
into each row's `tags`: `actor_kind` and `operator_id` (beside
the row's own `actor` column), `tool` (an `operator_acted` call's tool),
`dir` (a `backup_requested` copy's directory) and `conversation_id` (an
`assistant_turn_completed` turn's conversation), beside `node`, the publishing node, which every event row carries. The dashboard's
Audit log and backup history draw from these. A failure's kind is a tag too,
`error_kind` (an `executor_collected` launch's `max_turns` or `out_of_memory`, a
turn's `budget_exhausted`), and a spend record's row carries its `tokens` and
`calls` (a launch's are its harness's rounds).

**What is not here.** A request refused before any tool ran (a read sent to
the write transport, a token that is nobody, a malformed body, a backup with
no destination or one it refused (the `400`s below), a chat erase or
prune missing its confirmation, reason or cutoff) changed nothing and
is not recorded, except where the write surface refused it on its own authority
decision, on a stored row it read before any tool ran (a remark
somebody else wrote, an item's own project): that is `refused` like a tool's
refusal, since "you may not" is a fact an audit is read for.
A gesture with no tool behind it (a purge, a page's rename, trash and restore,
a comment take-down, a remark rewritten, and [a chat erase, prune or
horizon](#a-chat-erase-prune-or-horizon) under its verb: `chat.erase`,
`chat.prune`, `chat.channel.retention`) is recorded as a tool call is. A
chat erase's `reason` is not on its row: it travels on the
erase record itself, on the chat log, and in the serving node's `chat_erased`
log line; no row any data node keeps carries it. A
proven read over MCP is not recorded either, since a row per question
would bury the writes. Configuration and credentials keep their own records
(a revision names who created it, a credential who stored it), so
`/config` and `/secrets` publish nothing here. Like every event, the row
is written by the node the call reached, so a fleet's audit is the union of
its nodes' logs.

A record that could not be published is logged as
`operator_audit_not_published` at error on that node; the call is
already answered, and its tracker or page history is unaffected.

### The event log's time axis

`GET /events/series` counts the matching rows per bucket over a window. It
takes every filter `GET /events` takes bar the cursor and `agent` (see
below), plus:

| Name | Default | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `bucket` | *(required)* | `minute`, `hour` or `day`: a closed set, since an arbitrary width is an axis nobody can label. The log has `minute` (the spend series does not) because "what just happened" is the commonest question asked of a log. An unknown value is refused naming what is accepted, never defaulted. |
| `since` / `until` | (the 30-day history, to now) | RFC 3339 instants, half-open. Both edges snap **outward** to whole buckets, so the first and last bars are whole (a partial bar means something different from its neighbours'). No snap crosses the 30-day history (`event_history_seconds`): a window it clips, the default one included, begins at the **first whole bucket inside it**, and a window wholly below that bucket covers nothing (`since` equals `until`, no bars). The answer is labelled with the window it actually covers. |

The answer is `{bucket, since, until, bars, total, failed, by_category}`.
`bars` is **every** bucket in the window including empty ones, so a
quiet hour is a full-width gap.

The whole answer is cut against **one instant**, the serving node's clock
when the question arrived, and every count in it (`bars`, `total`, `failed`
and `by_category`) keeps rows from 30 days before that instant.
Across a fleet that instant is sent with the question, so every node cuts the
same bars (a window the history clips is cut down to the bucket the horizon
falls in, its first bar counting only what lies above the horizon) and
floors counts at the serving node's horizon. The
serving node sums every node's bars and only then drops that partial bar, so
no bar starts below the horizon (see `since` above), every bar
lies wholly inside the history, and a row any node holds inside a bar, the
first included, is counted however long that node took to answer.

Each bar is `{at, count, failed}`. `failed` is how many of the bar's rows
reported a failure, by the rule a turn's own `failed` mark uses: the event
said so, or its type is one (`llm_unavailable`, `budget_exhausted`,
`turn.guard_breach`, `executor_failed`). It is a **split** of
`count`, never an addition. The answer's own `failed` is the sum of the bars'. The engine counts these because a
screen holds a page of rows, never the window.

`by_category` is how many rows each category would give with the
**category filter lifted** and every other one applied (counted through its own filter, every value
but the selected one would read zero). A category with no rows is absent, so a
caller rendering the closed set reads a missing key as zero.

It is counted over the window **that was asked for**, not the snapped one
`since` and `until` report: a chip says how many rows choosing it would
show, and those come from `GET /events` with the caller's own
edges. So the chips need not sum to `total`, which describes the whole-bucket bars. On a window the history clips, the chips reach down
to the horizon itself and so also count rows between it and the first
whole bucket, which no bar draws.

Two refusals, both **400** rather than a smaller answer:

- **`related_agent`** is not accepted. That filter folds each page's trace
  siblings into it (see above), so a count over the predicate alone is smaller than the listing shows, and a bar must not disagree with its
  own rows.
- **A window of more than 1,500 buckets** is refused naming the bucket and
  the span. Truncating would put a month's heading over a day of bars and
  coarsening would answer another question; use a coarser bucket or a shorter window.
  The buckets counted are the ones every node cuts, so on a window the
  history clips they include the one the horizon falls in, which the answer
  then drops.

### The live token meter

`budget` carries the fleet's **shared token counters** as the budget gate
enforces them: for the company and for every seat whose `token_budget` caps a
window, **one entry per capped calendar window** (the day, the ISO week and the
month on the company's clock) with that window's spend, its ceiling (from the revision this node runs), the gate's refusal stamp and the engine's judgement of it. It
is the only figure that can honestly be divided into a configured ceiling,
since both cover the same span. The dashboard's other token figures are spend
rollups over a reader-chosen window; dividing one into a
ceiling is wrong by whatever was spent outside it.

```json
{
  "meter_id": "node-a:7f3c…", "seq": 42, "timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
  "org": {
    "windows": [
      {
        "period": "day", "window": "2026-09-23",
        "starts_at": "2026-09-22T22:00:00Z", "resets_at": "2026-09-23T22:00:00Z",
        "used": 2710450, "limit": 3000000, "state": "near"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

A seat's meter rides on its row of the `agents` push as `budget: {windows: […]}`
in the same shape.

- `period` is `day`, `week` or `month`, and `window` is its label on the
  company's clock, the same on every node. `starts_at` and
  `resets_at` are the window's half-open span in UTC; `resets_at` is when its
  allowance comes back without a ceiling being raised. `timezone` names the
  clock the windows were cut on.
- Only **capped** windows are listed, each with its `limit`; a scope that caps
  none carries `windows: []`, and a seat that caps none carries no meter.
- `state` is the engine's own judgement, so no screen holds a threshold: `refusing` when the window has no
  room left for a single token (every window that refused a round, since the refused round is counted, and the condition a seat is
  [parked](../concepts/agent-runtime.md#the-budget-park) on), `near` once
  `used` reaches **nine tenths** of `limit`
  (`engine.BudgetNearFraction`, served as `near_fraction` on
  [`GET /budgets`](#get-budgets)), and `ok` otherwise.
- `refused_at` is when the window last turned a call away, in UTC, and
  **absent** while it has not: a round whose charge it refused, or work turned
  away before its first call because the window was already full (a turn's
  next call, a seat's delivery parked, a person's question, a reflection pass),
  each recorded as the gate's refusal on the scope a charge would be refused
  by, the company's before the seat's. A refused round is counted in
  `used` (the vendor billed it), so a window that refused one
  reads past its `limit` by that round, and every later charge is refused
  against that figure. The stamp is kept in the shared counter, so every node reports the same one; it clears on the scope's next
  admitted charge or when the window turns over. A window whose ceiling was
  raised after a refusal keeps its `refused_at` until then, under a `state` of
  `ok` or `near`: it has room again, and the stamp is history.

Every node publishes a `budget_meters` snapshot of the counters as soon as its
seat host is running and every **15 seconds** (`engine.BudgetReportInterval`)
after, and **at once** when a budget window first refuses a charge, so
a stop reaches every open screen with the
refusal (a repeat refusal in the same window
waits for the tick). The projection folds each one in as it arrives. Until
the first lands, `budget` is **`null`** (nobody has read the counter), a different fact from a report whose `org.windows` is `[]` ("nothing
is capped"). A company with no ceiling anywhere publishes exactly that: an empty
list and no seats, without reading the counter. A node whose read of the
counter fails publishes nothing that interval, so the meter keeps the last
reading rather than drawing zeroes.

- `meter_id` identifies the node incarnation whose report is held. Every node
  reads the same counter, so reports under different ids describe the same
  figures at different moments. A report is a complete snapshot, so a
  consumer **replaces** what it holds rather than merging or taking a
  maximum: a window turning over must be able to lower the figure, and a
  ceiling removed must take its window's bar with it.
- `seq` is monotonic within a `meter_id`. The feed is
  **best-effort**: an ephemeral broadcast subscription that takes no acks,
  starts at the stream's tail on every (re)connect, and lets a slow consumer
  miss frames. So a report at or below the held `seq`
  from the same meter is dropped, a report from another meter read
  **earlier** than the held one is dropped, and a gap is closed by the next
  report, not replayed.
- `{}` means no report has arrived yet. Per-agent, `budget: null` means the
  same, or that the seat has no per-agent ceiling: the engine meters a
  seat only when its `token_budget` caps a window.

It is never persisted: a report reads a counter that
moves every round, so a replayed copy would show stale figures as current.

Each agent's `live_calls` is a list, `[]` between turns, of one call per turn the
seat runs (paired with its turn by `turn_id`), oldest first, each
`{ turn_id, phase, iteration, model, prompt, prompt_messages, response,
tool_executions, calls_elided, elided_calls, round_narration, partial_round,
round_num, rounds_used, rounds, rounds_elided, invocations, max_rounds, round_ceiling, round_started_at,
run_started_at, running_calls, running_calls_elided, steers,
cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, work_item, node, in_progress, versions }`
while an LLM call is under
way:

- `prompt_messages` is `[{role, content, sections}]`, the conversation the phase opened with. `sections` is that message's outline as the prompt's builder recorded it, `[{key, title, bytes, headed?}]`, tiling `content` exactly, with `headed: true` on a part that opens on its own heading line whose text is `title` (absent on a part the builder named, which may still open on a heading of its content's). It is absent on a message no builder outlined or whose text is not valid UTF-8; a finished phase record carries the same maps as `system_sections` and `user_sections`. See [a prompt carries its outline](../concepts/turn-engine.md#what-streams-during-a-turn) for the keys and the rules to check before slicing by one.
- `round_narration` is `[{round, content, declined}]`, what the model said in each round so far; `declined: true` marks a round that answered in prose where the phase had to end in a call, and is absent otherwise.
- `rounds_used` is the round the phase is on, counted from one: rounds that have come back, plus the one in flight from the frame published as that round's provider call is made. A finished phase record carries the same count under the same name.
- `rounds` is each round's own timing and tokens (a round is one model request, as the harness's record shows it): `{round, started_at, duration_ms, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, tool_calls, stop_reason}`.
- `invocations` is the phase's harness runs that have **ended**, each `{started_at, duration_ms, provider_key, model, outcome, first_round, last_round, requests_observed, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, tool_calls}`, as on the [phase record](../concepts/turn-engine.md#what-a-turn-records-about-its-time). The run in flight is not on it until it ends: its rounds are those past every entry's `last_round`. Empty until the first run ends.
- `max_rounds` is the round cap currently granted, which an extension can raise mid-phase.
- `round_ceiling` is the highest value any extension may raise `max_rounds` to.
- `round_started_at` is when the latest round made its provider call. It is later than every entry in `rounds` while that call is out, and equal to the last entry's start while the round's tools run; only the first is a model call in flight.
- `run_started_at` is when the harness run in flight was launched (the run whose rounds are past every entry in `invocations`). Absent between runs.
- `running_calls` is every tool call running now, in arrival order, each `{id, round, name, arguments, started_at}`: a **list**, since a harness may make a response's calls at once. `id` is the call's id, which its `tool_executions` row carries as `call_id` once answered. It is absent while no call runs and never carried forward from an earlier frame: a frame that stops listing a call means the call returned.
- `steers` is every person's note the phase has read so far, `{round, note_id, boundary}`: the round whose provider call first saw it, and the kind of step that read it (`round`, or `brief`, `tool_batch`, `finish` or `step` for a read by the phase's executor in its box, which is round 1). What the note said and who sent it are on the turn's `agent_turn_steered` rows. See [steering a running turn](#steering-a-running-turn).
- `node` is the node running the call.
- `versions` is `{prompt, response, narration, executions, rounds}`: the version of the copy the call holds of each heavy field. `prompt` numbers `prompt` and `prompt_messages`, `response` the `response`, `narration` the `round_narration`, `executions` the `tool_executions` with its `calls_elided` and `elided_calls`, and `rounds` the `rounds`. A number the node's projection never hands out twice, taken whenever the field is written: every field when the call begins, then each field a frame changes. So on the node a tab's socket reads, a version only grows for every call under every key, and a call cleared and rebuilt under its own key (`turn_id`, `phase`, `iteration`) is newer in every field than the copy a tab held before. A reconnecting tab is sent a snapshot, which replaces every copy it holds. Every surface that carries a call carries it.

Beside `live_calls`, each seat carries `live_call_seq`: the node projection's
own sequence (the one `versions` come from) read when any of the seat's calls
last changed: began, took a frame, froze as failed, or was cleared.
It is on every surface that carries the calls, an empty list included, and it
orders the calls themselves where a field's version cannot: across a clear,
which leaves no version behind, and across two calls, whose fields are never
compared (see [What the projection carries, and what the wire
sends](#what-the-projection-carries-and-what-the-wire-sends)). Like a version it
is a fact about one node's projection, and a snapshot resets what a tab holds.

Beside `live_calls`, each seat carries `turns`, `last_turn` and `paused`: the turns the seat is on, each with its `stage` of `context`, `phase` or `parked`, the newest turn it ended, and who paused the seat, when and why (`null` while nobody has). See [Agent States](../concepts/agent-runtime.md#agent-states). A call whose phase failed keeps `in_progress: false`
plus `failed: true` and an `error` object, so the dashboard renders the failure,
and no `partial_round` (the phase is over). The failed call stays until the
seat's next call opens, on that turn or another; the same phase running again under the same
turn and iteration (the review of a parked turn's resume that is held or
retried) replaces it with a call of its own rather than continuing the failed
one's rounds.

**A failure is told by its kind, and the company's configuration only to an
admin.** The `error` object and a seat's `last_error` are
`{kind, detail, phase, turn_id, at, event_id}`: `kind` is the classifier's
(`rate_limit`, `auth`, `server`, and the others), which the dashboard words for a
person, and `detail` is the failure in its own words, sent only to an admin. Those words name the company's `providers.llm` entries ("llm chain
exhausted after 1 provider (default)") and carry whatever a vendor or tool
wrote, and which entries a company configures is an admin's to read. The same
goes for each `invocations` entry's `provider_key`, and for the `provider_key`
of an executor on the `executors` push and snapshot and on the
[`executors`](#get-executors) board, which every other
reader, a seat's lead included, is sent without. The full text stays in the
engine's log and on the turn's own record.

#### What the projection carries, and what the wire sends

A running phase moves its seat's row on every progress frame (five times a
second while a round streams), so frames into the projection and
pushes out of it are trimmed and reassembled on the other side:

- **Into the projection**, `prompt` and `prompt_messages` are sent **once**,
  on the phase's opening frame, and carried forward (a 30 KB system
  prompt does not change mid-phase, and past `queue.MaxPayloadBytes` the
  publish is refused outright and the live row stops); a tool result
  and the joined `response` are sent **tail-bounded** on a live frame, since
  readers watch their end. The durable
  `agent_phase_completed` record keeps every one of them whole within its
  share of one message, and says what it left out past it
  ([what an agent record keeps](../concepts/event-system.md#what-an-agent-record-keeps)):
  a failed phase's call is frozen with that record's list, and carries its
  `calls_elided` and `elided_calls`. A running phase's frame is held to live
  shares instead: past them it
  keeps the newest calls (`calls_elided`, `elided_calls`), its first and newest
  rounds (`rounds_elided`, versioned with `rounds`) and the calls in flight that
  fit (`running_calls_elided`, carried as `running_calls` is).
- **Out to a tab**, an `agents` push carries a call's HEAVY fields (`prompt`
  and `prompt_messages`, `response`, `round_narration`, `tool_executions` with
  its `calls_elided` and `elided_calls`, and `rounds`) only when their version (`versions`) moved since the last push for
  the same call. Otherwise the key is ABSENT, never empty,
  and the tab keeps the copy it holds. They move once a round or once a tool
  call; between those, a push is the round being written
  (`partial_round`), the call in flight and the light fields. Over one
  long phase on the engine host (thirty rounds, 1 311 frames), each
  open tab is sent 5.9 MiB, against 185 MiB with every push whole.
- **A dropped push is noticed by the next one.** The socket drops a slow tab's
  oldest envelope rather than stalling every other tab, and a delta frame, dropped, would
  leave a tab wrong with nothing to say so. Every push names every version, so
  the push after a dropped one names a version past the copy the tab holds,
  and the tab asks for the seat's calls whole ([`live_call`](#queries)) rather than
  drawing the older copy as current. A field a push carries at a version older
  than the tab's (a push overtaken by a snapshot or an answer) is
  not taken. The handshake snapshot, `GET /agents`, the `agent` answer and the
  `live_call` answer always carry every field.
- **An answer is ordered against the pushes that overtake it.** The
  `live_call` answer is computed on its own and can reach the tab after a later push,
  so it carries the seat's `live_call_seq`, which the
  tab compares with the newest it has applied for the seat. An answer at or
  past it is merged like a push carrying everything. One BEHIND it describes
  each turn's call before those pushes: where they cleared that call or began
  another, that call is dropped (so a stopped seat never shows the running call
  read just before its completion); when they are the same call, it
  still brings each heavy field it holds at a newer version than the tab's,
  while the light fields stay the pushes'. If a push found the call behind
  while the answer was out, the tab asks again once that answer lands behind
  it, rather than waiting for a next push a frozen call never sends. An
  `agents` push whose `live_call_seq` is behind an answer already applied
  leaves the calls as the answer had them, and its other fields still apply.
- **A version is never handed out twice**, so "moved" and "newer" are one
  question. Counted per call, a call cleared and rebuilt under the same
  turn, phase and iteration would number its fields from one again, and a tab
  that missed the clearing push and the first after it would read
  every later push as older than its held copy, and keep that copy.

### `WS /ws/stream`

Upgrades to a WebSocket.  All frames are JSON envelopes of the form
`{"kind": "...", "data": ..., "ts": "<iso8601>"}`.

> **The socket is the dashboard's channel for state, not for everything.**
> The projection arrives here as pushes, and every question the query
> registry answers is asked and answered here too. REST carries
> every write: through
> [`/operator/act`](#operatoract--the-dashboards-write-surface) as the
> principal the session resolves to, through `/iam`, or through
> `/config`, `/secrets`, `/setup` and `/backup` (a write has to be
> able to say whether it happened, and a frame into a dropped socket has no
> answer), and the few guarded reads no query answers (`GET /secrets`,
> `GET /config/references`, `GET /setup/integrations` and its passes), which
> the dashboard reads through one loader
> that re-reads when the session changes and honours a `Retry-After`. The
> dashboard survives losing the socket by polling `/stream/snapshot` every
> five seconds, or when a `503` it answers says, and not at all after one
> with no `Retry-After`. Such a failure is easy
> to miss: the page is simply always a few seconds
> stale. `internal/e2e` closes that gap by replaying the frames a real server
> produced through the dashboard's own protocol module
> (`static/protocol/protocol.js`, the same source its bundle contains), so
> both halves of the protocol are checked against each other.
>
> **A kind a client does not know is ignored, never an error.** A fleet part
> way through a rolling upgrade has a node pushing kinds an older bundle predates, so
> the dashboard drops such a frame and counts it (the
> same fall-through is what a kind this build's engine sends and its own
> client forgot looks like), and the e2e replay fails on a non-zero count.

**Who may open it, and what each reader receives.** The handshake admits
every principal the guard resolves whose stage may act (the overview is
everybody's) and refuses one whose stage may not `403` before the upgrade.
Every push kind is received only by a socket whose caller holds what that
kind's question takes: `event` needs `admin` (it is an `events` row, carrying
every phase's prompt and response); `inbox_changed` needs the `watch` of its
seat that was allowed (the room decides, as an artifact's does) and the app of
the half that moved (`worklet` for a `tracker` frame, `gitlet` for a `code`
one, since each half of the inbox is listed only to a holder of its app); the eight
`chat_*` kinds need `chatlet` and a caller acting as a human seat (a socket whose
principal acts as no seat is shown no chat at all, a public room included), and
each chat frame then goes only to sockets whose seat may see its room
(`chatlet.Visible`); every other company kind is everybody's. The `agents`, `seats` and `executors`
pushes carry a call's and a run's **body** only to a caller who may read that
seat's (an administrator, or its lead), and to everybody else its status with
`body_withheld: true` ([A status reader never receives a
transcript](#a-status-reader-never-receives-a-transcript)). The snapshot is
built for the same audience. When the socket's credential is decided again and
it resolves somebody else (another login, another seat or none, other
permissions), or a published company moves which seats' bodies the caller may
read, the socket closes `1013`, and the reconnect's handshake builds the
snapshot for the new audience while the client asks who it is again; see
[Close codes](#close-codes).
#### Pushes

Server → client kinds:

| `kind` | When | `data` |
|--------|------|--------|
| `snapshot` | First envelope after the upgrade, and again on reconnect. | Same payload as `GET /stream/snapshot`. Agents carry their in-flight `live_calls` and `live_call_seq`, so a reconnect re-renders the live rows and restarts the calls' ordering. |
| `event`    | Every engine event published to `crewlet.events.>`. | `{ id, type, timestamp, source, actor, summary, category, trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, topic, agent_id?, channel_id?, payload }`: a `/events` row plus the full `payload` (from which the snapshot feed's `failed` flag derives). `agent_id` is the seat the event concerns and `channel_id` its agent-to-agent channel, filled by the rule that fills the store's own column, so live rows narrow to a seat or channel as pages do. `agent_phase_completed` events carry the system prompt, response and tool calls, so LLM invocations stream live; `agent_turn_progress` events (per tool-call round, tagged `turn_id` / `phase` / `iteration`) stream the in-flight call before its phase record exists. |
| `agents`   | After an event moved agents, or a read did (a run record reconcile, or the seat-lease read of the five-second tick). | The changed agents' overlays, each with `agent_id`, `role`, `activity` and `stopped_reason`: the *result* of the change, so a client merges rather than running its own state machine. Merge an overlay onto the roster row with the same `agent_id`; DROP one for a seat the roster lacks (a seat reaches the roster through the snapshot or a `seats` push, each already carrying its merged overlay). Each of its `live_calls` carries its heavy fields only when their `versions` moved since the last push for that call (paired by `turn_id`); keep the copy you hold of one left out. Every row carries the seat's `live_call_seq`, an empty list included, which orders the calls against a `live_call` answer (see [What the projection carries, and what the wire sends](#what-the-projection-carries-and-what-the-wire-sends)). |
| `seats`    | After anything changed the company (config activation, hire, move, removal). | The COMPLETE seat list, replacing what the client holds, each row with `agent_id`, current `handle` and `role` (name). Not folded into `agents` because a per-seat merge cannot express a seat's deletion. |
| `executors`| After an executor was launched in its box, asked a question, finished or was lost, and after a reconcile against the durable run record changed the set. | Every executor in flight. |
| `tokens`   | On the shared 5-second tick, when a spend record arrived or aged out of the live window since the last one (one aggregation per tick, not per phase). | The spend rollup, same shape as `GET /tokens/breakdown`. |
| `budget`   | After a node's token meter report is applied (every node reports at start, every 15 seconds, and at once when a budget window first refuses a charge, a company that caps nothing included). | `{ meter_id, seq, timezone, org: { windows: [...] } }`, the org-wide half: one entry per capped calendar window with span, spend, ceiling, refusal stamp and `state`. Per-seat figures ride on each agent's overlay in the `agents` push. See [the live token meter](#the-live-token-meter). |
| `org` / `tools` / `schedules` | On the same edge as `seats`: every published company. | The new org tree / tool surface / schedule list, so open tabs stop showing vanished seats. |
| `health`   | Every 5s, from a **single shared tick** (one timer for all clients). | The whole [health envelope](#the-health-envelope), exactly what `GET /health` answers. There is no query for it. |
| `result`   | Reply to a client `query` that succeeded. | `{ id, what, data }`; `id` echoes the request's. |
| `error`    | Reply to a client `query` that could not be answered, a `watch` not installed, or an `artifact_join` refused or an artifact's room withdrawn (`what: "artifact_join"`, naming the `artifact`; see `artifact_join` below). | `{ id, what, error, reason?, grants?, role?, retry_after?, refusal?, detail? }`; `error` is a code. See the rules below the table. |
| `pong`     | Reply to a client `ping`. | `null` |
| `inbox_changed` | A committed batch of a domain that keeps a person's notices (Worklet's, Gitlet's or the artifacts') wrote the watched seat notices or took some away. Every node serving the API holds the estate (`ingress` requires `data`), so each pushes to its OWN sockets from its own applier after the commit. While a node's own copy of a domain is out of service it stays in rotation and pushes the movements of a data node serving that domain, relayed over the broker, withholding its own applier's for that domain alone. Every switch of a domain's source sends each watched seat one frame naming that `source` with `unread_delta: 0` and empty `subject` and `reason`, because what moved during the switch is not replayed: read the inbox again. A node falling behind the peer it follows does the same, keeping that domain's movements for one round trip past its latest answer, at most 4 000. One frame per seat per batch. | `{ source, handle, unread_delta, subject, reason }`, and the frame itself carries `seat`. **Identifiers and a count, never content**: `source` is the domain whose notices moved (`tracker`, `code`, `artifacts`); `subject` is the id of the object the newest notice was written on (always empty on an `artifacts` frame): the task for a task commit, the change for a record about a change, the PERSON for a `prioritised` notice (whose task Worklet's notice names as `task`); `reason` is the reason it was routed under, in that domain's vocabulary. Read the notices through the composed `inbox` question, which decides who may read each domain's; `work_inbox` answers Worklet's alone, so a client re-reading it on a `code` frame never sees the notice that moved. `unread_delta` is a **hint** (a redelivery the engine already collapsed may count twice), so re-ask rather than add it to a badge. **Routed by seat, held to the half's app**: it reaches only clients whose `watch` for that seat was allowed (decided as the composed `inbox` question about that seat, with no app, since the halves are several apps' news), and of those only a reader holding the app of the half that moved: `worklet` for a `tracker` frame, `gitlet` for a `code` one ([ADR-0110](../../adr/0110-reaching-a-repository-takes-the-gitlet-permission.md)). An `artifacts` frame needs no app and reaches every watcher, naming no subject: each comment notice is held to its artifact's relation by the read, which a frame cannot decide. |
| `artifact_changed` | A committed artifacts batch moved an artifact whose room this socket is in: a version published, its title, description, icon or a label, shares, assets, trash, restore, transfer, purge, its folder, or a comment thread. Each node pushes from its own applier; while its own copy is out of service it pushes a sound data node's movements instead, relayed over the broker, and every switch of source pushes every room a `reset`, as for `inbox_changed`. | `{ artifact, what, head, position }`, where `what` is `version`, `meta`, `share`, `asset`, `trash`, `restore`, `purge`, `transfer`, `folder` (filed in another folder; a folder's removal, which re-files what it held, is not pushed per artifact), `comment` (a thread opened, a remark added, edited or removed, a thread resolved or reopened; it changes nothing about who may read, so the room is not decided again) or `reset` (this node cannot say which artifacts moved, or what moved across a switch of source: re-read; the room is decided again). **A hint, never content**: re-read through the questions that decide what you may see. |
| `artifact_data` | A committed datastore batch changed documents of an artifact whose room this socket is in. Each data node pushes from its own applier after the commit, or from a sound data node's while its own copy is out of service, as `artifact_changed` does. | `{ artifact, deltas?, keys?, reread?, schema?, resync?, gone?, through }`. **Shaped per reader**: a document in an `own_rows`, `editors` or `private` collection goes only to the members its rule admits, by the role each member's join decided; a batch a member may see none of is not pushed to them. Changed documents travel inline (`deltas`: `collection`, `doc`, `version`, `deleted`, `body`, `read`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `updated_at`) while the frame stays within 64 KiB, otherwise as `keys` with `reread: true`. `schema` says collections changed; `resync` says this node's pushes may have gaps, a switch of source among them (read whole); `gone` says the datastore was purged. `through` is the store's version after the batch, the `since` of the next catch-up. |
| `artifact_presence` | Who is in an artifact's room changed: somebody joined, left, or moved what they do or look at, on this node or another. Coalesced to at most ten a second per room, each carrying at most ten new or changed members (longest-waiting first, the rest in following frames). | `{ artifact, upsert, leave, counts?, truncated }`: the members now presented that are new or changed (`session`, `seat`, `kind`, `activity`, `focus`, `at`, and for an agent `turn`, the run of the turn whose tool call put it there), and the sessions no longer presented. Past 50 members a room presents the 50 most recently active with `truncated: true` and `counts: { human, agent }` of the rest, and returns to everybody below 40. **Told, never stored**: see [Presence](#presence-in-an-artifacts-room). |
| `chat_posted` / `chat_edited` / `chat_deleted` / `chat_reacted` | A committed chat record put, rewrote, tombstoned or reacted to a message. Sent only to sockets whose seat may read the room (see [Chatlet](#chatlet)), decided at the batch's own position. | `{ channel_id, op, op_id, message_id, channel_seq, thread_root?, author, author_kind, at, position, excerpt?, mentions?, channel_name?, channel_kind? }`: evidence that something landed, never the message. `channel_seq` is contiguous per room, so a client holding 41 and handed 43 reads 42; `op_id` is how a tab recognises its own gesture coming back. |
| `chat_room_changed` / `chat_membership_changed` | A room was created, patched, given a horizon, erased or pruned; its membership was replaced. **People a membership change took out of a private room are sent its `chat_membership_changed` too**, though they may no longer read the room, so their rail lets it go without waiting for its next read; the frame names the room and the record and no member. **A `chat_room_changed` naming no room** (`channel_id` empty) is a GAP: this node switched the source of its chat batches or fell behind and dropped some, and the screen reads every room it holds again. | The same shape, the room's own fields only. |
| `chat_cursor_moved` | A person's own read state moved (a flush, a mute, do-not-disturb) through any surface on any node: every node serving sockets watches the coordination record and pushes the change to that seat's own sockets only. | `{ handle, cursors?, muted?, dnd_until?, updated_at?, revision }`: the WHOLE state; keep the one with the highest `revision`, which the rail's `read` carries too. |
| `chat_presence` | Who is in the chat room this socket's `presence` frame named (`room: "chat"`) changed: somebody opened it, left, started or stopped typing, or a seat began or stopped working on an answer there, on this node or another. Also the room whole as the socket joins it, ahead of every later change. Only a socket whose seat may read the room is put in its presence, and a record that narrows the room takes out every socket whose seat no longer may. Coalesced as `artifact_presence` is. | `{ channel_id, roster?, upsert, leave, counts?, truncated }`: with `roster: true` the room whole, replacing what was held (a roster naming nobody is the socket taken out of the room); otherwise the members now presented that are new or changed and the sessions no longer presented, in `artifact_presence`'s member shape. A person is `viewing`, or `editing` while they type (the engine puts it back to `viewing` six seconds after the last re-assert); a seat at work is an `agent` member, `editing`, with `focus.thread` the message its answer will land under (empty for the room), `status` the phrase the room shows and `turn` its run. **Told, never stored**, by the presence hub every room shares (ADR-0038). |

**`error` frames**

- `unauthorized` adds `reason` and `grants`, as the REST envelope does: the rule that decided, and the grants any one of which would admit the caller (an EMPTY list means no grant would, because what is missing is a relation such as leading that person). On an artifact refused for a role below the verb's need, `role` is the role to ask the owner for.
- A refusal on authority is worded by the authority table's one mapping on every transport, so `code`, `reason`, `grants` and `role` match the same decision everywhere. A caller with no relation to an artifact gets `not_found` with nothing beside it, as for an id nothing holds.
- **No question or watch is decided by a verb that asks a recent proof or needs a person present** (a question registered that way is refused at node start, and the build checks the verbs an answer decides by inside itself). So a frame, and a query's REST answer, is never `step_up_required` or `token_refused`: the socket cannot carry a step-up.
- A **watch refusal** has no `id` and names `what: "watch"`:
  - `unauthorized`: the caller may not watch that seat (with `reason` and `grants`).
  - `unavailable`: this node could not read the chart that decides it or the directory a login resolves through. Carries `retry_after` as a query's `unavailable` does (same rule, `0` for a read no wait clears), never the `refusal` or `detail` behind it, because what the directory says about a login names the seat it is bound to.
  - `not_found`: a login names no record; only `admin` is ever told.
- Query codes: `unknown_query`, `unauthorized`, `not_found`, `bad_params`, `unavailable`, `artifact_trashed`, the five revision codes (`unreadable_revision`, `unsealed_revision`, `unreadable_fleet_revision`, `unsealed_fleet_revision`, `unknown_seal_revision`, each with a `detail` naming what fixes it, as [`/config`](#a-revision-this-node-cannot-open-is-refused-whichever-route-reads-it) answers them), or `query_failed` for every other failure (the reason goes to the log, never the socket).
- **`artifact_trashed` is not `not_found`**: it answers a question about the content of a trashed artifact (its datastore) asked by somebody it is disclosed to, the state its owner's restore ends. REST twin: the artifacts routes' `409 artifact_trashed`. A reader with no relation gets `not_found`.
- **`unknown_query` covers a surface this process does not have now**: a question whose source is not wired here is never registered, and a Worklet or Doclet question on a node whose runtime does not run them answers the same. It is unknown rather than empty and never carries a `Retry-After`, because waiting cannot give the node a store it was not configured with. REST twin: `404`. Only a node's FIRST revision on a native backend needs no restart: it builds Worklet and Doclet on a node that ran neither and is answered from then on (see [Worklet and Doclet](#worklet-and-doclet)); a revision that switches a backend after that waits for restart, as [A native backend changes at a restart](../concepts/control-plane.md#a-native-backend-changes-at-a-restart) says.
- **`unavailable` is not `query_failed`**: the node understood the question and cannot answer it *here* (a projection still catching up after a restart or fresh join, an unreachable coordination store, no copy of the estate to answer from, or a state-log refusal). Worklet, Doclet and Chatlet are read through the [estate router](../concepts/scaling.md#how-a-request-reaches-the-estate), so a copy out of service or a restarting data node is a holder to ask again, not a fault. The frame carries `retry_after` (whole seconds before asking this node again), `detail` (a sentence for the reader: what happened and what to do, agreeing with `retry_after`, for every condition including an unanswering coordination store and no data node serving, in the words the act route and work surface use; the refusal's own detail, which names positions and settings, goes to the answering node's log) and, behind a state-log refusal, `refusal` (its code: `behind`, `log_full`, `deferred`, `broker_refused`, ...). **A `retry_after` of `0` is the answer, never an omission**: waiting will not change it (a log at its byte ceiling, a record this node cannot decode, a barrier its broker refused), so ask another node or wait for an operator; see [Read consistency](../guides/consistency.md#the-fifteen-refusals). REST twin: `503` with the same `detail` and `refusal` in the body and `Retry-After` carrying the hint, absent where it is zero.
- **A work, page, chat or search question on a node not yet handed a company** is `unavailable` with `refusal: "no_active_revision"`, Worklet's, Doclet's and Chatlet's one sentence as `detail`, and `retry_after: 15` (the reconcile poll that brings the company). REST twin: `503 no_active_revision` with the same detail and `Retry-After: 15`, as every surface over those halves answers such a node.
- **`bad_params` is not `query_failed` either**, in the opposite direction: the node understood and *refused* the question (a parameter missing, malformed or outside the accepted set), so the fault is the caller's and a retry repeats it. REST twin: `400`. It carries **`detail`**, the refusal's own sentence naming the parameter to change and what it accepts (`days is 91, and a spend window is 1 to 90 company days. Ask for at most 90`), with no class name (not the engine's, nor a finer one such as `tokens.ErrWindowLength`, which a Go caller tests with `errors.Is`) and no echo of the query's name. The REST `400` body carries the same `detail` beside its `error`.
- A frame has ONE `detail` key: `unavailable`'s words, `bad_params`'s sentence or a revision refusal's remedy. Every other code's text stays in the node's log, since a failure's own text can carry a path.
- The dashboard asks again after exactly a frame's `retry_after` (not at all after a `0`) and keeps no wait of its own, so this hint and a REST refusal's `Retry-After` are its only retry clock.

#### Client frames

Client → server kinds:

| `kind` | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `ping` | Keepalive; server replies with `pong`. |
| `watch` | Become a recipient for one seat's seat-routed frames: `{ kind: "watch", seat }`. An empty `seat` clears it (always allowed). One socket watches one seat at a time (a tab looks at one screen), so a second watch replaces the first. **`seat` names a record as `work_inbox`'s `handle` does**: a seat's handle, either of your own names, or somebody's **login**, resolved to the record their notices are kept under (the seat the identity directory binds them to), where the watch is installed because every `inbox_changed` frame for them is pushed to that name. It follows [Whose record a personal question answers for](#whose-record-a-personal-question-answers-for) to the letter, asking the directory only once the watch is decided as far as it can be without it. A login that names nobody answers `not_found` to `admin` and is refused like any other seat to everybody else. **It is decided like `work_inbox` about the same seat**, since it buys that seat's `inbox_changed` frames: the seat's own holder, whoever leads it through the chart, or `admin`, and `worklet` either way. Three answers, none closes the socket. **Allowed** installs the watch. **Refused** installs nothing, drops any watch the socket held, and replies `error` with `unauthorized`; not a `4403` close, because a client reads that as "this browser may not have the live channel at all". **Undecidable** (this node could not read the chart, or the directory a login resolves through) installs nothing and replies `unavailable` with the `retry_after` that says when asking again can change the answer (`0` where no wait will). Installing would hand a seat's frames to somebody this node could not show was allowed them; refusing would tell a lead they lead nobody because the node is behind. **Every time the socket's credential is decided again by an identity record that names it, and on every published company (when a lead can move), the current watch is decided again**: a refusal withdraws it and says so, and an undecidable answer keeps it, since nothing has been learned against a decision already made. A watch with nobody resolved behind it closes the socket with **4401**. |
| `artifact_join` | Enter an artifact's room: `{ kind, id, artifact, since? }`, where `since` is the `through` this tab last held. **Decided like reading the artifact** (`get_artifact`: the owner, a share naming you, your unit or the company, or leading the agent that owns it), three-valued, and no answer closes the socket. **Allowed** answers `result` with `{ artifact, session, role, roster, through, resync }`: your session, your role, the room as this node's sockets were last shown it with you in it (every later `artifact_presence` frame is the difference from that `roster`: replace the room with it, then apply each push), the datastore's version, and `resync: true` when `since` is absent or older than the datastore can account for (read the collections whole), `false` when a catch-up from `since` suffices. **Refused** answers `error` with `not_found` and the `artifact`, in exactly the words an artifact nobody holds gets, or `artifact_trashed` for an artifact disclosed to you and in the trash, whose room carries nothing until its owner restores it. **Undecidable** answers `unavailable` with `retry_after`. A socket is in at most **8** rooms; a ninth is `bad_params`. **The join is decided again** on every decision of the socket's credential and on every share, unshare, trash, transfer or purge of the artifact: a refusal withdraws the room with an `error` frame (`what: "artifact_join"`, `error: "not_found"` or `"artifact_trashed"` for the trash, `artifact`, no `id`) on a socket that stays open, and a role that moved shapes the pushes after it. From the moment such a movement lands until its decision does, the room's `artifact_data` pushes are held back, and a member the decision keeps is sent `resync`. **An undecidable answer fails closed**: the room stays joined (`artifact_changed` and `artifact_presence` keep flowing) but its `artifact_data` pushes stay held back, and the node asks again after a backoff (250 ms, doubling to at most 30 s, or the refusal's own longer wait) until a decision lands, which resumes the room with `resync` or withdraws it. A room is never kept at its pre-withdrawal role on an answer nobody could vouch for. |
| `artifact_leave` | Leave an artifact's room: `{ kind, artifact }`. No answer; leaving a room the socket is not in is not an error. A closing socket leaves every room it was in. |
| `presence` | Say what you are doing in a room: `{ kind, room, … }`, where `room` names the kind of room and so the field that names it. **`room: "artifact"`**: `{ kind, room, artifact, activity, focus }` in an artifact's room you joined with `artifact_join`, where `focus` is `{ version?, region?, collection?, doc?, field? }`. **`room: "chat"`**: `{ kind, room, channel_id, activity, focus? }` for the chat room this tab is looking at, and this frame IS the join: a tab looks at one chat room at a time, so naming a room takes the socket out of its previous one and into the named one once that room's own visibility admits your seat (a room you may not read puts you in nobody's presence and shows you nobody's, with nothing said); an empty `channel_id` leaves. Send `editing` while your person types, re-asserted at least every six seconds, and `viewing` otherwise; `focus.thread` is the thread they type under. A tab re-sends it after every reconnect, since the new socket is in no room. `activity` is `viewing`, `editing` or `idle`. No answer. **Who** is doing it is never the frame's to say: the room shows the seat your credential resolved to. At most **ten a second** per socket, whatever rooms they name; frames past that are dropped, as is a frame naming no kind this build keeps. |
| `query` | Request one thing, answered with exactly one `result` or `error` frame: `{ kind, id, what, params, wait_ms }`; `id` is any client-chosen value echoed back. **`wait_ms` is how long the client waits once it sent the frame** (the dashboard's ten seconds; 90 seconds for a transcript page, `executor_session`, as long as a person's read of a session can take: [two transcripts at a time](#executor-sessions)). Past it the node stops the question, ending any read it started and freeing what it holds, and sends nothing for it. A frame without it is answered for as long as the socket lasts; either is stopped at once by a `query_cancel` naming its `id`. **There is no per-frame credential**: every question is asked as the principal the handshake resolved (and each decision of the credential since), and decided by what it is registered under: the overview's questions for everybody, an app's for that app, admin's for admin, a seat's trail by `audit.seat.read`. Queries run concurrently with each other and with the push stream, so one database read cannot stall a tab's live rows: at most **four** at a time per **socket**, a tab's share of the node's reader pool (whose floor is sized as two full dashboards at four each); a fifth waits on its own socket rather than in the pool the engine's own reads share. |
| `query_cancel` | Give up on a question still in flight: `{ kind, id }`, the `id` its `query` frame named. The node stops it at once, ending any read it started (a transcript page's included) and freeing what it holds, and sends nothing for it. No answer; naming a question already answered, or none, changes nothing. The dashboard sends it for a question a screen stops waiting for (left, or another session chosen). |

#### Queries

Each query (`what`) is answered by the *same* function the matching
REST route calls, so the two surfaces cannot diverge:

| `what` | `params` | Answers with |
|--------|----------|--------------|
| `agent` | `{id, history}` | `GET /agents/{id}`: config, live state and `llm_history`. `history=false` answers the seat and its live state with an empty `llm_history` and no `next`, for a caller asking what a seat is doing rather than what it said: the finished calls' payloads are whole transcripts |
| `live_call` | `{agent_id}` | `GET /query/live_call?agent_id=…`. `{agent_id, handle, live_calls, live_call_seq}`: the seat's calls in flight, one per turn it runs, each with every field and its `versions`, or `live_calls: []` while it has none (a seat the projection has never seen included, at `live_call_seq` 0), and the seat's `live_call_seq` beside it either way, which the tab orders the answer by against the pushes that may overtake it. Asked and answered by the seat's AGENT ID, the key every overlay is merged by, and never by its name, which two seats may share; `handle` is a label. From the projection alone, so it costs what a push does — the REPAIR a tab makes when an `agents` push names a version of a heavy field newer than the copy it holds: the push that carried the field was dropped (see [What the projection carries, and what the wire sends](#what-the-projection-carries-and-what-the-wire-sends)) |
| `agent_memory` | `{id, limit, skills_order}` | `GET /agents/{id}/memory`. A seat's trail, so it takes `audit.seat.read` — the seat's lead, or `admin`. ANSWERED BY THE NODE HOLDING THE SEAT, which it names (`held_by`, or `none` with an empty answer for a seat no node holds; `unavailable` while the holder is silent or still taking the seat) — every node keeps a copy of a seat's memory and only the holder keeps it current. Four collections, each a page (`limit`, at most 50; the episodes, skills and profiles also end at 1 MiB of text each, so a page can be shorter) with its counted total beside it: the diary (`diary_total`), the episodes (`episodes_total`), the synthesized skills (`skills_total`, newest drafted first, or in `skills_order` — `uses`, the most used first, or `updated`, the most recently changed — which the holder applies to the whole set BEFORE it cuts the page, so the page is the top of the set and never the newest page re-sorted; any other value is `bad_params`) and the COUNTERPARTY PROFILES (`counterparties_total`) — what this seat has learned about the colleagues it works with, both instants carried because `last_updated_at` moves on every interaction and `last_corroborated_at` only when the traits changed. `traits` is a bag whose keys the model invents, never a fixed schema. Plus `latest_reflection` (the newest live diary entry, whatever the page) and `onboarded_at`. An episode's `ask` and `plan_summary` are their OPENINGS, at most 600 bytes each — the figure a seat is shown of a past turn's words before they are condensed (`learning.EpisodeAccountBytes`) — with each whole text's size in `ask_bytes` and `plan_summary_bytes`. The diary is keyed on the derived agent id and the other three on the seat's handle; both are resolved from the one identifier a caller has, the handle. See [the route](#get-agentsidmemory) |
| `agent_episode` | `{id, episode}` | `GET /agents/{id}/memory/episodes/{episode}`. A seat's trail, so it takes `audit.seat.read`, as `agent_memory` does. ONE EPISODE WHOLE — what the turn was asked and what it did, complete — answered by the seat's holder as `agent_memory` is (`held_by`); `episode: null` for one the seat no longer holds. See [the route](#get-agentsidmemoryepisodesepisode) |
| `memory_overview` | `{}` | **Decided per seat by `audit.seat.read`**, as `agent_memory` is, and answered for exactly the seats the caller may read — every one for `admin`, a lead's own agents for a lead, none for anybody else; a seat this node cannot decide makes the whole answer `unavailable` rather than a shorter list. Each seat's memory totals — `diary_total`, `episodes_total`, `skills_total`, `last_reflection_at` and the `latest_reflection` itself — each counted by the node holding the seat, gathered in ONE scatter rather than a read per seat, with `held_by` per row (`none` for a seat no node holds, nothing counted), an `unavailable` reason on a row whose holder did not answer, and the fleet `coverage`. The seats the caller may read, handle order, no cap. See [the section](#memory_overview) |
| `executor_sessions` | `{handle, cursor, limit, read_level, …}` | `GET /agents/{id}/sessions`. The seat's EXECUTOR SESSIONS, the latest begun first: a row per turn whose executor captured its harness's session or that read its conversation, naming the sealed object in the fleet's object store that holds the session its harness kept when its run ended — the whole record of what the run read, called and wrote — and how the turn ended. A seat's trail, so it takes `audit.seat.read` — the seat, its lead or `admin`, the verb an executor's tail is decided by — and an absent `handle` is the caller's own seat. Read through the estate router, so any node answers, at the caller's freshness (`read_level`; this surface's own when absent). A page of `limit` rows (25 when absent, 100 at most) with `next_cursor`, the cursor of the page after it, absent on the last; `read_level` and `position` say how it was read, and `complete: false` that the answering copy holds a record of the log it could not read. Each row says which launch would continue it (`continued_by`: `relaunch` while its turn is live, `next_turn` once it has ended, `next_fire` once a fire of a schedule has), whether it would (`continuable`, `null` where that cannot be said now), where (`continues_in`: `any_box` or `parked_box`) and where not, why (`not_continuable`), the session its turn's first launch was handed (`base_turn`), whether it is in progress (`in_progress`: its turn has not ended and its row names a kept session, with the engine's sentence for one, `in_progress_note`) and the engine's note on a session its turn went on past (`kept_note`: kept up to a session its turn went on past, or of a turn that was lost). See [the route](#get-agentsidsessions) |
| `executor_session` | `{handle, turn_id, cursor, read_level, …}` | `GET /agents/{id}/sessions/{turn_id}`. One turn's session and a page of its TRANSCRIPT, its sealed object opened and read as its harness recorded it — entries of `brief`, `note`, `late_call`, `wake`, `model`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `summary` and `unread` — every entry's text redacted at this read. Decided as `executor_sessions` is, and it shows more than the run's live output did: every call's input and each result's text, to an entry's bound. A page holds at most 200 entries and 1 MiB of text, each entry at most 16 KiB, and `cut` says why it ends where it does, `next_cursor` the cursor of the page after it, absent on the last; `read_level`, `position` and `complete` say how the session's row was read. A node decodes at most two transcripts at once, and a question past them waits for a slot, nothing opened, for as long as its caller does. An object the store no longer holds, one that does not open, one that is no archive and one this build does not read are each an answer (`state`) with the engine's sentence (`why`), never a failure. Its first page says of the row whether a launch would continue the session, and a later page leaves `continuable` null. A turn the seat keeps no row of is `not_found`: it recorded none, or its row went with the end of a later turn of its conversation that was handed it, past the retention, or with the seat. A session released while it is read is said as released, from its row read again: `not_found`, or `state: none`, each saying nothing more of it can be read. See [the route](#get-agentsidsessionsturn_id) |
| `event` | `{id}` | `GET /events/{id}` — one event with its full payload, and `node`, the node that published it (every stored event carries it, not only this answer's) |
