| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/pushes` | Its push history, newest first in the order the pushes landed on the code log (never by the instant each record carries, which steps back when the log's leader changes). `?limit=`: 1–200, unset or `0` is 50. `?cursor=`. `?brief=true` reads it **in brief**, as a screen draws it: each push's introduced commits counted (`introduced_count`) and not listed, and a push of more than five commands cut to five (its refused ones first, each with its reason, then the first it sent), the commands left out counted by what became of each in `omitted` (`created`, `moved`, `forced`, `deleted`, `unchanged` and `refused`, each absent at zero; `omitted` itself absent where nothing is left out), so an import's push of a thousand tags is five lines and a count rather than about 140 kilobytes. A page in brief holds no more pushes; it sends less. `?push=<id>` narrows the history to that one push, read whole, and is `400 bad_params` beside `limit`, `cursor` or `brief`; a push the history does not hold (another repository's, or past the 181 days it keeps) is an answer with no row. `?pusher_kind=` (`agent`, `person` or `gitlet`) and `?pusher=` (a seat's handle, or the human seat a person holds; none for `gitlet`) narrow it to one pusher's pushes as [Gitlet § Counting pushes](../concepts/gitlet.md#counting-pushes) counts them; `?since=` and `?until=` (RFC 3339, to the microsecond) to those whose record landed in `[since, until)` ([Gitlet § Narrowing a push history](../concepts/gitlet.md#narrowing-a-push-history)). A narrowed page reads at most 5 000 pushes and 4 MiB of their rows and `limit` is then the pushes it keeps, so it can hold fewer or none beside a `next`, and it answers `push_scan`, whose `to`, beside a `next`, is the instant of the push it ended at. Each is `400 bad_params` with its sentence (an unknown kind, a pusher without its kind, a handle not shaped as a seat's or beside `gitlet`, an instant before 1970 or finer than a microsecond, an `until` not after `since`, beside `push`), as `day_bounds` is beside a pusher or outside the window. Each push names its id and who pushed it: a person's push (`actor_kind` `operator`) the credential it came through (`actor`: `pat:<credential id>` for a machine token, `token:<id>` for a Tier A token, `session:<lineage>` for a signed-in session, as every record a write leaves names it) and the human seat its principal holds (`actor_seat`: a person's own, or the seat the identity directory binds a token to); a seat's push (`actor_kind` `agent`) the seat's handle as both `actor` and `actor_seat`, and the run behind it (`run`: `turn_id` the turn that made it, `work_backend` and `work_key` the work item that turn was charged to and the key its tracker shows, `model` the model it ran on, and for a push the seat's coding box made, `run_id` the launch that pushed (the `launch_id` its `executor_launched` event carries) and `harness` the harness the box ran, such as `claude-code`; each stamped by the engine from the call or run that made the push, never read from a commit, each at most 256 bytes, a longer value cut to its opening beside its length and a digest of the whole; absent from a person's push); the ref lifecycle's push (`actor_kind` `system`) no `actor`, `actor_seat` or `run`: the engine on its own account, each command a deletion whose `old` is the commit to restore the branch at. `via` names how the pack was built: `git`, sent by a client's git (a person's, or a seat's coding box's); `engine`, built by the engine for a code tool's write ([Gitlet § Engine-built commits](../concepts/gitlet.md#engine-built-commits)); `merge`, the move of a branch a change's merge record made, its actor who merged it ([Gitlet § A merge, end to end](../concepts/gitlet.md#a-merge-end-to-end)); `expiry`, the ref lifecycle's deletion of seats' idle branches ([Gitlet § The ref lifecycle](../concepts/gitlet.md#the-ref-lifecycle)); `queue`, a merge queue's landing; `import` and `mirror`, an import's and a pull mirror's sync. A push also names the node that received it, every ref it moved or was refused with the reason, its pack, and the position its record landed at; and `change`, the change its own record merged on a branch it set (`repo`, `ref`, `title`, `state`), a merge's or merge queue landing's before any a push merged beside it, else the lowest-numbered, with `changes_more` counting the others. A push every ref of which a rule refused (an attempt: a protection, the grant, the default branch, a moved tag or a reserved ref) is a row too, with no pack and nothing introduced, and `offered`, how many commits it offered that the repository lacked, where they were counted; a row recorded before the engine kept it carries none. A ref the engine refused for being longer than 255 bytes or not UTF-8 is named in a bounded form: as much as fits in 255 bytes, then its length and a digest of the whole. `?day_bounds=` (as the listing takes them) answers `push_days`, the repository's pushes on each day between two bounds, oldest first, zeros included, whatever the page holds; it is refused beside `push` |
| `GET /gitlet/counts` | A scope's counts, the parts `?parts=` names (comma-separated, at least one: `changes`, `repos` or `queue`). `changes` is `{live, draft, open, closed, merged}`, `live` the draft and open together. `repos` is `{project, scratch}`, each `{live, importing, active, archived, deleted, purging}`, `live` the first three together, every repository the caller may read whatever any filter says, so `repos` beside `?repo=` is `400 bad_params`. `queue` is `{live, more}`, the live entries of the scope's merge queues, counted when read, at most 10 000, `more` where it stopped there. The scope is `?repo=`, one repository whatever its state, or, where it names none, every repository in use the caller may read; a count is never narrowed by a listing's filters. `changes` and `repos` are read from counts the applier keeps, every part at the caller's freshness, so `session` after a write includes it. A data node of a build that does not count a part refuses it unread and another node answers. Refused `404 not_found` (`not_declared`) for a `repo` nothing declares, `400 bad_params` for no part, an unknown part, a `cursor` or a nonzero `limit`, and `403 not_permitted` for a repository the caller may not read, which a person never meets ([Counting changes](../concepts/gitlet.md#counting-changes)) |

Every answer carries the `position` and `level` it was read at. They read at the
REST read path's level (`stale` by default) through the same freshness keys as
every other question: `read_level` (`linearizable`, `stale`,
`consistent_prefix`, or `session` beside a `min_position` on the code log),
`max_lag_seconds`, `max_lag_seq` and `min_position`
([Read Consistency](../guides/consistency.md#which-surface-reads-at-which-level)).
**`session` reads a write back**: a write that lands on the code log answers
with the position its record landed at, and a read naming that position as its
`min_position` at `read_level=session` is answered only once the serving node
holds it, else `503 unavailable` (`behind`) within the read's budget, never
served from before the write. This is how a screen draws the list it just
changed (the dashboard's `SESSION_QUERIES` lists them, [a change's
questions](#a-changes-questions), [a repository's
content](#a-repositorys-content) and the section counts, under the code log). A
bare `session`, naming no position, is `400 bad_params`: it would wait for
nothing. A `min_position` on another log is `400 bad_params` too. A client that
must not conclude a repository is undeclared from an old copy (a script about to
create one) asks `read_level=linearizable`: at `stale`, a repository declared a
moment ago may not have reached this node's copy and is answered `404`.

A refusal is the read surface's:

- `404 not_found` for a repository that is not declared, with `"reason":
  "not_declared"`, and for a company that hosts no code, with `"reason":
  "not_hosted"` — told apart by the `reason`, since they are remedied
  differently: a repository is declared in `code.repos`, and declaring one
  changes nothing until the company sets `code.backend: gitlet`;
- `403 not_permitted` for a repository the caller's grant does not cover, the
  `detail` naming who asked, the repository and why; for a seat a
  `visibility: unit` repository shuts out, that visibility and who among the
  seats does read it ([Visibility](../concepts/gitlet.md#visibility)). A person
  holding the Gitlet permission reads every repository, so is never answered it;
- `403 unauthorized`, `"reason": "no_grant"` and `"grants": ["gitlet"]`, for a
  caller without the Gitlet permission, before any repository is read;
- the guard's own answers for a caller it could not resolve, given before any
  question is asked: `401 invalid_token` for no credential the node accepts, and
  `503 identity_unavailable` with `Retry-After: 2` where this node could not tell
  who it is (it cannot read its identity estate);
- `400 bad_params` naming the parameter or level refused;
- `503 unavailable` with `Retry-After` for what clears by waiting: this node
  behind the code log or a `session` read's floor, no quorum, no data node
  serving the read;
- `500 query_failed` for anything else.

A company that hosts code on a node that serves none of it now (or that has not
read whether it does) is answered `503` under the code the git routes name
above, as the envelope's `error`, with its `message` and a `detail` saying what
this node found: `applying` (`Retry-After: 5`), `config_apply_failed`,
`code_unknown` (the `detail` naming what it could not read) or
`native_backend_needs_restart`, the last three with no `Retry-After`, since
waiting clears none of them and another node serves the read. Over the socket
the same answer is an `unavailable` frame whose `refusal` is that code, with the
same `detail` and `retry_after`. Every one of them is served through a drain.
### A change's questions

A [change](../concepts/gitlet.md#changes) is read through four more
questions, decided per repository as the rows above are, read at the same freshness keys and refused in the same vocabulary. A change of a repository the caller may not read is left out of a listing, and answered `403 not_permitted` alone.

| Route | Question | What it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /gitlet/changes` | `code_changes` | Changes, newest first, a page at a time (`?limit=` 1–200, unset or `0` is 50, and `?cursor=`). It names at least one of: `?repo=` (a repository by name); `?state=` (`draft`, `open`, `closed` or `merged`); `?work=` (a work item, `<backend>:<id>`); `?reviewer=` (changes asking a seat's review, or a person's by the human seat they hold); `?needs=` (`review`, `fix`, `me` or `person`: what its changes wait on; `me` is the changes asking the caller's review, then the caller's own awaiting a fix, a page filling across both, each row naming its half in `waits_for`, `review` or `fix`); `?readiness=` (`ready`, `approval`, `checks` or `blockers`: where the merge stands); `?window=` (`24h`, `7d` or `30d`: changes that moved within that time, newest move first where nothing else leads; a live `?state=`, `draft` or `open`, leads instead, newest opening first, the window tested on each change); or `?text=` (words in the title or description, see the `?text=` paragraph below). `?owner=` narrows further. `?sort=updated` lists a live `?state=` (`draft` or `open`) newest last move first, by `updated_at`; a window nothing else leads is already so. `?sort=opened` is newest opened first, refused on such a window. `sort=updated` beside `?reviewer=` or `?needs=`, or with no live state and no such window, is `400 bad_params`. `?readiness=` lists the open changes whose merge stands in that bucket ([Changes by where their merge stands](../concepts/gitlet.md#changes-by-where-their-merge-stands)), beside any other filter, sort or window; with a `?state=` other than `open` it is `400 bad_params`; every page it narrows carries `narrowed_to`, the bucket, so a page without it came from a node that does not read `?readiness=`. A live state by its last moves steps over merged and closed changes' conversations, at most 1 000 a page, and may answer few rows with a `next`. Each change carries its row, its repository by name, its reference (`web!42`), the caller's `access` to its repository, `open_findings` (findings none of its authors has answered), `updated_at` (the later of its lifecycle's last record and the last thing written about it, never its home's facts) and, while live, its `readiness` judged in the read. A page counts the changes it **scanned**, so it may hold fewer than its limit and still carry a `next`, except a page the index of changes' words leads, which is served full |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/changes/{n}` | `code_change` | One change by number, `?part=` at a time. With no part, or `revisions`: its detail (row; for a closed change `closed_by` and `closed_by_kind`, absent where a push nobody made deleted its source; description; authors; conversation counters with `spoken_at`, when somebody last wrote on it, absent until then and never the home's facts; recorded mergeability; `target_tip`, its target's tip as the read found it, absent where the branch is gone; readiness) on the first page beside its revisions, newest first, each with the facts its home recorded and how its push moved the branch (`via`, and `forced` where it rewrote it: a force-push, or the engine's rebase onto the target). `reviewers`, `comments`, `reviews` and `findings` page that part of the conversation. `queue` pages its queue entries in queue order (each `{entry_id, target_ref, head_oid, method, enqueued_by, state, reason, checks, paths, commit_oid, enqueued_position, enqueued_at, ended_position, ended_at}`: who queued it and how it landed, was ejected or dequeued; kept as long as the queue's history, 30 days after it ended), 50 a page by default, at most 200. `moves` pages the lifecycle's moves, oldest first (each `{kind, by, by_kind, reason, was, became, position, at}`: who closed, reopened, drafted, readied, edited or retargeted it, a close's reason, a retarget's branches from and to, the work item an edit set), 100 a page by default, at most 500. `standing` is the asker's own standing findings (open, or answered by an author) by id: every finding a review of theirs carries or, of a later revision, supersedes, at most 1 024 (`MaxStandingFindings`) a page, none for a credential bound to no seat. `files` is a revision's files and `diff` one file's patch (`?file=`, or `?file_b64=` for a path's exact bytes), or with `?patches=true` every file's patch a page at a time, read from the **base its facts record**, never the target's tip now; or with `?since_revision=`, what changed between that earlier revision and this one, kept to the paths either touches (`kind` `interdiff`). `?revision=` reads at a revision other than the head. `findings` places each finding in that revision: `placed`, by finding id, is where its lines are now (`start`, `end`), `outdated` where its own lines changed, `gone` where the revision holds no file at its path |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/changes/{n}/routing` | `code_change_routing` | Whom the change's records reached: records that reached anybody, newest first, a whole record a page (`?limit=` 1–200, unset or `0` is 50), each with `record_id`, position, instant, `excerpt` and every `recipients` entry: a seat's handle or the human seat a person holds, `kind` (`agent` or `person`), the one `reason` it heard under, `addressed` where it asks something of them, and `fallback` and `fallback_rank` for a substitute reached because nobody better was. `delivery` says what the answer can say: `reached` where it lists a record; `nobody` for a change opened since `retained_from`, whose notices would all still be kept; `swept` for one opened before it, whose notices a sweep was entitled to take. `retained_from` is thirty days back, how long a seat's notice is kept (a person's is kept the company's `inbox.retention_days`, never less), so a record older than it lists only the persons it reached |
| `GET /gitlet/reviews` | `code_reviews` | The reviews one reviewer gave, newest first across the repositories the caller may read (`?reviewer=`, required: a seat's handle or the human seat a person holds; `?limit=` 1–200, unset or `0` is 50; `?cursor=`), each naming the change it judged: repository, reference, title and state. A page counts the reviews it **read**, so it may hold fewer than its limit and still carry a `next` |

`?cards=true` on `GET /gitlet/changes` answers each listed change's `card`:
`comments`, `reviews` and `changes_requested`; `reviewers` (at most 8, each
`handle`, `kind`, `verdict`, `verdict_revision`, `asked`, `reason`,
`owned_paths` and `owned_paths_omitted`) and
`reviewers_omitted`; `checks`, a check rollup of its head for its target
(`state`, `counts`, `required`, `required_passed`, `last_ended`,
`running_since`, `failing`, `failing_more`, `more`), absent where no attempt is
kept; and `ejected` (`reason`, `at`, `checks`, `checks_more`, and `tested_in`
where its checks failed on a train) where a live change's newest queue entry
was put out in the last day. An older data node refuses `cards` and another
answers; a card never reads as zeros where it was not answered. `cards=` other
than `true` or `false` is `400 bad_params`, and `cards=true` on any other
question is refused naming it.

`?text=` on `GET /gitlet/changes` narrows the listing to the changes in whose
title or description every word of it appears (a word is two or more letters
or digits, case folded, no stemming; at most 8 words and 400 bytes,
`400 bad_params` past either or with no word), in the order the listing reads
without it, never ranked. Words alone name a listing, newest opened first.
With no `?reviewer=`, `?needs=`, `?work=` or `?readiness=`, the answering data
node's index of changes' words leads: it reads the newest 5 000 changes of
the narrowest of the listing's repository, owner, state and rarest word, keeps
the newest 1 000 holding every word, and judges each in the read beside every
change moved since the index last caught up, so pages are full; newest is when
each change's open was asked (the instant its id carries, the same on every node). Beside a
reviewer, a need, a work item or a readiness bucket, that walk leads and the
words are judged on each change it read. Every page it narrows carries
`changes_text`, `{}` where the search was whole: `truncated`, more changes may
hold the words than one search reads; `indexed_back_to`, an instant, the index
is still being built newest first and has reached back to the changes opened
then, so one opened at or before it may be missing; `building`, the index was
behind its rows, so a change holding them may be missing. None says that no
change does. A page without `changes_text` came from a node that does not read
`?text=`, and is the listing unnarrowed. Across repositories a deleted
repository's changes count toward both bounds until its purge
([Searching changes by their words](../concepts/gitlet.md#searching-changes-by-their-words)).

Each reviewer row of `?part=reviewers` carries `owned_paths` where a
revision's facts asked the reviewer as a path owner: the globs of every owner
resolving to them that the revision touched, sorted, at most 32 and 1 KiB, and
`owned_paths_omitted`, how many more. An ask by name carries none, and asking a
path owner again by name drops them. A card's face carries the same where that
ask waits, was answered by their review or ended with the change. Each
revision's `facts` carry `measured_at`, when its home read them by its own
clock, to the microsecond. Facts and asks recorded before this build carry
none of these, nor does an older data node's answer.

`?part=finding_paths` on `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/changes/{n}` answers
`finding_paths`: the change's findings counted by `path`, `state` and
`revision` (`findings`), in that order (`?limit=` 1 to 1 000, unset or `0` is
500, and `?cursor=`); `revision` and `file` beside it are `400 bad_params`. An
older data node refuses it and another answers. The detail carries
`participants` (`rows` of `handle`, `kind`, `verdict` and `verdict_revision`,
at most 32, and `omitted`), each reviewer row `at`, when the record that last
moved it landed (absent past the notices' horizon), and each finding
`raised_at`, when the review that raised it landed. A merged change's detail
carries `reverted_by` (`repo`, `ref`, `title` and `state`), the latest change
`code_revert_change` opened to revert it, absent where none was.

`?part=viewed` on `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/changes/{n}` answers `viewed`: the
files the asker marked viewed with `code_mark_viewed`, in `path_digest` order,
each with `path_digest`, `file_digest` and `at`, and beside a page that holds
one, `viewed_key`, the repository's key in lowercase hex (`?limit=` 1 to
1 000, unset or `0` is 500, and `?cursor=`, a digest). `path_digest` is the
HMAC-SHA256 under the key of the path's UTF-8 bytes, and `file_digest` that of
the path, a NUL byte, the object id, a NUL byte and the mode the mark was made
at (both empty for a file the change deletes), each in lowercase hex. A mark is
current while the revision shown gives the file a `file_digest` equal to the
mark's. A person's own alone: a seat or a credential bound to no seat is
answered none, and so is a change that is closed or merged; a read Ask Crewlet
makes for a person is answered the marks without the key. `revision`, `file`
or `context` beside it is `400 bad_params`. An older data node refuses it and
another answers.

A part read by object id (`files`, `diff`, and `findings`' placing) reads the
change's rows at the caller's freshness, every other row at `session` floored
at that first read's position, and asks the home Gitlet node at the floor of
the records that moved the revisions it reads, so no answer is from an older
copy than the first read saw. A change's question adds these refusals to the code reads':

- `404 not_found` with `"reason": "no_change"` for a number the repository
  holds no change of, and `"reason": "no_revision"` for a revision the change
  does not have;
- `404 not_found` with `"reason": "unrecorded"` for a revision of a change that
  was merged or closed before its home recorded its facts, so it has no base to
  read its files from, and `"reason": "unrelated"` for one whose head shares no
  history with its target (its change is every file of its head);
- `404 not_found` with `"reason": "no_object"` for a `file` the revision does
  not hold, or an object its repository's home Gitlet node holds no object of,
  in the Gitlet node's own sentence;
- `503 unavailable` for a revision of a live change whose facts its home has
  not recorded yet (within a minute of the push), and for a read
  by object id no Gitlet node holding the repository could answer in time;
- `400 bad_params` for a parameter its part does not take: a `revision` to the
  revisions, a `file` to `files`, a `since_revision` that is not earlier, a
  `diff` naming neither a file nor `patches`, or both, `patches` on another
  part.

`?part=excerpts` pages the change's findings as `findings` does and answers
`excerpts`, each finding's [excerpt](../concepts/gitlet.md#findings) by its
id, read at the finding's own revision: `status` (`A`, `D`, `M` or `R` as the
revision changes the file, absent for one it leaves as it was), `binary`,
`lines` (each `mark`, `" "`, `"+"` or `"-"`, its `old` and `new` numbers, and
`text`, or `text_bytes` where the line is longer than an excerpt shows) and
`more` where the window held more than 40 lines. It also answers `context`,
the lines shown either side of each range (`?context=` 0 to 10, 3 when unset),
and the findings page's `next`. A finding whose revision's facts its home has
not recorded has no excerpt. `context` on another part is `400 bad_params`. An
older Gitlet node refuses the read and another answers.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CREWLET_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://crewlet.example.com/gitlet/changes?repo=web&state=open"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CREWLET_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://crewlet.example.com/gitlet/repos/web/changes/42?part=diff&since_revision=2&file=upload/retry.go"
```

These questions only read. A change is opened, edited, closed, reviewed,
discussed and answered through the code tools: a seat's, or a person's on
[`/operator/act` and `/operator/mcp`](#operatormcp--your-own-assistant), each
made as the human seat they hold. Every record those writes leave tells the
seats and people it concerns: a seat is woken, and a person's notice is
read through the composed [`inbox`](#queries) question and marked with
`code_mark_inbox` ([Who a change wakes](../concepts/gitlet.md#who-a-change-wakes)).
A change's files are marked viewed with `code_mark_viewed`
([Viewed files](../concepts/gitlet.md#viewed-files)).
The steps a person takes are [Review a
change](../guides/gitlet.md#review-a-change).

### A repository's content

A repository's refs, files, history and diffs are eleven more questions,
decided per repository as the rows above are and refused in the same
vocabulary. All but `code_refs` and `code_tags` read the repository's
**content**, which its home Gitlet node answers by object id; `code_tags` lists
the tags its copy holds at the repository's own last record. They are the reads a seat's
[code tools](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#the-companys-code) make, one
implementation:

| Route | Question | What it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/refs` | `code_refs` | Live refs under `?prefix=` (`refs/heads/`, the default, `refs/tags/`, or a directory of either ending in `/`), by name, a page at a time (`?limit=` 1–1000, unset or `0` is 200, and `?cursor=`); the first page carries the repository in detail too. `?order=moved` lists branches by last move, newest first (`refs/heads/` only), `?moved_since=` and `?moved_before=` (RFC 3339) keeping those whose last move is in that window. `?contains=` keeps the refs whose name below the prefix holds it in any case; a page reads at most 10 000 refs and answers `next` however few it kept. `?detail=true` answers `refs_detail` in place of `refs`: each ref's `moved_at`, `moved_by` (the push that set it: `push_id`, `actor`, `actor_kind`, `actor_seat`, `via`; absent past the push history's 181 days, or where one record moved it there twice), `protection` (the matching rules' `patterns` and what they allow together), a branch's `change` (`number`, `title`, `state`: its live change, else its newest) and `may_delete`, or `delete_refusal` with `delete_detail`. `?active_since=` on a first page answers `active_branches` (`count`, and `more` past 1 000): the branches other than the default that moved since |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/tree` | `code_tree` | A directory's entries at `?ref=`: its root, or `?path=` (`?path_b64=` for a path's exact bytes); or, with `?recursive=true`, every file below it, a page at a time (`?cursor=`) |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/find` | `code_find` | The files of `?ref=`'s tree whose path holds `?q=`'s characters in order, in any case (each character one of the path's, a space too; at most 256 bytes): `matches`, best first, each its `path` (`path_b64` beside it where it is not UTF-8), `oid`, `mode` and `spans`, the runs of matched characters as `[start, end)` code points. A file whose name holds the query ranks before one whose directories do, then the closer the characters, the earlier and the shorter the name. `?limit=` (1–100, unset or `0` is 50) bounds them, and fewer are answered where their paths fill one answer; `total` is how many files match and `files` how many the tree holds. One answer, no next page: type on to narrow it. A link is a file; a submodule is not, nor is a path past 4 KiB |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/blob` | `code_blob` | A file's lines at `?ref=` and `?path=`, `?start_line=` to `?end_line=`, a page at a time; `?ref=` a blob's own id with no path reads that blob, and a path naming a directory answers its listing |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/log` | `code_log` | The commits that changed `?path=` (or every commit) newest first from `?ref=`, each with parents, author, committer, `engine_committed` where that is the engine's convention, its two dates and its subject. `?limit=` a page (1–100, unset or `0` is 25); `?grep=` a literal the message must hold; `?since=` (RFC 3339) the oldest commit date kept; `?until=` (RFC 3339) the instant every commit kept is before (an `until` not after `since` is `bad_params`); `?pushed_by=` a seat's handle, keeping the commits a push by it brought, with `unjudged` the commits the node's index of pushes could not judge. A history narrowed by `pushed_by` is never immutable |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/blame` | `code_blame` | Which commit last changed each line of the file `?path=` at `?ref=`, `?start_line=` to `?end_line=` (at most 500 lines a read), a page at a time |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/tree-commits` | `code_tree_commits` | The commit that last changed each entry of the directory `?path=` (`?path_b64=`; the root where it names none) at `?ref=`, as `git log -1 -- <entry>` names it: `entries`, each its `path` (`path_b64` beside it where it is not UTF-8) and `commit`; `commits`, each commit they name once as `code_log` lists it; and `total`, the directory's entries. A page begins at `?cursor=`, code_tree's own (`e:<n>`, the listing's n-th entry), so the column fills beside the listing; it holds up to a hundred entries, fewer where their commits fill one answer, and its `next` goes on. An entry with no `commit` is a directory that holds no file and never did along its history, which git names no commit for, or, marked `out_of_time`, the first entry of a page whose read ran out of time before finding it: the page ends after it. A page whose read ran out of time is marked `out_of_time` itself, ends where its `next` says, and is answered bare |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/diff` | `code_diff` | What changed from `?base=` to `?head=` (both required): the per-file stat, narrowed to `?paths=` (repeated, at most 64); or one `?file=`'s patch (`?file_b64=`); or, with `?patches=true`, every file's patch in the stat's order (`patches`: `file`, `path`, `status`, `patch`, `continues`, and `rest_omitted` where the patch stops before a line longer than one answer holds), narrowed by `?paths=`, with the stat's totals and an empty `files`. Renames are detected unless `?renames=false`; a page at a time |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/tips` | `code_tips` | Up to 100 objects named by their **whole** ids in `?oids=` (comma-separated), a page of them in that order: each one's `type`, what it peels to (`peeled`, `peeled_type`), for an annotated tag its `tag` (`tagger`, `tagger_email`, `tagged_at`, `subject`, each described by its size past its bound as a history's fields are), and for one that is or names a commit that `commit` as `code_log` lists it. With `?base=` (any revision: a branch, `HEAD` for the default branch, or an id), each commit's `behind` and `ahead`: the commits the base has that it lacks and the reverse. A page whose read ran out of time counting ends early with a `next`; its first tip, where that is the one it ran out on, is answered with `counts_out_of_time` and no counts. Immutable where `base` is a whole id or absent |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/tags` | `code_tags` | The repository's tags as its home Gitlet node's copy holds them at the repository's own last record or later, so every tag its row counts, newest first by their own date (an annotated tag's tagger date, a lightweight tag's commit's committer date: git's `creatordate`), by name where two share a date; a tag with no date (a lightweight tag of a tree or a blob, an annotated tag naming no tagger) is dated at the epoch, after every later tag. `?limit=` a page (1–100, unset or `0` is 25) and `?cursor=`. Each is its whole `ref`, its `oid` and that object's `type` (`tag` for an annotated tag), what it peels to (`peeled`, `peeled_type`) and its `date`, or `date_unix`, its seconds, for a date past the year 9999; `total` counts every tag. The first row of the first page is the newest. Never immutable: it carries the answering copy's `position` |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/compare` | `code_compare` | How `?base=` and `?head=` relate: their merge base, which contains which, how many commits each has that the other lacks, the first page of what head changed since the merge base; and `preview`, what merging head into base would do as the repository's home merges it: `state` `clean`, `conflict` (`conflicts` the paths, `conflicts_omitted` how many more) or `unknown`, a merge its home could not decide in a read's time. It is the same merge a change's [mergeability](../concepts/gitlet.md#mergeability) is recorded by. Where one commit contains the other (a fast-forward, or a head base already holds) the merge is `clean`, answered from the comparison with no merge asked of the home |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/commits/{sha}` | `code_commit` | One commit by its **whole** id as `code_log` lists it, with `pushed_by`, the push that introduced it where the Gitlet node's index names one; `push`, that push's row whole (who pushed it, the run behind a seat's push, every ref it moved) where the push history still holds it; `tagged`, the tags naming it, read at the repository's own last record or later; and the changes it belongs to: `merged`, each change whose merge it is, and `revisions`, each revision it heads (`revision 2 of web!42`), at most 50 of each, `more` set where either holds more. Each change carries how it landed once merged (`merge_oid`, `merged_at`, `merged_via`, `merged_by` with `merged_by_kind`, and `override_reason`, a person's reason for merging past its gate) and, for one merged through its gate (`direct` or `queue`), `gate`: `approvals` of the revision it merged at (each `{handle, kind, revision}`, at most 8, `approvals_more` past them), `checks_on`, the commit its gate's checks ran on (a direct merge's head, or the tip a queue's landing left the branch at, which an entry inside a train shares with the train's last), `checks`, their rollup as `code_commit_marks` answers one, and `gone` where none of those rows is kept and the merged revision was pushed over 30 days ago, past which they are swept |

A revision (`?ref=`, `?base=`, `?head=`) is a commit's id, whole or its
first 7 or more hex digits, or a branch, a tag, a whole ref, or `HEAD` for the
default branch (the default where `ref` is not given); a branch whose name is
all hex digits is named by its whole ref. Every ref a request names is
resolved in one read at the caller's freshness (`HEAD` too, the default
branch read from the repository in that same read, so a question at the
default branch costs no more than one naming a branch), and the home Gitlet node is asked
at the position of the record that last moved each, so its copy holds what
the ref named.

**A question every revision of which is a whole id never changes**, and says
so to a request that names who it is for (a bearer, or the dashboard's
`X-Crewlet-Reader`): it is answered with a strong `ETag` and `Cache-Control: private,
max-age=31536000, immutable`, and `304 Not Modified` to a request naming that
tag in `If-None-Match`. A request that names nobody, a tab's cookie
alone, is answered the same page with `Cache-Control: no-store`, since a kept
answer would be shared by everybody who signs in on that browser and not every
person reads code ([Security headers on every
response](#security-headers-on-every-response)). Such an answer is the page alone (the
repository by the name asked, the `kind`, the `rev` read, the `next` cursor and
the kind's own part), cut the same on every Gitlet node. A question naming a
ref or an abbreviation is answered bare, without the tag, since what it names
can move, and carries beside the page: `resolved`, each ref by the parameter
that named it (whole name, commit, where it last moved); the answering copy's
`position`; `pushed_by`, the push that introduced each commit the page names,
with `coverage`, what the node's index of pushes holds; and on a history's
page `tagged`, the tags naming each commit (at most 8 a commit, newest first,
`more` past them), absent where the node keeps no readable tag index, which
says nothing of any commit's tags. Also answered bare: a comparison whose
merge preview is `unknown`, a page of `code_tree_commits` marked `out_of_time`,
a history narrowed by `pushed_by` (it reads the node's index of pushes), and
every `code_commit` (its changes and push move).

A content question adds these refusals to the code reads':

- `404 not_found` with `"reason": "no_ref"` for a ref the repository holds no
  live ref of, every one named, and `"reason": "no_object"` for an object id
  the repository holds no object of, or a path the revision holds no such
  directory or file at;
- `400 bad_params` for a revision that names nothing, a `code_commit` `sha`
  that is not a whole commit id (an abbreviation is expanded by `code_log`
  with it as `ref` and `limit=1`), a read too large to answer whole — narrow
  it — a `code_find` with no `q`, one past 256 bytes, not UTF-8 or holding a
  NUL, or a `limit` past 100, and a parameter the read does not take;
- `503 unavailable` where no Gitlet node holding the repository could answer
  in time, which is never an answer about the repository.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CREWLET_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://crewlet.example.com/gitlet/repos/web/tree?ref=main&path=upload"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CREWLET_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://crewlet.example.com/gitlet/repos/web/compare?base=main&head=feature/retry"
```

### Merge queues and checks

What a repository's merge queues hold and what its checks measured are five
more questions, decided per repository as the rows above are and refused in
the same vocabulary: a listing across repositories keeps the rows of those the
caller reads, and a read naming one repository the caller's grant shuts out is
`403 not_permitted`, however narrowly it asks. Each reads at the caller's
freshness, so a screen reads its own merge, enqueue or re-run back at the code
log's floor (`read_level=session&min_position=…`):

| Route | Question | What it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /gitlet/queue` | `code_queue` | The live entries of merge queues (waiting or testing) in queue order: `?repo=`'s, one of its branches' with `?target=` (a whole ref, `refs/heads/main`), or every repository's the caller reads where it names none. Beside them `trains`, the candidates of the trains testing the targets the page reaches, and, on a named repository's first page, `ejected`: the entries its queues (its `?target=`'s alone, where it names one) put out in the last day, newest first, at most 50, each the change by its `number`, who enqueued it, why (`reason`: `check_failed`, `checks_undefined`, its branch's checks file defining a required check in no form that runs, `conflict`, `gate_unmet`, `head_moved`, `not_fast_forward` or `repo_mirrored`, its repository a pull mirror), the required `checks` that failed on what it was tested in or that no checks file defines, or the `paths` its merge conflicted on, `tested_in` for a failed check's culprit (`candidate_id`, `base_oid`, the commit the candidate was merged onto, the branch's tip for a train's first, and `commit_oid`, where the checks failed: its run is `code_check` at that commit for `target_ref`), and `ejected_at`. Every entry and every ejection names its change's `title` and `source_ref`, and every ejection how it was to land, `method`, `delete_source` and `close_task`, which is what a re-queue sends. `?trains=true` answers, naming no repository, the trains of the targets the page reaches and the ejections of every repository the caller reads, and on any first page `ejected_total`, `{total, more}`: every ejection of the last day the read covers, counted up to 10 000, `more` where it stopped there, and then the rows are of the ejections counted; unset or `false` leaves them out, anything else is `400 bad_params`, and so is `trains` on any other question. A page at a time (`?limit=` 1–200, unset or `0` is 50, and `?cursor=`) |
| `GET /gitlet/checks` | `code_checks` | Attempts of checks, in one of these shapes. A repository's (`?repo=`): newest ended first, every attempt not yet ended after them. A change's (`?change=` its number: its head's attempts, checked for its target) or a commit's (`?oid=`, a whole id: checked for every branch, for the change's target beside `?change=`, or for one branch beside `?target=`, in full: `refs/heads/main`). `?latest=true` beside a change or a commit answers each check's **latest attempt** alone, one row a check and a branch (what each check stands at, which a merge gate reads), at up to 64 a page where `?limit=` is unset, every check one checks file declares, so a change's head's checks are one read; a repository's listing and the window refuse it, `bad_params`, since they walk endings in time. The **window**, naming no repository: every repository's the caller reads whose attempts ended at or after `?since=` (RFC 3339; unset, the thirty days an attempt's rows are kept) and before `?until=` (RFC 3339, after `?since=`; unset, up to the newest ending), newest ended first; a window over a past interval is read from its end down, so its first page is that interval's newest attempts however many ended after it; a repository's listing refuses both bounds. Every shape narrows by `?name=`, a check's name, and `?state=` (`queued`, `running`, `passed`, `failed`, `errored`, `cancelled`, `skipped`; the window, which lists the attempts that ended, takes the last five alone unless it lists where checks stand). `?standing=recent` or `?standing=failing` lists where each check stands instead: each check's latest attempt for a branch, of a live change's head, a live change's newest queue entry or a protected branch's tip, attempts not yet ended included, beside `?repo=` or across every repository, within `?since=` (refused with `?until=`, `?change=`, `?oid=`, `?target=` or `?latest=`), narrowed by `?name=` and by `?state=`, any of the seven, `queued` and `running` in the window too. `recent` lists what runs and waits first, then the endings newest first; `failing` the failures, errors, running, queued, cancelled, passed and skipped, each newest ended first. Each row names the change it judges (`change`, `source_ref`, `change_head`), and a first page counts the attempts by state (`standing_counts`, a state in `at_least` counted to its bound of 128), narrowed by `?name=` and never by `?state=`. Every row names its repository twice, `repo_id` and `repo`, its name, which every link to it takes; the window's too. A page at a time (`?limit=` 1–200, unset or `0` is 50, 64 beside `?latest=true`, and `?cursor=`) |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/checks/{oid}/{check}/{attempt}` | `code_check` | One attempt whole: its row, the definition it ran under, its tail, the failures its ending named (`path`, `line`, `test_id`, `message`) and `log`, the object a failed run's log is kept as, with its `size`; `tests` (`total`, `failed`, `skipped`) where its JUnit report was read; and where its output's lines were counted `log_lines`, its whole output's lines, `tail_first_line`, the number of the tail's first line in it, and `tail_cut` where that line began before the tail, each absent where not counted. `?target=`, the branch it was checked for, is **required**: one commit is checked for every branch a change heading it merges into, and a ref's slashes are no path segment's |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/checks/{oid}/{check}/{attempt}/log` | `code_check_log` | A page of that log: `?offset=` (bytes from its start, `0` unset) and `?limit=` (1–262144 bytes, unset the most), answering `object`, `size`, `offset`, `text` and `next`, where the next page starts, absent on the page that reaches the end. A page never ends inside a character: it ends before it, and `next` starts on it. Its tail, where a failure is printed, is one read from `size` back. `?target=` is required, as above |
| `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/commit-marks` | `code_commit_marks` | What a history page draws beside each of up to 100 commits named by their **whole** ids in `?commits=` (comma-separated), in that order: `checks`, for each branch the commit was checked for (at most 4, `checks_more` past them), each check's latest attempt rolled up: `state` (`failing`, `running`, `pending`, `cancelled` or `passed`, the first that holds), `counts` by state, `required` and `required_passed`, `last_ended`, `running_since` and the `failing` checks by name, required first (at most 8, `failing_more` past them); `merged`, each change whose merge commit it is, and `heads`, each revision it heads (`{change, n}`), at most 4 of each (`more` past them), every change with `merge_oid`, `merged_at`, `merged_via` and `merged_by` (`merged_by_kind` beside it) once merged. Read from the rows alone, at the caller's freshness: a check's rows are kept 30 days after it ended, so an older commit carries no `checks`, which says nothing about whether it was checked |

**A narrowing is sought, never filtered out of a page.** A repository's
listing and the window seek an index that leads with the state, or with the
check's name and then the state, so a narrowed page holds as many of the
attempts the narrowing names as follow its place, whatever ended around them: `?repo=web&state=running` answers what runs now on its first page,
however many attempts ended in the thirty days kept. A change's and a commit's
listings test it while walking that commit's attempts, which their shape
bounds. What still makes a page short is the caller's grant: the window keeps
only the repositories the caller reads, so its page may be short, or empty with
a `next`: follow it until it is absent.

**A log page is immutable by its object, never by its attempt.** Asked with
`?object=` (the key `code_check` answers as `log.object`) the page is
answered with a strong `ETag` and cached for good, to a request that names its
reader, as a [read by whole object ids](#a-repositorys-content) is: an object's key is
minted for one upload and never reused. Asked without it, the page is answered
bare: an attempt's ending can be replaced by a later one (a runner declared
lost that was only slow), and the ending it keeps keeps its own log.

The check questions add these refusals to the code reads':

- `404 not_found` with `"reason": "no_check"` for an attempt the repository
  holds no row of (never queued, or past the thirty days an ended attempt's
  rows are kept) and `"reason": "no_log"` for an attempt that kept no log
  (only a failed run keeps one), or no longer the `?object=` asked for, the
  sentence naming the one it keeps;
- `400 bad_params` for an attempt that names no `target`, an `attempt` that is
  not a whole number from 1, a `state` that is no check's (or, on the window,
  that is not an ending: `queued` or `running`), a `since` that is no
  instant, a log `limit` past one page or an `offset` past the log's end, an
  `object` that is no object's key, and a narrowing the shape does not take
  (a `since` beside a repository, a `change` or an `oid` with none);
- `400 bad_params` for `code_commit_marks` naming no commit, more than 100,
  one twice, or one that is not a whole id, or a `limit` or `cursor`.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CREWLET_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://crewlet.example.com/gitlet/checks?since=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z&state=failed"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CREWLET_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://crewlet.example.com/gitlet/repos/web/checks/4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904/unit/1/log?target=refs/heads/main"
```

### `GET /gitlet/search`

The question `code_search`: matching lines across every `search: indexed`
repository the caller may read, or the repositories its `repo:` filters name,
answered by the one scatter over the Gitlet nodes ([Code
search](../concepts/gitlet.md#code-search)). A repository the caller may not
read is left out of an unfiltered search; a `repo:` naming one is `403 not_permitted`.

| Parameter | What it is |
|---|---|
| `q` | **Required.** The search as a person writes it ([Finding code](../guides/gitlet.md#finding-code)): `repo:<name>`, `path:<pattern>` and `ref:<ref>` filters first, then the text, at most 400 bytes |
| `mode` | `literal` (unset), `regex` (RE2, one line at a time) or `word` (not inside a longer word) |
| `ignore_case` | `true` folds case; `false` or unset does not |
| `repo`, `path`, `ref` | One more filter each beside those in `q`: a repository or path widens the search; a `ref` beside a different `ref:` is refused, as two `ref:` filters are |
| `limit` | Most lines, 1–500; unset or `0` is 500 |
| `context` | Lines of the file each side of a line, 0 to 3; unset or `0` is none. With it, `limit` is at most 100, and unset is 100 |
| `per_file` | Most lines per file, 1 to 500; unset or `0` is every line. With it, each line names `file_matches`, how many lines of its file matched |
| `read_level` | Level the caller's repositories are listed at: `stale` (unset), `linearizable` or `consistent_prefix`, with `max_lag_seconds` and `max_lag_seq` beside `stale` |

The answer is `hits` in repository, path, line order. Each has `repo`, `path`
(`path_b64` beside it for non-UTF-8 bytes), `line`, `text` (at most 256 bytes),
`blob` (the file's object id) and `matches` (byte offsets `[start, end)` in
`text`, at most 32). With `context`: `before` and `after`, the surrounding
lines, a line another answered line carries not repeated. With `per_file`:
`file_matches`. Beside `hits`:

- `tips`: the commit each repository with a hit was searched at, by name.
- `coverage`: `searched`, `building`, `stale`, `not_answering`,
  `not_permitted`, `no_ref`, `past_limit`, `grep_not_named`, `not_indexed`,
  `skipped_files` and `truncated`, as [Code
  search](../concepts/gitlet.md#code-search) tells each.

An empty `hits` says only that nothing matched in the repositories counted under
`searched`: every set beside it but `not_indexed` names repositories not read,
and `skipped_files` counts files passed over.

**It answers at the tip it names, so it takes no floor.** Each repository is
searched at the commit its answering Gitlet node holds for the ref (`tips`), and
a hit's file is read at that commit by id ([`code_blob`](#a-repositorys-content)).
So `read_level=session` and `min_position` are refused `400 bad_params`. A
repository declared a moment ago is listed for an unfiltered search at
`read_level=linearizable`.

Refusals are the code reads' ([above](#the-code-reads)), plus `400 bad_params`
for: a `q` that is missing, past 400 bytes, without a run of three characters to
look up, or whose expression does not compile; a `mode` that is none of the
three; a `limit` past 500; a `context` past 3; a `per_file` past 500; a `limit`
past 100 beside `context`; more than eight `search: grep` repositories. A `repo:`
naming a repository that nobody declared is `404 not_found` with `"reason": "not_declared"`, naming it.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CREWLET_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://crewlet.example.com/gitlet/search?q=repo:billing%20path:src/**/*.go%20retryBudget&ignore_case=true"
```

### `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/readers`

Who read a `visibility: unit` repository's **contents** over a range of company
days: every clone and fetch whose answer carried a pack, and every server-side
read that answered (a seat's code tools or a person's assistant), summed over
every node and day, one row per reader (a credential and the human seat it acted
as, or a seat, and how it read). What counts and how it is kept: [Who read
it](../concepts/gitlet.md#who-read-it). It is the query `code_repo_readers`,
also `GET /query/code_repo_readers?name=…` and the socket's query channel
([Queries](#queries)), one implementation; the operator tool `code_repo_readers`
answers the same pages.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `from`, `to` | Company days on the company's clock, `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive: the thirty ending today where neither is named, the thirty ending at `to` where only `to` is, at most 181 days apart (the days the records keep) |
| `cursor` | The `next` of the page before; left out for the first page |

**Admin only** (`code_repo_readers`, the operator tool's own verb): any other
caller is refused `403 unauthorized` naming `admin` before anything is read. The
answer names people and credentials, so no repository's grant gives it.

A unit's repository answers `200`:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `repo` | The repository's name |
| `recorded` | `true` |
| `from`, `to` | The range read |
| `readers` | The page's readers, ordered by `principal_kind`, `principal`, `via` and `seat`: `principal_kind` (`operator` for a credential, `agent` for a seat), `principal` (the credential's login `pat:<credential id>`, `session:<lineage>` or `token:<id>`, or the seat's handle), `seat` (the human seat a credential acted as, or the seat's own handle; absent for a credential bound to nobody), `via` (`git` or `tool`), `reads`, `bytes` (sent to the reader) and `last_at` (newest read). Present, and empty, where nobody read it in the range |
| `readers_elided` | First page only: readers the per-day cap left out (one node's day names at most 1 024); `0` where complete |
| `next` | Cursor of the next page, absent on the last |

A page holds at most 32 KiB of readers. A `visibility: company` repository's
readers are not recorded: it answers `200` with `"recorded": false` and a
`detail` saying so and how to have them recorded.

The repository is read by name as the caller at `linearizable`, so one declared
a moment ago is never answered undeclared. The readers come from the usage log,
which takes none of the freshness keys above, so the answer carries no
`position`. Refusals are the code reads': `404 not_found` for a repository nobody
declared and for a company that hosts no code, `503` for a node that serves none
of Gitlet now and for a usage log no data node serves, and `400 bad_params`
naming what to change for a range or cursor the read cannot take.

### `POST /gitlet/repos/{name}/verify`

Begins a check of **this node's** copy of one repository against its rows: every
pack against the bytes its row names, the refs against what was written, and
git's connectivity check. With `?repair=true` it also repairs what it finds, then
checks the copy again. The repair is **in place** where everything found is the
copy's own directory out of place (a file the engine does not write there, a
fixed file edited or replaced by a link, a pack no row names, a shape the node
refuses to run git in), keeping every pack and index and downloading nothing;
otherwise, or for what that leaves, a **rebuild** (every pack found whole is
linked, not downloaded again). `repair` is `true` or `false`; anything else is
`400 bad_params`.

Before checking, the node brings its copy to the **log's head**, which appends a
barrier to the code log; with `min_position` it brings it to that position on
the code log (a code read's `position`) with no barrier, and a copy already
there is checked as it is. A sweep of many repositories reads its listing at
`read_level=linearizable` once and names that position on every verify, costing
the code log one barrier, not one a repository. A position that does not parse,
or one on another log (alone or repeated beside the code log's own: a verify
reads the code log alone) is `400 bad_params`.

**It is the one `/gitlet/` route whose work grows with the repository**: it reads
every byte of the copy, about nine seconds a gigabyte (git's connectivity check
nearly all of it), about twice that with a repair, which outlives any proxy's
read timeout. So the check runs on the node's own time (the request ending, or a
proxy closing it, ends nothing) and the request waits **a quarter of a second at
most**. A check that ends within it (a copy up to some 25 MiB) is answered
**`200`** with the report; one still running is **`202 Accepted`**, with its
address in `Location`. Read the outcome there (below).

```json
{ "id": "0190d2f2-…", "repo": "web", "repair": false, "state": "running",
  "started": "2026-10-14T21:30:00Z" }
```

Refused at once, having read nothing, so a retry costs nothing:

- `404 not_found` for a repository that is not declared (`"reason":
  "not_declared"`, its `detail` naming `code.repos`), for a company that hosts
  no code (`"reason": "not_hosted"`, as on the reads), and for one **this node
  holds no copy of**, which carries `"reason": "not_held"`. A Gitlet node keeps
  a copy only of repositories it has served and not evicted; building one to
  check would download the whole repository and evict a warm one. Verify the
  Gitlet nodes that serve it (with requests routed by repository, one or two).
  The `reason` separates the cases because a sweep of every repository on one
  node treats them oppositely: a repository the node does not keep is passed
  over, while a name nobody declared is a mistake.
- `503 unavailable` with `Retry-After: 10` when the node's maintenance lane has
  no free slot or background work leaves the check no memory. A check holds one
  slot of that lane, and its connectivity check's memory, from admission to end
  (background indexing keeps one slot free for it), so the lane bounds how many
  checks run at once.
- `409 verify_running` when a check of the repository with the other `repair`
  setting is running on the node, naming it as `running`. One with the same
  setting is answered as that one: two asking share one check.
- `503 unavailable` with `Retry-After: 30` on a node where Gitlet is stopping,
  and `500 query_failed` **with its sentence** when the node's memory cannot
  hold the check at all (the sentence says to run it on a node with more).

A repair writes into the node's copy, so a draining node refuses the route.
Mounted only where git is served.

**Admin only**, as the deployment's other controls are (`fleet.operate`, which
asks a signed-in person for a recent proof; the read below is `fleet.read`): a
caller without `admin` is refused `403 unauthorized` naming it, before the node
is asked anything. The check holds a maintenance slot and a repair rewrites what
every fetch on the node is served from: an operation on the node, which no
repository's grant decides.

### `GET /gitlet/repos/{name}/verify/{id}`

A verification begun by the `POST` above. `state` is:

- `running`.
- `done`, with `report`, the node's check:
  - `packs` and `refs` checked.
  - `repaired_by_sync`: what the node's sync before the check found damaged and
    repaired in place (a file the copy no longer holds: no problem of the copy,
    nothing a repair rebuilds).
  - `problems`: each sentence names the file and both values (none means a copy
    exactly its rows).
  - After a repair, how: `repaired_in_place` (the copy's own directory put right
    in place), `rebuilt`, or both (a rebuild followed for what the in-place read
    left); `problems` is then what the check after it found and `found` what the
    first check found.
- `failed`, with `error` (`unavailable` for what a retry or restart clears, a
  stop among them; `query_failed` otherwise), `detail` (its sentence: a pack the
  object store does not hold, the stop that cut it short) and `report`, **what
  the check found before it failed**.

`ended` is set once it is not running.

While `running` and checking the copy, `deadline` is **when the node ends that
check by**. Each pass is bounded by the copy's size (about 1.1 seconds a
mebibyte: connectivity check a second of it, hashing a tenth, against a measured
9 ms); a pass still running then is ended, `failed` saying it ran past its bound,
rather than holding its slot. A client waits by it. It is absent while the node
first brings its copy to the rows it checks against, and while a repair reads it
whole in place or rebuilds it: each object store read those make is bounded on
its own, as every sync's is.

The node keeps a verification **an hour after it ends**, until the repository's
next verify begins, and never across a restart; one it does not keep is `404
not_found`. A read, so a draining node still answers it. A client polls by the
stated `deadline`, at doubling waits from the quarter of a second the request
already waited; a poll costs a lookup.

## Agent Memory

### `GET /agents/{id}/memory`

What one seat has learned, in one round trip, **answered by the node holding the
seat**. Also the `agent_memory` query, which takes `{id, limit,
skills_order}`; the route takes `?limit=` and `?skills_order=` (`uses` or
`updated`; the newest drafted first when absent), the order the holder reads the seat's whole set of
skills in before it cuts their page.

`{id}` is the seat's **handle**, the canonical identifier everywhere, or a
person's **login**, which names the seat the identity directory binds them to and
is never read as a handle. It is a seat's TRAIL, so it takes `audit.seat.read`
(the seat's lead, or `admin`); an absent name is the caller's own seat. The
answer resolves the store's two keys (diary and onboarding marker by derived
agent id; episodes, skills and counterparty profiles by handle) itself.

```json
{
  "id": "<handle>",
  "diary": [
    { "id", "content", "retention", "source", "turn_id",
      "created_at", "ttl_until", "retrievals" }
  ],
  "diary_total": 142,
  "episodes": [
    { "id", "turn_id", "agent_handle", "task_summary", "ask", "ask_bytes",
      "plan_summary", "plan_summary_bytes",
      "review_outcome", "tool_sequence", "skills_used",
      "conversation_key", "work_key", "created_at", "ended_at",
      "duration_ms", "compacted", "count",
      "compaction": { "common_task_pattern", "done", "notable_patterns" } }
  ],
  "episodes_total": 38,
  "skills": [
    { "id", "key", "title", "summary", "version", "updated_at", "uses" }
  ],
  "skills_total": 4,
  "counterparties": [
    { "subject": { "handle" | "external_id" + "platform", "name" },
      "resolved", "traits", "interactions",
      "first_seen_at", "last_updated_at", "last_corroborated_at" }
  ],
  "counterparties_total": 11,
  "latest_reflection": { "id", "content", "…": "a diary row" },
  "onboarded_at": "2026-09-01T08:02:11Z",
  "held_by": "node-2"
}
```

**Who answers.** A seat's memory is written to the store of the node running it
and carried to every node on a compacted changelog, so every node that ever held
a seat keeps a copy and only the holder keeps it CURRENT. The serving node reads
the seat's lease and:

| The lease names | The answer |
|---|---|
| nobody | empty, with `held_by: "none"`: copies on disk are of unknown age, none is shown as the seat's memory |
| this node's own incarnation | read here, once the seat is attached; while it is arriving (hydrating before its mailbox attaches) the read is `unavailable`, not short |
| a peer | asked of that incarnation on an ephemeral scatter (`crewlet.held.read`), 2 s budget; silence (a draining holder or lapsed heartbeat included) is `unavailable` naming the node, never an empty memory |

`held_by` is the node that answered. A node with no broker is the whole fleet and
answers from its own store. `unavailable` is a `503` with a `Retry-After` on REST
and the socket's `unavailable` code with `retry_after`: a moment's wait, not a
fault.

**Every collection is a page with its total beside it.** `limit` (1–50, default
50) pages all four; `diary_total`, `episodes_total`, `skills_total` and
`counterparties_total` are COUNTED in the store over the seat's whole set. The
answer is one reply on the broker, so the episodes, the skills and the
counterparties each also end at 1 MiB of text (a quarter of half the reply),
before the row that would pass it and never before the first: a page can hold
fewer than `limit` rows while its total counts them all. A diary note is bounded
where it is written, so the diary takes no such bound. A skill row never carries
the skill's body.
`latest_reflection` is the newest live diary entry whatever the page (a profile's
summary asks for `limit=1` and reads the totals and this), null when the diary
holds none.

**Every key is present on every answer**, as an empty list or a zero, so "learned
nothing" is distinct from "this answer lacks that half".

**An episode:** `task_summary` is the label of the event that woke the turn,
`ask` what it was asked (`""` if told nothing), `plan_summary` what it did. A
compacted row stands for `count` turns and carries `compaction` (what they had in
common, how many ended `done`, counted from the members, and what varied);
`compaction` is `null` on a raw row.

**A listed episode carries only the openings of its two long texts**, so one
long turn does not fill the page. `ask` and `plan_summary` are each at most
their first 600 bytes, cut between characters and never inside a redaction
marker (the figure a seat is shown of a past turn's words,
`learning.EpisodeAccountBytes`); `ask_bytes` and
`plan_summary_bytes` are the whole texts' sizes: a text is whole exactly when its
size is its length. The whole row is
[`GET /agents/{id}/memory/episodes/{episode}`](#get-agentsidmemoryepisodesepisode).

### `GET /agents/{id}/memory/episodes/{episode}`

One episode **whole**: the listing's row with `ask` and `plan_summary` complete.
Also the `agent_episode` query, which takes `{id, episode}`. Answered by the node
holding the seat under the rules of `GET /agents/{id}/memory` above, its rule
included: `audit.seat.read`, the seat's lead or `admin`.

```json
{
  "handle": "<handle>",
  "episode": { "id", "task_summary", "ask", "ask_bytes", "plan_summary",
               "plan_summary_bytes", "…": "an episode row" },
  "held_by": "node-2"
}
```

`episode` is `null` for one the seat does not hold (dropped or folded into a
compacted row since it was listed, or another seat's), an ordinary absence. An
episode's ask and account came in one turn's event, which the transport held to
8 MiB, so a whole read fits; should one ever not, it is `unavailable`, with the
holder saying how large the answer was, rather than cut.

### `memory_overview`

Every agent seat's memory at a glance: the list **Doclet › Agent diaries** draws.
A socket query with no parameters (no REST route; `GET /agents/{id}/memory` is the
one seat's record).

```json
{
  "seats": [
    { "handle": "swe", "diary_total": 142, "episodes_total": 38,
      "skills_total": 4, "last_reflection_at": "2026-09-28T16:02:11Z",
      "latest_reflection": { "id", "content", "…": "a diary row" },
      "held_by": "node-2", "unavailable": "" }
  ],
  "coverage": { "nodes": [{ "id": "node-1", "answered": true, "error": "" }],
                "complete": true }
}
```

**Every agent seat in the chart, in handle order, no cap**; a person keeps no
engine-written memory and is not listed. Each row is counted by the node HOLDING
the seat under the rules of `agent_memory` above, gathered in ONE round: the
serving node lists every seat lease once, groups seats by holding incarnation,
reads its own from its store and puts ONE request on `crewlet.held.read` naming
each holder's seats; each holder answers for its own in one reply, inside the
same 2 s budget. A row is one of:

| Row | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `held_by` a node, `unavailable` empty | counted by that node; the totals are the ones `agent_memory` carries |
| `held_by: "none"` | no node holds the seat; nothing counted, because no copy is current |
| `held_by` a node, `unavailable` set | that node did not answer (or its answer could not be read), or is still taking the seat; the reason is here and the zeros beside it are not a count |

`coverage` is the shape every fleet answer carries: this node and every holder
asked, each `answered` or with its `error`, and `complete` only when all
answered. An unreadable lease table fails the whole answer as `unavailable`.

The rows are **projected** by `internal/learning/memread`, not the learning
package's structs marshalled directly, which have no `json` tags and carry every
row's raw embedding vector.

Sources:

* **`diary`**: the seat's private observation log, written by
  `reflect_and_persist` and the reflection pass, live entries only, newest first.
  `retention` is `diary_long` or `diary_short`; a short entry carries the
  `ttl_until` it lapses at. `retrievals` is how often it has been recalled.
* **`episodes`**: one row per completed turn (or compacted cluster), newest
  first. `duration_ms` is milliseconds (a Go `time.Duration` marshals as
  nanoseconds).
* **`skills`**: the seat's own synthesized skills, drafted from repeated work and
  loadable mid-turn via `use_skill`. Archived rows are hidden and stale ones
  shown, because a stale skill still works and revives on use.
* **`counterparties`**: what the seat learned about the people it works with,
  most recently updated first. `last_updated_at` moves on every interaction,
  `last_corroborated_at` only when the traits changed. `traits` is a bag whose
  keys the model invents. `subject` carries a `handle` for a seat of this company
  and an `external_id` with its `platform` for anybody else.
* **`onboarded_at`**: when the seat first finished onboarding, or `""`; a pass
  claimed and never finished is not an onboarding.

A store that cannot be read fails the read rather than answering an empty
section: "remembers nothing" and "the store did not answer" are opposite facts.
The table is strictly per-agent; cross-agent procedural artefacts are
[promoted](../concepts/agent-learning.md) as draft pages in the shared knowledge
backend, reachable by all members via query-time search.

---

## Executor Sessions

Every turn whose [executor](../concepts/code-sandbox.md) captured its harness's
session keeps it, sealed in the fleet's
[object store](../concepts/object-store.md), named by the turn's row of the
`executor` log
([ADR-0073](https://github.com/crewlet/crewlet/blob/main/adr/0073-a-seats-executor-session-is-a-sealed-object-its-turns-row-names.md)).
That session is the whole record of what the run read, called and wrote. Two
reads show it: a seat's sessions, and one session's transcript.

**Both are the seat's trail**, decided per seat by `audit.seat.read` (the seat
itself, whoever leads it, or `admin`), as it decides
[`executor_tail`](#queries) and a seat's phases with their prompts and responses:
a session reaches nobody the run's live output did not. **It shows more than the
live output.** The live output names each tool call's subject (whole only within
8 KiB) and a failed result's first line, never a result's body; a transcript
holds every call's whole input, each result's text to an entry's bound (file
contents the run read, what its commands printed) and every subagent's thread.
Redaction at the read matches the credential shapes the engine knows, not values:
a secret of no recognisable shape that a run read is in its transcript as read.

`{id}` is the seat's **handle**, or a person's **login**, which names the seat the
identity directory binds them to; an absent `handle` on the socket is the
caller's own seat. A refusal names `admin`, which would have admitted the caller.

**Any node answers.** Rows are read through the estate router (a node without
`data` asks a data node) at the caller's freshness (`read_level`,
`max_lag_seconds`, `max_lag_seq`, `min_position`; this surface's own level when
absent, and a bare `session` is refused), and a session's bytes through the
fleet's one object store, opened under the node's own keyring. Each answer says
how its rows were read (`read_level`, `position` and `complete`), as every answer
of a state-log domain does.
### `GET /agents/{id}/sessions`

The seat's executor sessions, **the latest begun first**, paged: `?limit=` rows
(25 when absent, 100 at most) after `?cursor=`, the `next_cursor` an earlier
page handed out. Also served as the `executor_sessions` query.

```json
{
  "handle": "swe",
  "sessions": [
    {
      "turn_id": "0193f0c2-6a1e-7c55-9d1a-3b6f0e2a4c11",
      "conversation_key": "slack:C0ENG:1700000000.000100",
      "work_key": "",
      "harness": "claude-code",
      "harness_version": "2.1.310",
      "captured_at": "2026-10-30T12:04:00Z",
      "ended_at": "2026-10-30T12:05:00Z",
      "ending": { "outcome": "completed", "decision": "done", "delivered": true,
                  "delivered_to": "chatlet", "completed_work": "…" },
      "ask_excerpt": "…",
      "kept": true,
      "object_bytes": 41234,
      "in_progress": false,
      "base_turn": "0193f0b8-2d4c-7e1a-9b3f-5c8d7e6f1a20",
      "continued_by": "next_turn",
      "continuable": true,
      "continues_in": "any_box"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "48121",
  "read_level": "stale",
  "position": { "stream": "CREWLET_EXECUTOR_LOG", "generation": 1, "seq": 48207 },
  "complete": true
}
```

- **A row begins at its turn's first launch** where the turn read its
  conversation (its `begin`), else at its first capture. **A row goes with the
  turn that was handed it**: once a later turn of its conversation that was
  handed its session and kept one of its own ends, its end absorbs the turns its
  read handed out and their rows leave the list, as do rows past
  `turn_engine.conversation_session.retention_days` and a removed seat's.
- **`ending`** is the engine's account of how the turn ended; `null` while the
  turn runs, or when its end was lost and the engine has yet to record it `lost`
  (a day after its last record). `outcome` is `completed`, `failed`, `stopped` or
  `lost`. The rest is sent only where the ending establishes it:
  - `decision`: the reviewer's. `completed_work`: the reviewer's. `blocked_on`:
    the executor's. `answer`: the engine's answer to a colleague's ask.
  - `delivered`: whether the reply reached the party waiting; `delivered_to`: the
    surface it was owed on (sent whether or not it went).
  - `delivery_unknown`: whether it went is not known (the turn's call record was
    cut to stay bounded and the kept calls show no delivery); never beside
    `delivered`.
  - `stopped_by` and `stop_reason`; `failure`: the engine's.
  - `unkept`: the turn's newest capture where it was not kept: `launch_seq`,
    `capture_seq` and `reason` (quotes what refused it). Sent only where newer
    than the last capture the row named; one at the row's own place, whose record
    the log took before the turn's end after all, is the row's and kept.
  - `went_on: true`: the turn went on past the session its row names (its record
    did not hold its last word, the final capture of its last launch that ran a
    job, kept). The named session was kept while the turn still worked, so it
    holds what the turn did up to there and nothing after. Sent beside every
    `unkept` this engine records, and on a row naming no session. The row keeps
    what it names; the conversation's next turn continues it, told so.
  - `last_word`: the final capture's `launch_seq` and `capture_seq`, where the
    end said the turn went on and that capture was its newest. A row at that
    place holds it after all (the log took its record although the run's own
    record held it refused) and is sent without `went_on`.
  - `spent_sessions`: the sessions a launch spent, each its `session` id and its
    `loss` (`context_exhausted` or `request_refused`); no launch continues them.

  The prose among them, and `ask_excerpt` (the first kibibyte of what the turn
  was asked), are a model's or a person's words, **redacted at this read**,
  `unkept.reason` included.
- **`kept`** says the row still names a session's object, of `object_bytes`
  sealed. A row naming none is an ending alone, for one of four reasons its
  transcript's `why` and its `not_continuable` say: its turn captured nothing
  (yet, while it runs); its newest capture was not kept and none before it was
  (or an end an earlier engine version recorded took the older one off the row);
  a run [ran out of context](../concepts/conversation-sessions.md#a-session-that-ran-out-of-context-is-retired)
  in its session, which retired it; or the seat's session budget
  (`turn_engine.conversation_session.max_bytes_per_seat`) released its object for
  newer ones, keeping how the turn ended. Only the budget releases a session its
  turn went on past, said with the newer capture `unkept` names.
- **`in_progress`**: the row names the session of a turn that has not ended, the
  newest its runs have kept (a job's final capture while the turn goes on to its
  review or waits on a person's answer, or one a loss left its box to take). Its
  run may have gone on past it, and its last call may have no result yet. A
  relaunch continues it only where `continuable` says so, since a relaunch
  continues the newest kept capture of the job it follows, and a live turn's row
  often names an earlier job's. `false` on any other row, a live one naming no
  session yet included.
- **`in_progress_note`** is the engine's own sentence, the one a seat's own
  `list_sessions` and `read_session` carry
  ([A seat reads its own](../concepts/code-sandbox.md#a-seat-reads-its-own)):
  "This turn has not ended: this is the newest session its runs have kept,
  captured at `<captured_at>`; its run may have gone on past it, and its last
  call may have no result yet." Absent where `in_progress` is `false`.
- **`kept_note`** is the engine's own sentence told every reader of an ended row
  whose session its turn went on past: for `went_on`, that the session was taken
  while the turn still worked and what it did after is not in it; for a `lost`
  turn, that the session may not hold the last of what it did. It carries the
  newer capture `unkept` names and why, redacted (that reason quotes what refused
  the capture, so a seat reads the note fenced). Absent on any other row; a row
  at its turn's `last_word` holds all the turn did, unless the turn was lost.
- **`trimmed_note`** is the engine's own sentence, the one a seat's own
  `list_sessions` and `read_session` carry, told every reader of a row whose
  session was [trimmed past the bound](../concepts/code-sandbox.md#each-launchs-session-kept)
  to what its harness's resume loads: "The history before this session's newest
  compaction was trimmed to keep it within the bound a kept session is held to:
  its transcript begins there." Absent on any other row, and on one whose
  session is no longer kept.
- **`base_turn`** is the ended turn whose session this turn's first launch was
  handed to continue: its conversation's head as the dispatch read it (of the
  conversation's ended turns whose rows still name a session, the one that read
  the conversation last), held on the log by the turn's `begin`. Absent where the
  read named none, that session had gone before the `begin` landed, or no `begin`
  landed. Whether a launch took it up is the `executor_collected` records'
  `brief` (`continued_conversation`).
- **`continued_by`** is the launch the rest is about: `relaunch` while the turn
  is live and its run is neither over nor ending; `next_turn` once it has ended,
  or its run is over or ending and its end is not on the log yet. For a turn of a
  schedule's conversation (`conversation_key` `schedule/…`) it is `next_fire`,
  decided the same way and said in the schedule's words. Absent for a turn that
  served no conversation, and on a transcript's later page.
- **`continuable`** says whether that launch would continue this session, decided
  by the one decision that launch takes, of the member of the seat's executor
  chain it would be launched on now (the first not sitting out its plan).
  - **A relaunch**: the turn live and not ending, the newest kept capture of the
    job a relaunch would follow (stating its save point, named by the row), and a
