    runner that restores its harness, format and release
    ([A relaunch continues the turn's
    session](../concepts/code-sandbox.md#a-relaunch-continues-the-turns-session)).
  - **The next turn**: only the conversation's head (of its ended turns whose
    rows still name a session, the one that read the conversation last, named by
    the same read's snapshot) is continued, where that runner restores it
    ([A conversation's next turn continues its last turn's
    session](../concepts/code-sandbox.md#a-conversations-next-turn-continues-its-last-turns-session)).
  - **The member is the one the node holding the seat would pick**, sitting its
    own spent plans out, off the chain of the revision the launch runs on: for a
    turn whose resumed segment is running, the revision it was admitted under;
    for a next turn, the revision live when it comes. The node answering asks it,
    once a page (a live turn's session by its turn, a head by none), itself where
    it holds the seat.
  - **`continues_in`**: `any_box`, in whichever box the launch gets (a relaunch
    from the kept capture, in the box its job parked in where that capture was
    taken while the job still worked, from the copy that box holds; the next turn
    from the head, in a box of its own); or `parked_box`, a relaunch's alone,
    where the kept capture is not continued but a person's answer would carry the
    turn's parked run on in the box it parked in (still held, ran the row's own
    session there, runs that member's harness in its cell, on the node host for a
    box on the engine host), nowhere else, while the box is held. A company with
    `turn_engine.conversation_session.enabled: false` continues no kept capture:
    only `parked_box` is said, and no next turn continues anything.
  - **`not_continuable`**, in the engine's own words, redacted, is why the launch
    would not continue it, why that cannot be said now, or, for `parked_box`, why
    no other box would. A row that is not its conversation's head names the turn
    whose session the next turn is handed instead; one naming no session says
    which of the four reasons it is; a live turn with no session of its own says,
    where its row still holds the session its first launch was handed, that a
    relaunch in a box of its own continues that one.
  - Decided as far as the engine can know before a box is chosen: whether the box
    can take the session up, is a box of its own, and whether the seat's budget
    can carry it are the launch's to find out.
  - `false`, with no `continued_by`, for a turn that served no conversation once
    it has ended or is ending.
  - `null` where it cannot be said now:
    - the turn's run record, or its row read as a relaunch reads it, could not be
      read;
    - the job a relaunch would follow is still working, or a claim on it has
      neither taken its final capture nor begun its turn; its capture is still
      being kept, or its record was sent and never answered. A relaunch asks the
      executor log again before deciding, continuing the capture where it landed,
      else the newest capture that job kept before it, until fourteen hours have
      passed since the capture's object was minted on the reading node's clock
      (the twelve a record may name it in, past which the executor log refuses
      the record on its own clock, and two for any two machines' clock skew);
    - a capture of an earlier job is still being kept while the turn has kept
      none of its own (once one lands a relaunch no longer continues the session
      the first launch was handed; beside a kept capture of the turn, an earlier
      job's keep changes nothing and the row is decided);
    - what the launch is launched on cannot be said (every member of the seat's
      chain sitting out its plan, no node holding the seat, the node holding it
      not answering);
    - only the resume of a collected job decides the relaunch, and its turn has
      not begun (a round lost a second time, or carried on in its box only where
      its sign-in was replaced);
    - the turn's run is over or ending and its end is not on the log yet, which
      `not_continuable` then says.

    A resumed turn says, as it begins, whether it collects its job or carries the
    round on; from then on, its review included, the row is decided on that.
  - **Reads per page**: the coordination store once for its runs (a live turn's
    record alone where the listing does not hold it, none where every row has
    ended); once more for the seat's lease where a row asks the node holding the
    seat (a live row whose run is neither over nor ending, or a conversation's
    head). Answered whether or not either answers. A live row is read again at
    `linearizable` only where the page was read below that and the row names
    another capture than its run's record keeps, or the record keeps none. An
    ended row is decided on the page's own snapshot, each head read in the same
    transaction as the rows.
- **Paged by where each row began**, which nothing moves, so a page never skips
  or repeats a row captured again or ended between two reads. `next_cursor` is
  absent on the last page. `complete: false` says the answering copy holds a
  record of the log it could not read, which may hold rows missing from the page.

A `cursor` that is not a page's position (a positive whole number) is
`400 bad_params`; any other answers the rows begun before the position it names.

### `GET /agents/{id}/sessions/{turn_id}`

One turn's session and a page of its **transcript**, `?cursor=` the
`next_cursor` an earlier page of it handed out. Also served as the
`executor_session` query, which takes `{handle, turn_id, cursor}`. The
first page (no `cursor`) says of its row which launch would continue the
session and whether, as a page of `GET /agents/{id}/sessions` says it, on the
head of its conversation the row's own read names; a later page leaves
`continuable` `null`, saying it is the first page's to say.

```json
{
  "handle": "swe",
  "session": { "turn_id": "…", "…": "the row as GET /agents/{id}/sessions sends it" },
  "state": "read",
  "entries": [
    { "kind": "brief", "at": "2026-10-30T12:00:00Z", "text": "Fix the flaky test in ENG-7.", "bytes": 28 },
    { "kind": "tool_call", "at": "…", "tool": "Bash", "text": "{\"command\":\"go test ./cache/...\"}", "bytes": 33 },
    { "kind": "tool_result", "at": "…", "tool": "Bash", "failed": true, "text": "FAIL cache_test.go:40 …", "bytes": 2201431, "cut": true },
    { "kind": "note", "at": "…", "text": "## A note from ada, sent while this turn was running\n…", "bytes": 214 },
    { "kind": "brief", "thread": "agent-a1", "text": "Look for the race.", "bytes": 18 }
  ],
  "from": 0,
  "cut": "entries",
  "next_cursor": "0193f0c3-0d5e-7a14-8b2f-61c9e2d0a7f3.2.200",
  "bounds": { "entries": 200, "bytes": 1048576, "entry_bytes": 16384,
              "read_lines": 1048576, "read_bytes": 268435456 },
  "read_level": "stale",
  "position": { "stream": "CREWLET_EXECUTOR_LOG", "generation": 1, "seq": 48207 },
  "complete": true
}
```

**The archive is read as its harness recorded it**, through the runner's own
knowledge of the format it packs: Claude Code's transcript and each subagent's
own (its sidecar, every entry of which names the subagent in `thread`, after
the run's own), and OpenCode's session export, each message by the kind
OpenCode 2 gives it (its `type`). Each entry is one of:

| `kind` | What it is |
|---|---|
| `brief` | What the run was handed: the engine's brief, a later launch's on the same session, or — in a subagent's `thread` — the brief the run's own model wrote it |
| `note` | A note a person sent the run while it worked, as its harness handed it to the model: the engine's heading naming who sent it, then their words. Read wherever the harness filed it — OpenCode as a person's message, Claude Code as a hook's context in a record of its own — by the heading every note opens with, which starts its line or follows only the harness's framing, so a tool's words quoted on a line never head one; and the line the run's own hook printed as it handed notes over, late calls beside them or not (the live output's `[steer]` line), saying whose reached the run |
| `late_call` | A call of this work that finished after the run that made it had stopped waiting for it (its harness gave up on it, or the run was cut off or replaced), as the engine handed it to the run while it worked: the engine's heading, its words, the call's outcome and the call. Read as a note is, by the heading the engine opens it with; and the line the run's own hook printed as it handed over such calls and no note |
| `wake` | A message somebody wrote about this work while the run worked, as the engine handed it to the run: the engine's heading naming its writer, a line saying where it was written and whether it asks for an answer, then the writer's words inside their fence, where a heading counts for nothing. Read as a note is, by the heading the engine opens it with; and the line the run's own hook printed as it handed over such messages and no note |
| `model` | What the model wrote |
| `tool_call` | A tool the model called, its input as JSON, the tool in `tool` |
| `tool_result` | What the tool answered, `failed` where the harness recorded an error |
| `summary` | A compaction summary: the harness's own account of the conversation before it, which the model read in its place |
| `unread` | A part of the record the read could not read, said where it was so a gap never reads as continuity: a line that is no record, a line longer than the read reads of a harness, a record or a message of no shape the read knows, an OpenCode message of a kind the read does not know, a transcript that is no plain file in the archive (a link), a text whose redaction could not be read, a call's result or a text joined from parts with a part written out of order past the value bound, a Qwen Code compaction's summary past the value bound, a Qwen Code or Gemini CLI tool result past it whose error is no text or that names its output or error twice, a record past the lines and elements one read reads (`bounds.read_lines`) |

The harness's bookkeeping (a session's title, a snapshot of the files it
edited, its system notices), the model's thinking and a tool result Claude Code
spilled to a file are no entry. Nor are the messages OpenCode writes for itself:
its notices in the person's turn (a background job's ending, a reminder, an
instruction file it loaded), an update of the run's instructions, a skill or a
shell command a person ran in the session, the end of an execution, a switch of
the session's agent, model or directory, and a compaction that handed the model
no summary. `at` is when the harness recorded the entry,
absent where its record says no time, or one outside the years 0 to 9999 —
all RFC 3339 can spell, and a box's own agent can write any instant into what
its run packs.

**Redacted at this read, whatever the capture did.** Every entry's text is
passed through the engine's one redaction pass (`redact.Secrets`) **before it is
cut**, and is always **an opening of what its whole text redacts to**.
Everything that can reach the entry's bound, and the longest a credential the
redaction knows can run past it (a private key's block), is redacted inside as
much again, so a credential that begins inside the bound is recognised whole —
a key cut in half by a bound is one the redaction no longer recognises — and
nothing the read could not settle is handed out, however much the redaction
shrinks what comes before it (a key's block becomes one short marker): a
credential that runs across the end of what can reach the bound is not handed
out at all, and the entry is cut where it begins. The rest of a long text is not
scanned only to be dropped.

**Bounded, and the cut said.** A page holds at most `bounds.entries` (200)
entries and `bounds.bytes` (1 MiB) of their text; an entry's text is at most
`bounds.entry_bytes` (16 KiB), cut on a character and marked, with
`cut: true`. Every entry's text is redacted whole before it is cut, and its
`bytes` is always the size of what its whole text redacts to, the text it would
show whole. **Never the size as recorded**, which beside a text shown whole
says how long each value its redaction took out was. A line of the
record is read however long it runs: a value in it (a text, a name, a call's
input) is held to 2 MiB and past it streamed through the redaction into its
entry, never held. One read frames at most `bounds.read_lines` (2^20) lines of
the record and the blocks and parts in them, and takes at most
`bounds.read_bytes` (256 MiB) of the archive as it inflates — and, apart, at
most as many bytes as a tar's members hand out, which a sparse member can make
up without the archive holding them. `cut` is why the page ends before the
transcript does:

| `cut` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| absent | The transcript ends on this page; `next_cursor` is absent |
| `entries`, `bytes` | The page holds all it may; `next_cursor` is the cursor the rest is read from |
| `read` | The read stopped where no later page can go further — the archive's bytes run past `bounds.read_bytes`, or the record more lines and elements than `bounds.read_lines`. The entries shown are all that can be |

Every page is read again from the archive's start, so a page costs what the
archive does rather than what is behind it. **The cursor names the object it
was read from, and how this build counts a transcript's entries**: a live
turn's session moves to a newer object with every capture, and a rolling
upgrade can answer one page on a build that counts entries otherwise, so a
cursor of an object the row has since replaced with a newer capture, or of
another count, is `400 bad_params` — read the transcript again from its start —
rather than a page continued in another archive, or at an ordinal that names
another entry. The refusal says why in the row's words: of a turn that has not
ended (`in_progress`), that its runs have kept its session again since the
cursor was handed out, which is true whichever capture moved it; of an ended
turn, that its session was captured again. A cursor of a row that names no
object any more is answered as
its first page would be, `state: none` with the engine's sentence: the seat's
session budget released the object, or the turn's end did, its newest capture
not kept — each only of a turn that ended — and an ended turn is never captured
again.

**Two transcripts at a time on each node.** One read holds at most 29 MiB
measured, and of what
harnesses and ordinary tools write takes up to about 49 seconds for a person (58
for a seat's words): one value of `password:` lines streamed through its
redaction to `bounds.read_bytes`, beside a second read. So a node decodes at
most two transcripts at once, 58 MiB live at their worst (87 MiB with the heap's
room under the engine's memory limit), whichever socket
question or REST request asks for them. A request past them waits for a slot,
its session's object not yet opened, for as long as its caller waits, and a
slot frees within one such read, so an answer comes within 110 seconds (that
read with a tenth to spare, and one slot's wait), which the dashboard waits;
nothing in the answer says it waited, and a caller that gives up first is
answered nothing. A value none writes at that density, a password's value every
few bytes the whole budget long, takes 98 seconds or more and fails closed once
it runs past that wait: a socket question's `wait_ms` ends its read, answered
nothing, and the
dashboard says the transcript could not be read in time. A seat reading its own
sessions waits two minutes, so its read of such a session, or one queued behind
other reads at their bounds, is answered unavailable.

**An object that cannot be read is an answer, never a 500.** The row is still
the turn's account of how it ended, so `state` says why no entries are shown
and `why` says it in the engine's own words — never in anything the archive
held:

| `state` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `read` | The entries are the transcript's |
| `none` | The row names no object: its turn captured nothing (yet, while it runs), its newest capture was not kept, a run ran out of context in its session, which retired it, or the seat's budget released it |
| `missing` | The object store no longer holds the object, which the turn's row, read again, still names |
| `unreadable` | The object does not open: it is sealed under a keyring key this fleet no longer holds, or its bytes are not the ones sealed for this turn |
| `malformed` | It opened, and is not an archive of its harness's format, and `why` says which of six ways: it is not gzip-compressed, its compressed bytes are corrupt, it ends part way through, it holds no tar of its harness's files, it holds no export document of its harness's, or its bytes are not laid out as its format describes (a box's own agent can rewrite what its run packs before a collection takes it) |
| `unsupported` | It is of a harness or an archive format this build does not read |

A store that did not answer is `503 unavailable` with a `Retry-After`, and a
turn the seat keeps no row of is `404 not_found`, saying how a row goes: its
turn recorded none, or its row went with the end of a later turn of its
conversation that was handed it, past the retention, or with the seat. Absent
on a node with no object store, where the rows are still listed.

**A session released while it is read is said as released.** Reading a
session holds nothing, so between the read of its row and the end of its
object's stream a later turn's end can absorb it, the seat's budget release it,
the end of a turn that ran out of context in it retire it, the retention delete
it or its turn capture it again — and the collector take the object once no row
names it. Read alone, a collected object is `missing`,
and one taken while it streams one whose bytes do not open, so a read whose
object fails, as it opens or as it streams, reads the turn's row once more, at
`linearizable` whatever the request asked, and answers what the row says now:
no row is `404 not_found`, saying its row went while it was read and that
nothing more of it can be read; a row naming no object is `state: none` with
its reason and the same; and a row naming a newer capture is read from that
capture on a first page, and refuses a later page's cursor as one captured
again (`400 bad_params`). `read_level`, `position` and `session` are then that
read's. Only where the row still names the object is the failure the store's or
the archive's own — `missing`, `unreadable`, or `503 unavailable` — and the row
is read again once, a newer capture that fails too said as it fails. A row that
cannot be read again leaves the failure unknown, a release as much as a loss,
and is `503 unavailable`. A later page whose row went, or names no object,
before it is read is answered the same way; the pages already read stand as
they were.

---

## Fleet, Executors & Schedules

### `GET /mcp-servers`

Backs the **Servers** tab of **Settings › MCP & tools**: every MCP server, what the configuration declares for it, what each live node did with it, and the engine's built-in tools.
**It is everybody's, in two readings**, as [`GET /llm/entries`](#get-llmentries) is: a server's condition and tools tell a member why an agent lacks one. A caller `config.read` admits (an administrator) reads the answer below whole, `reading: "admin"`, as `GET /config` shows them the launch commands. Anybody else reads [a member's reading](#a-members-reading-of-mcp--tools), `reading: "member"`, which names no launch line, failure sentence or wait.

**Off the status records, not a fan-out.** Each node re-publishes its MCP servers on its [status record](../concepts/coordination.md#its-status-record) within a renew period of a change. A child that died after it started counts as failed until the engine has [brought it back](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#a-server-that-dies-or-will-not-start); a shared server whose start failed counts as started once a retry brings it up. One row per server, instances counted (a per-seat template has one instance per seat that node holds). One read of the records, counted against the lease table's presence, is every node's answer. A live node with no record counted at its presence's epoch (just started, or back at a new epoch and not yet written) is `reported: false` and its cells are UNKNOWN, never zeros, which would read as "started nothing". A node that reports and started nothing is `reported: true` with no rows.

`servers` lists every server this node's configuration declares, then any a node reports that the configuration does not carry (`configured: false`: a node on an older revision mid-rollout).
- The launch is the non-credential parts: `transport`, `command`, `args`, `url`; `env` and `headers` are never here.
- `enabled` is whether the configuration runs the server at all (`mcp_servers[].enabled`, true on a server it does not carry).
- `description` is what the configuration says the server is for, the line each agent's prompt lists beside its name (`""` when it says nothing).
- `title`, `catalogue` and `vendor` are what the [curated catalogue](#get-mcp-catalogue) recognises the server as, by address or command: the entry's title, its key and the vendor mark the dashboard draws. An unknown server is titled by its name, with `catalogue` and `vendor` empty.
- `started`, `failed` and `waiting` are summed over the nodes, `tools` is the most one started instance serves, and `state` is decided here so no screen re-derives it.

`waiting` counts a seat's instances held back, unstarted, for a credential a [provisioning pass mints for that seat](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#shared-vs-per-role-servers) and has not sealed yet, where nothing that pass last reported says it cannot. They are neither started nor failed, since nothing is wrong; each starts once the seal reaches its node. So does an instance whose token the engine issues at use while its integration is still settling it (a grant the vendor is still applying): nothing is sealed, so its node asks again on the restart schedule (15 seconds, doubling to 5 minutes) and starts it once issued. One whose pass reports that a person must act first (its own credential missing or refused, an approval outstanding, the seat's account failed or switched off, or the integration disconnected) counts as `failed`, judged again at every pass of the node's status record, since a wait with no end is a failure somebody must act on.

| `state` | Means |
|---|---|
| `disabled` | The configuration turns the server off (`enabled: false`): nothing is started and no seat is granted it. Decided before anything a node reports, so a node on an earlier revision that runs it shows only in its own cell until it applies this one |
| `needs_sign_in` | The server is [signed in to with OAuth](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#signing-in-with-oauth) and nobody holds a grant for it, its vendor refused to renew the grant or let it run out, or nothing serves it and the nodes hold it back for a sign-in (its grant was made for an address the server is no longer configured at). Nothing is started until somebody signs in. Decided next, before the other counts |
| `running` | Every instance any node launched is serving: started, listed its tools and was up when its node last wrote its record |
| `partial` | Some are serving and some are not: a node's environment, one seat's credentials, or one child that died and is being restarted, rather than the server |
| `failing` | Something failed and nothing is serving: instances were launched and none serves (the server, its command or address, or credentials every seat shares), every instance went down and is being restarted, or the server was held back, unlaunched, for a value that resolves to nothing (a shared server's own, or one every seat's instance lacks) |
| `waiting` | Nothing was launched and nothing failed, and some seat's instance waits for its provisioned credential. Only where nothing else decides: a server serving one seat while another waits is `running`, and a failure beside a wait is `partial` or `failing` |
| `not_started` | Every reporting node started nothing for it: a per-seat template granted to no seat a live node holds |
| `unreported` | No live node has a status record counted |

`error` is one failed instance's reason, cut to 512 bytes on the status record, and `error_seat` the seat it was launched for (none for a shared server). It is the instance down longest on that node, so `error`, `error_seat`, `error_class` and `down_since` are one instance's facts (ties go to the lower seat id). The whole text is in the node's log: `mcp_server_failed` for a start that failed; `mcp_server_credential_missing` for an instance held back, unlaunched, because a value it is started with resolves to nothing and nothing mints it, or the minting integration cannot mint until a person acts (from the node's last pass over the seat; the status record re-judges it against the integration's latest report); `mcp_server_credential_unsure` for one held because what that integration last reported cannot say whether it holds the seat up ([Tools and MCP](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md)); `server_exited` or `server_restart_failed` for an instance that went down after it started. `wait` is one waiting instance's sentence (the variables it waits for and the integration minting them), bounded the same way, and `wait_seat` its seat: the instance waiting longest on that node; the node's `mcp_server_awaiting_credential` line carries it.

`error_class` is why that instance failed, in the classes a person tells apart by what fixes them ([Tools and MCP › Why a server failed](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#why-a-server-failed)), or `""` where none fits. `down_since` is when the longest-failed instance on the node stopped serving, or first failed to start, the same instant across the retries of one outage (`null` when none has failed). `restarts` is how many times the node brought the server's instances back since each was started from its spec, summed: a count that climbs while the server stays up is a server that flaps.

The `url` is answered with credentials withheld. These read `redacted`: the value of any query parameter whose name marks a credential (`key`, `token`, `secret`, `sig`, `pass`, `auth`, `session`, `credential` and the like, any case) or whose value has a known credential's shape; a path segment of a known credential's shape; a fragment's credential (`#access_token=...`); a user name in the address. Scheme, host and port stay readable, and an address with nothing to withhold is answered as written.

`unlisted_annotations` are the entry's `tool_annotations` keys that no instance started on a reporting node lists a tool for (by the server's own name or with the entry's `tool_prefix`), sorted: each overrides nothing anywhere it runs, a misspelling or a tool the server no longer serves. A key only SOME instances lack is not here, because a per-seat child serves what its seat's credentials reach (an `mcp-atlassian` child for a seat holding only a Jira credential lists no Confluence tool). Each node publishes the keys none of its own started instances lists, whole and as many as its 16 KiB status row holds (the first by sort), counting the rest, and the answer keeps those every such node names: past a node's cut it can miss a key but never names one an instance lists. `unlisted_annotations_count` is the list's length where every node's list was whole, and where one was cut the most keys the list may stand for (the fewest a started node counts), so a count above the list's length says a node's list was cut and the list may miss keys; with no instance started the list is empty and the count 0. Each instance's own keys are on its `tools_discovered` log line (`annotation_keys_unlisted`).

`refused_tools` are the server's tools not offered for their name, and `shadowed_tools` the ones another server's tool of the same name is offered in place of ([Naming a server and its tools](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#naming-a-server-and-its-tools)). Each is `{tool, reason, message}` or `{tool, by, message}`:
- `tool` is the name it would be filed under (the server's `tool_prefix` and its own name).
- `reason` is `characters`, `too_long` or `builtin`.
- `by` is the configured name of the server whose tool is offered instead.
- `message` is the engine's sentence saying why and what would offer it (a shorter `tool_prefix`, one where two servers share a name), which a screen shows as written.

Each tool is listed once across the fleet, sorted, every one any node named. A node names at most 8 of each on its status record, so `refused_count` and `shadowed_count` say how many there are, as the node counting the most counts them, never fewer than listed. Both lists are always present, empty where every tool is offered. The node's log names each too (`mcp_tool_refused`, `tool_name_collision`).

```json
{
  "reading": "admin",
  "nodes": [{"id": "node-1", "reported": true}, {"id": "node-2", "reported": true}],
  "servers": [
    {"name": "github", "title": "GitHub", "catalogue": "github", "vendor": "github",
     "configured": true, "shared": false, "transport": "http",
     "command": "", "args": [], "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/",
     "state": "partial", "started": 3, "failed": 1, "waiting": 0, "tools": 26,
     "unlisted_annotations": [], "unlisted_annotations_count": 0,
     "refused_tools": [
       {"tool": "gh_add_pull_request_review_comment_to_pending_review", "reason": "too_long",
        "message": "\"gh_add_pull_request_review_comment_to_pending_review\" is not offered: it is 52 characters, and 50 fit beside the longest prefix a harness gives the engine's tools. Shorten the tool_prefix \"gh_\" by 2 to offer it"}
     ],
     "refused_count": 1, "shadowed_tools": [], "shadowed_count": 0,
     "nodes": [
       {"node": "node-1", "reported": true, "started": 2, "failed": 0, "waiting": 0, "tools": 26,
        "error": "", "error_seat": "", "wait": "", "wait_seat": "",
        "error_class": "", "down_since": null, "restarts": 0},
       {"node": "node-2", "reported": true, "started": 1, "failed": 1, "waiting": 0, "tools": 26,
        "error": "401 Bad credentials", "error_seat": "backend-dev", "wait": "", "wait_seat": "",
        "error_class": "credential_rejected", "down_since": "2026-11-01T08:52:10Z", "restarts": 4}
     ]}
  ],
  "alarms": [
    {"kind": "mcp_server_partial",
     "title": "A tool server is down for some agents", "person": "…",
     "detail": "1 of 4 instances of github is not serving, and one has been down for 7m 50s (backend-dev's, on node-2, credential_rejected): 401 Bad credentials",
     "remedy": "The agents and nodes whose instance serves are not affected. …",
     "entries": [
       {"key": "github",
        "detail": "1 of 4 instances of github is not serving, and one has been down for 7m 50s (backend-dev's, on node-2, credential_rejected): 401 Bad credentials",
        "since": "2026-11-01T08:52:10Z", "seat": "backend-dev",
        "fix": {"kind": "restart", "server": "github", "seat": "backend-dev"}}
     ]}
  ],
  "approvals": [
    {"id": "0190f3a8-6b1c-7d2e-9f00-1a2b3c4d5e6f", "at": "2026-11-01T09:02:11Z",
     "server": "github", "tool": "gh_merge_pull_request", "raw": "merge_pull_request",
     "digest": "sha256:9c1f…", "seat": "backend-dev", "turn_id": "…", "launch_id": "…",
     "item": "ENG-42", "args": {"owner": "acme", "repo": "web", "pullNumber": 71},
     "status": "waiting", "answer": "", "answered_by": "", "answered_at": null}
  ],
  "builtin": [
    {"key": "work", "label": "Work items",
     "description": "Worklet, the company's tracker: read, file, discuss and move work.",
     "tools": [
       {"name": "list_work_items", "description": "…", "source": "builtin",
        "annotations": {"read_only": "yes", "destructive": "unknown",
                        "idempotent": "yes", "open_world": "unknown"},
        "risk": "read_only", "risk_declared": true, "external": true,
        "delivers": "", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"…": {}}},
        "group": "work", "gate": "worklet"}
     ]}
  ],
  "agents": [
    {"seat": "backend-dev", "name": "Backend Dev", "unit": "Engineering", "unit_key": "eng",
     "servers": [
       {"server": "github", "reason": "integration", "tools": 26, "state": "partial"},
       {"server": "linear", "reason": "unit", "tools": 31, "state": "running"}
     ],
     "mcp_tools": 57, "builtin_tools": 34, "over_budget": false}
  ],
  "tool_budget": 100
}
```

`builtin` is the engine's own tools as the company's agents are offered them (each agent all but those its `builtin_tools` below leaves out), group by group in the catalogue's order, each tool a [catalogue row](#the-tool-catalogue) whose `gate` says who may call it ([Groups, and who may call each one](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#groups-and-who-may-call-each-one)). It is the built-ins of the registry this node applied, which every node applies alike, plus `list_mcp_server_tools` and `activate_tool`, which the engine hands the onboarding pass and a worker and no registry holds. A group the company offers nothing of is left out (a company on Jira gets no `work` group, one on Slack no `chat` group). A node with no active revision sends an empty list.

`alarms`, in an administrator's reading only, are the [MCP alarms](alarms.md) standing on the answering node's latest evaluation, in the table's order: the evaluation its health count, `crewlet.alarm.active` gauge and alarm log lines were told, so they never disagree. Each is the table's `kind`, its `title` and `person` for a company owner, the longest-standing server's `detail`, the `remedy`, and `entries`, one per server it stands on in name order: `key` (the server), that server's own `detail`, `since` (when the instance down longest went down, or the wait held longest began; `null` for a refused name, which carries no instant), `seat` (the agent whose instance the detail names, `""` for a shared server's), and `fix`, the one gesture that fixes it, decided by the engine:

| `fix.kind` | For | Acts on |
|---|---|---|
| `restart` | `mcp_server_failing` and `mcp_server_partial` | [`POST /mcp-servers/{name}/retry`](#post-mcp-serversnameretry) on `fix.server`, with `fix.seat` where it names one agent's instance. A server nothing serves is restarted whole; a partial one only for the agent whose instance is down, so the agents it serves keep their sessions (a shared server's instance restarts on every node) |
| `integration` | `mcp_server_waiting_long` | The integration that mints `fix.seat`'s credential for `fix.server`, which the server's [detail](#get-mcp-serversname) names in `resolved.binding` |
| `edit` | `mcp_tools_refused` | The server's configuration: a shorter `tool_prefix`, or one, as each name's `message` in `refused_tools` says |
| `sign_in` | `mcp_oauth_needs_sign_in` and `mcp_oauth_expiring` | Signing the company in to `fix.server` again: [`POST /mcp-servers/{name}/oauth`](#post-mcp-serversnameoauth) |
| `approve` | `mcp_approval_waiting` | The calls `fix.seat`'s run holds for approval on `fix.server`, each answered with [`POST /mcp-approvals/{id}`](#post-mcp-approvalsid) by its id in `approvals` |
| `review` | `mcp_tools_changed` | The changes in `fix.server`'s [detail](#get-mcp-serversname) `changes`, each accepted or kept blocked with [`POST /mcp-servers/{name}/changes`](#post-mcp-serversnamechanges) |

The list is always present, and empty on a node that runs no state log, which evaluates no alarm: ask a data node.

`oauth`, on each server row of an administrator's reading, is the server's [OAuth sign-in](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#signing-in-with-oauth), `null` for a server not signed in to with OAuth. It is the grant's public half, never a token or the client's secret:

```json
{"grant": "authorization_code", "status": "connected", "client": "dcr",
 "client_id": "registered-client-id", "issuer": "https://auth.example.com",
 "resource": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp", "scopes": ["read", "offline_access"],
 "connected_by": "jane.doe", "connected_at": "2026-11-01T09:00:00Z",
 "expires_at": "2027-01-30T09:00:00Z", "failure": null}
```

`grant` is `authorization_code` (a person signs the company in) or `client_credentials` (the engine signs in as the company's [service identity](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#signing-in-as-a-service-identity)). A service identity is always `connected`, with `client` `""` (it registers nothing), the configured `client_id` and `scopes`, and `issuer`, `resource`, `connected_by`, `connected_at`, `expires_at` and `failure` empty: nobody signs in to it, and a credential its vendor refuses fails the server's instances (the row's `state`), never asks for a sign-in.

`status` is `connected` (the engine renews it as the server is used), `needs_sign_in` (nobody has signed in: `client_id` is then the company's own client's, or `""`, and the scopes are the ones the configuration asks for), `expired` (past the end its vendor stated) or `refresh_failed` (its vendor refused to renew it, `failure` carrying `{said, at}` in the vendor's words, bounded and redacted). `expires_at` is `null` where the vendor stated no end. `resource` is the server address the grant was issued for (RFC 8707), the only one its tokens are sent to.
`callback_url` and `client_metadata_url`, on the answer itself, are the two addresses a vendor that allowlists them is given: where it sends a person back after a sign-in, and the engine's client metadata document (the client id a `cimd` sign-in is made as). Each is `""` on an engine with no public address. A member's reading carries neither, and no `oauth`; it carries the state.

`approvals`, in an administrator's reading only, are the calls agents' runs hold for a person's approval ([Asking a person before a tool runs](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#asking-a-person-before-a-tool-runs)), the longest waiting first: each while its run is parked on it (`status: "waiting"`), and once an answer is recorded until the run carries on to its next job (`"answered"`, with the `answer` (`once`, `always` or `deny`), `answered_by` and `answered_at`, as the answer's seal opens on this node). `id` is what the call is answered by; `tool` is the tool as the run called it and `raw` the server's own name for it, which Always allow sets the level of; `digest` names the definition the run was offered; `item` is the key of the work item the run was on, or `null`. `args` are what the call would send, opened from their seal under this node's fleet keyring, `null` where they do not open here: as sent while the call waits on an answer the reader may give, redacted otherwise ([Asking a person before a tool runs](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#asking-a-person-before-a-tool-runs)). A member's reading carries no `approvals`. Always present.

`agents`, in an administrator's reading only, is every agent seat in the chart's order with the MCP tools its grants hand it, and `tool_budget` the count past which an agent is flagged: 100, the engine's own, which no setting moves ([Each agent's tools, and the budget](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#each-agents-tools-and-the-budget)).
- `unit` and `unit_key` are the name and key of the seat's unit, both `null` for a seat at the root of the chart.
- `servers` is every server the configuration declares whose grant reaches the seat, on or off, in name order. `reason` is why, as the server's [`reaches`](#get-mcp-serversname) says it (`every_agent`, `unit`, `seat` or `integration`). `tools` is how many tools it offers the agent: every tool the live nodes' listings name at a level other than `blocked` (a tool refused its name is never listed), except a tool the agent's own [limits](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#narrowing-a-server-for-a-team) block; the whole listing for each agent a per-agent server reaches; `0` for a server turned off (granted to nobody) or one a limit turns off for the agent. `state` is the server's own, its row's.
- `mcp_tools` counts each tool name once, even when two of the agent's servers list it.
- `builtin_tools` is how many tools in `builtin` the agent is offered; the budget does not count them. It is every one but those the engine leaves off: a tool whose `gate` is a grant the agent does not hold (`health_tools`, `ssh_read`, `ssh_operate`, `delegated_decisions`, or `growth_read`, `growth_operate` or `growth_administer` at the tool's growth product), and below `full_access` the code writes its `role.code.access` could never use ([Groups, and who may call each one](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#groups-and-who-may-call-each-one)). So it differs per agent.
- `over_budget` is `mcp_tools` above `tool_budget`. A server's tools count while it is down, since they come back with it.
- `agents` is `null` while the answering node has not read the fleet's listings yet, a moment after it starts; that is not an agent holding no tools.

To add a server, `PUT /config/mcp-servers/{name}` with `If-None-Match: *`, see [Per-entity read and write](#per-entity-read-and-write). A service identity (`oauth.grant: client_credentials`) written with no `oauth.client_secret` is written reading `${MCP_<SERVER>_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET}`, where [storing its secret](#put-mcp-serversnamevalueskey) puts it, on an add and on a replacement alike.

### `GET /mcp-catalogue`

What a server is added from, for the add flow of **Settings › MCP & tools**. It is decided by `tools.read`, so **it is everybody's**, in two readings. A caller `config.read` admits reads the answer below, `reading: "admin"`: the registry the company's configuration names, searched for `q`. Anybody else reads `{"reading": "member", "curated": [...]}`, the curated half alone whatever `q` says: the registry is an address an administrator chose (possibly on the company's own network), a search is a request the engine makes to it, and searching is part of adding a server. A plain read, not a question: nothing in it is live, so the
socket does not carry it. It sits outside `/mcp-servers/`, whose next segment is always a server's name, so a server may be called `catalogue` and still have its own [detail](#get-mcp-serversname).

`curated` is the curated catalogue whole, in its order, whatever `q` says: a table compiled into the engine and reviewed in pull requests, so it answers the same on a node with no egress. Each entry is a vendor's server as its own page described it on `read_at`; a local server launched through a package runner names the `package` it fetches at the exact `release` its facts were read against. The engine also [recognises a configured server by it](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#the-curated-catalogue-and-a-community-registry).

`community` is empty unless `q` is given and the company names a registry (`mcp_registry.url`), and then holds what that registry answered for `q`: the newest version of each server whose name holds `q`, at most 20, in the registry's order. The registry speaks the [MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) v0.1 API. Every listing is `community: true` and a draft for the same add flow an address typed by hand goes through: no `read_at`, `integration`, `prerequisite` or fixed `value`, and its `vendor` is set only when its remote address is a host the curated catalogue recognises. A listing is offered with a Streamable HTTP remote at a fixed https address, or else an npm or PyPI package from the public registry at an exact release, launched as `npx -y <package>@<release>` or `uvx <package>==<release>`. A listing the engine cannot read whole (a field past its bound, a direction override in its text, a templated address, a runner argument, a package from another registry, a deprecated or deleted listing) is left out and counted in `left_out`. The engine dials the registry alone, never anything a listing names, and follows no redirect.

`registry` is the address the company names, or `""`. `reason` says why a search found nothing to offer: the company names no registry, or the registry could not be reached, refused, or answered something that is not the v0.1 server list. A failed search is that `reason` beside the curated half, never an error in its place; only `q` itself (empty after trimming, over 200 characters, or holding a control character) is refused, as `bad_params`.

```json
{
  "reading": "admin",
  "curated": [
    {"id": "linear", "name": "linear", "title": "Linear", "vendor": "linear",
     "description": "Issues, projects, cycles and documents.", "transport": "http",
     "url": "https://mcp.linear.app/mcp", "command": "", "args": [],
     "headers": [{"name": "Authorization", "description": "A Linear API key.", "required": true,
                  "secret": true, "value": "", "format": "Bearer <API key>", "from_integration": false}],
     "env": [], "tool_prefix": "", "tool_annotations": {}, "auth": ["oauth", "headers"],
     "oauth_client": "cimd", "integration": "", "prerequisite": "",
     "docs": "https://linear.app/docs/mcp", "read_at": "2026-11-01", "package": "", "release": "",
     "community": false, "publisher": "", "version": "", "updated_at": null}
  ],
  "community": [
    {"id": "com.example/weather", "name": "weather", "title": "Weather", "vendor": "",
     "description": "Forecasts and alerts for a place.", "transport": "http",
     "url": "https://mcp.weather.example.com/mcp", "command": "", "args": [],
     "headers": [{"name": "X-API-Key", "description": "Your API key.", "required": true,
                  "secret": true, "value": "", "format": "", "from_integration": false}],
     "env": [], "tool_prefix": "", "tool_annotations": {}, "auth": ["headers"], "oauth_client": "",
     "integration": "", "prerequisite": "", "docs": "https://weather.example.com/docs/mcp",
     "read_at": "", "package": "", "release": "", "community": true,
     "publisher": "com.example", "version": "2.1.0", "updated_at": "2026-10-27T08:00:00Z"}
  ],
  "registry": "https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io",
  "reason": "",
  "left_out": 1
}
```

### `GET /mcp-servers/{name}`

One MCP server, whole, for its page under **Settings › MCP & tools**. Decided by `tools.read`, **so it is everybody's**, in the two readings `GET /mcp-servers` answers: a caller `config.read` admits reads the answer below, `reading: "admin"`; anybody else gets [a member's reading](#a-members-reading-of-mcp--tools).

**What the fleet lists, not what this node runs.** A per-agent server runs only on the nodes holding its seats, so the answer is the union of the live nodes' listings ([Tools and MCP › What every server lists](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#what-every-server-lists)). A node's listing counts only while it holds its presence at the epoch it wrote it under, so a drained, dead or restarted node stops counting at once.

- `server` is the server's row exactly as [`GET /mcp-servers`](#get-mcp-servers) answers it; `nodes` the live nodes its cells are drawn against.
- `listed` is each live node's listing: when it last changed (`at`), how many instances it is the union of, and how many tools it counts.
- `tools` is every tool a live node lists, by name, each once:
  - `name` as offered (`tool_prefix` applied), `raw` as the server names it, `title`, `description` (the server's words, cut to 1,024 bytes).
  - `annotations` with the company's overrides applied, as words (`yes`, `no`, `unknown`), and the engine's one reading of them: `risk` (`read_only`, `additive` or `destructive`; a tool declaring nothing is `destructive` with `risk_declared: false`) and `external` (whether a call may reach past the company; true unless the tool says not).
  - `digest` names the definition shown (the one most instances list); `definitions` counts the different definitions the fleet lists under the name (more than one mid-upgrade). `instances` and `nodes` are summed across the fleet.
  - `input_schema` and `output_schema` are the definition's schemas, or `null` where none is kept: no output schema published, schemas past 64 KiB, or a tool past its listing's 1 MiB of schemas (kept in name order).
  - `level` is the level the tool runs at, decided by the server's entry by `raw` (`tools.levels`, else `tools.default`, else the level its hints start it at): `allow`, `approve` (offered, each call held for a person's answer) or `blocked` (listed here, offered to no agent; [Tools and MCP › Setting each tool's level](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#setting-each-tools-level)). For a server the configuration does not declare, `level` says what the nodes did. `custom` is whether `tools.levels` names it.
  - `held` is a tool its level would run unasked whose definition changed since that level was decided, or that the server added after its first listing: its `level` answers `approve`, and each call asks a person until somebody accepts the change (`changes`).
  - `removed` is a tool the server no longer lists, kept, named by the definition accepted for it, with no instances or nodes, until somebody accepts that it went.
- `baseline` is the level of every tool `tools.levels` does not name: the entry's `tools.default`, or `null` where it sets none, leaving each at the level its hints start it at (`allow` where `risk` is `read_only`, else `approve`). `auto_accept_changes` is the entry's `tools.auto_accept_changes`: each change is accepted as it is listed rather than held for review ([Tools and MCP › Accepting a server's changes automatically](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#accepting-a-servers-changes-automatically)); `false` for a server the configuration does not declare. `unlisted_levels` are the tools `tools.levels` names that no live node lists, sorted: a level that decides nothing, most often a name written with the `tool_prefix` or spelled otherwise than the server spells it. Empty where the listings cannot say (no live node lists the server).
- `changes` is every change the server made to its tools since their levels were decided ([Tools and MCP › When a server changes a tool](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#when-a-server-changes-a-tool)), by `tool` (the server's own name), then by definition: one per tool listed under a definition nobody accepted (two nodes listing two such definitions make two changes), and one per accepted tool no live node lists, judged only where every live listing is whole. Empty for a server whose first listing is not accepted yet. The administrator's reading only.
  - `kinds` is `added` or `removed` alone, or the parts that moved: `title`, `description`, `schema`, `annotations`.
  - `before` is the definition accepted (`null` for an added tool), `after` the one listed now (`null` for a removed tool), each `{digest, whole, title, hints_title, description, annotations, risk, risk_declared, external, input_schema, output_schema}` read off the declared hints; `before` adds `accepted_by` (`null` for the server's first listing), `accepted_at`, `first_listing` and `auto_accepted` (accepted as listed under `tools.auto_accept_changes`, `accepted_by` naming the node); `after` adds `instances`.
  - `whole` is a definition read from the record the fleet keeps under its digest, words and schemas whole: `title` is the tool's own title, `hints_title` the one its hints carry. Where `whole` is `false` the fleet keeps no record, `title` and `description` are the words a listing keeps (a description's first KiB) and `hints_title` is `""`.
  - `unshown` names each part in `kinds` the answer cannot show: a part either side has no record for, or whose two sides read alike (say it changed and is not shown, never that nothing changed). Always a list.
  - `loosened` is a change whose hints claim less risk than the accepted ones; `held` whether it holds the tool at Needs approval now; `seen_at` when the fleet first stored the definition listed now (`null` for a removal, or a definition with no record).
- `server_info` (`name`, `title`, `version`, `protocol`) and `instructions` are what the server said of itself in its handshake, from the listing that changed last; `null` and `""` where no live node's listing carries them. Both are the server's own words, bounded.
- `dependants` is what removing the server takes with it, exactly as a dry run of [`DELETE /config/mcp-servers/{name}`](#delete-configmcp-serversid-remove-an-mcp-server-and-clear-what-names-it) answers: the `mcp_env` blocks and box entries it clears, and the stored values nothing reads once it is gone. Empty lists for a server the configuration does not declare.
- `instances` is every instance of the server, **read from the nodes holding them when you ask** ([Tools and MCP › A server's health](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#a-servers-health)): each node whose status record reports one, and each live node with no record counted, is asked over the broker within two seconds. A node answers at most 200 instances of a server. Each instance has:
  - `seat` (`""` for a shared server's one instance), `node`, `state` (`running`, `failed` or `waiting`), `since` (when that state began: its session's start, when it stopped serving or first failed, or when first held back), `restarts`, `tools`.
  - `failure` (why a failed instance is not serving: `{class, said, at, node, seat}`, `null` otherwise), `wait` (what a waiting one waits for), `last_failure` (its latest failure, kept after it came back), `last_answer` (when it last answered: a start that listed its tools, or a tool call that came back).
  - Every `said` is the engine's sentence carrying what a server or its process said: redacted, cut to 512 bytes, somebody else's text.
- `instance_nodes` names each node asked: whether it `answered`, the `reason` it is named for where it did not, and `count`, how many instances it holds, never fewer than it listed. A node that did not answer is never read as one holding nothing.
- `last_success` and `last_failure` are the latest answer and failure across the instances read, `null` where none.
- `last_check` is the server's latest test ([below](#post-mcp-serversnamecheck)), whoever asked through whichever node: `at`, `by`, the `seat` it was made for (`""` for a shared server), `ok`, and `nodes`, each as a test answers it but without its tools. `null` where never tested. An administrator's reading only.
- `values` is every header (remote server) or variable (local one) the server is sent, and the secret of the OAuth client it signs in with, by name and never by value. An administrator's reading only. What [`PUT /mcp-servers/{name}/values/{key}`](#put-mcp-serversnamevalueskey) stores. Each has:
  - `key` as the document spells it (`oauth.client_secret` for the client's secret); `as` (`header`, `env`, or `oauth` for the client's secret, which goes to the authorization server alone).
  - `variable`, the one variable it reads (`""` for a value written in the document, one reading several, or a key an integration binds per agent).
  - `set`: whether the secret store holds every variable it reads (a literal is set; a key bound per agent is never set at the server's level).
  - `stored_at` and `stored_by` from the variable's row (`null` where the store holds none); `optional` (`optional_keys` names it); `bound_by`, the integration that hands each agent its own value under the key, `null` for one the document sets.
- `reaches` is every agent seat the server's grant reaches, in the chart's order, each `{seat, reason, via}`; the grant itself, whether or not the server is on (a server turned off reaches these seats again once turned back on). Empty for a server the configuration does not declare ([Tools and MCP › Choosing which agents get a server](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#choosing-which-agents-get-a-server)). `reason` is:
  - `every_agent`: the entry has no `access`.
  - `unit`: a unit `access.units` names holds it; `via` is that unit's key, the nearest one named.
  - `seat`: `access.seats` names it.
  - `integration`: the server reads each agent's own vendor credential and the seat is on at its lane; `via` is the lane.

  `via` is `null` for the other two. Each also carries `limited`, what the seat's own `mcp_limits` and every enclosing unit's hold the server to, `null` where none does: `{off, off_by, tools}`. `off` is whether a limit turns the server off for the seat (its grant stands); `off_by` the key of the unit whose limit does (`null` for the seat's own, or where none does); `tools` every tool a limit holds back, sorted, as `{tool, level, by}`: the server's own name, `approve` or `blocked`, and the unit whose limit holds it (`null` for the seat's own). The tool runs at the stricter of that level and its own ([Tools and MCP › Narrowing a server for a team](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#narrowing-a-server-for-a-team)). An administrator's reading only.
- `resolved` is what the engine decides from the configuration, so a screen never re-derives it; `null` for a server the configuration does not declare:
  - `auth`: `integration` (a per-agent server reading each agent's own credential from one of the company's integrations), `headers` (the engine sends values the configuration sets, HTTP headers or a local server's environment) or `none`.
  - `runs_on`: `engine_host` for a local server, `""` for a remote one.
  - `timeouts`: `startup_seconds` and `request_seconds` in force (the engine's 120 and 300 where the configuration sets none) and whether each is the default.
  - `binding`: the integration a per-agent server reads: its `vendor`, `by` (`declared` in `seat_credentials` or `recognised` from its address or command), and the `keys` it is started with, `{field, key}` by name; `null` for none.
  - `box_seats`: the seats whose executor box is given the server through `sandbox.mcp.servers`, each with the `cell` its box runs in. A seat the server is not granted to is not one, nor is any seat while the server holds a tool back at a level other than `allow`.
  - `warnings`: placements expected to fail, `{seat, message}`: a local server given to a `container` box, whose image or a setup step must provide its command.
- `usage` is the server's calls per tool over the last seven company days, today included (`since`, `until`, `days`), every data node's, from the replicated `usage` domain ([Tools and MCP › How a server is used](../guides/tools-and-mcp.md#how-a-server-is-used)). A call counts on the day its turn ended.
  - `tools` has one row per tool called in the range: `tool` as offered (a `tools[].name`); `calls`; each call in exactly one outcome, `failed` (the server answered with a failure), `unavailable` (the server was not running) or `refused` (the engine refused it before it ran), the rest answered; `total_ms`, how long the calls that ran took between them; `last_at`, the newest call that ran (`null` when none did); `seats`, the handles of the seats that made them.
  - `elided` counts the entries the per-seat-day cap of 512 tools dropped in the range, on any server: zero says every count is whole.
- `calls` is the server's newest calls in the same days, at most 50, newest first, read out of the phase records on every data node: `calls[]` each `{at, seat, turn_id, tool, outcome, refusal, duration_ms}`. `outcome` is `answered`, `failed`, `unavailable` or `refused`; `refusal` the class of a failure the engine classified (`""` otherwise); `duration_ms` `null` for a call nothing timed. `coverage` says which data nodes answered ([coverage](#reading-the-fleets-history-coverage)).

Never a credential: no `env`, no `headers`, no seat's `mcp_env` value, and no call's arguments or result, which stay on the turn for whoever may read the seat's trail. A server no node configures, reports or lists is `404 not_found`. A node that has not yet read the fleet's listings, or could not read its store, answers `503 unavailable` with `Retry-After: 15`, never a server that lists nothing.

```json
{
  "reading": "admin",
  "server": {"name": "github", "title": "GitHub", "catalogue": "github", "vendor": "github",
             "configured": true, "shared": false, "enabled": true, "description": "",
             "transport": "stdio", "command": "github-mcp-server", "args": ["stdio"], "url": "",
             "state": "running", "started": 3, "failed": 0, "waiting": 0, "tools": 42,
             "unlisted_annotations": [], "unlisted_annotations_count": 0, "refused_tools": [],
             "refused_count": 0,
             "shadowed_tools": [], "shadowed_count": 0, "nodes": [{"node": "node-a", "reported": true,
             "started": 2, "failed": 0, "waiting": 0, "tools": 42, "error": "", "error_seat": "",
             "wait": "", "wait_seat": ""}]},
```

### A member's reading of MCP & tools

`GET /mcp-servers`, `GET /mcp-servers/{name}` and `GET /mcp-catalogue` answer anybody `config.read` does not admit in a member's reading, `reading: "member"`: each server's condition and its tools, and nothing that names a launch line, a header, a variable, an account or a call. It is built from types of its own, copied field by field, so a field added to the administrator's answer reaches no member until added here too.

A server's row carries `name`, `title`, `catalogue`, `vendor`, `configured`, `shared`, `enabled`, `description`, `transport`, `state`, `started`, `failed`, `waiting`, `tools`, `refused_tools`, `refused_count`, `shadowed_tools`, `shadowed_count` and `nodes`, each node's cell its counts, `error_class`, `down_since` and `restarts`. It leaves out `command`, `args` and `url`, each cell's `error` and `wait` sentences and the seats they name, and `unlisted_annotations` with its count (about a configuration only an administrator reads). The list's `nodes` and `builtin` are as an administrator reads them. It has no `alarms` (their detail quotes failure or wait sentences) and no `agents` or `tool_budget` (which servers an agent holds is read off the configuration's grants, as a seat's `tool_sources` on the org chart is, which no other reader gets either).

A server's detail carries `server` (the row above), `nodes`, `listed`, `tools` (every field, `held` and `removed` included), `server_info`, `last_success` and:

- `instances`, each without its `wait` (the variables a waiting instance waits for), and each `failure` and `last_failure` as `{class, at, node, seat}`, without `said`: what a server or its process said can name an address or an account;
- `instance_nodes` as `{node, answered, count}`, without the `reason` a node did not answer;
- `last_failure` as `{class, at, node, seat}`;
- `resolved` as `{auth, runs_on, timeouts, binding}`, `binding` as `{vendor, by}`, without the `keys`, the `box_seats` or the placement `warnings`;
- `usage` as `{since, until, days, tools, elided}`, each tool's row `{tool, calls, failed, unavailable, refused, total_ms, last_at}`, without the `seats` that called it: how often a tool is used tells a member whether it is, and who called it is the trail of that seat's work.

It leaves out `instructions`, `dependants`, `calls`, `reaches` and `changes`: a change is reviewed by who may decide it.

```json
{
  "reading": "member",
  "server": {"name": "github", "title": "GitHub", "catalogue": "github", "vendor": "github",
             "configured": true, "shared": false, "enabled": true, "description": "",
             "transport": "stdio", "state": "running", "started": 3, "failed": 0, "waiting": 0,
             "tools": 42, "refused_tools": [], "refused_count": 0, "shadowed_tools": [],
             "shadowed_count": 0, "nodes": [{"node": "node-a", "reported": true, "started": 2,
             "failed": 0, "waiting": 0, "tools": 42, "error_class": "", "down_since": null,
             "restarts": 1}]},
  "nodes": [{"id": "node-a", "reported": true}],
  "listed": [{"node": "node-a", "at": "2026-11-01T09:00:00Z", "instances": 2, "tools": 42}],
  "tools": [{"name": "get_issue", "raw": "get_issue", "title": "Get issue", "…": "…"}],
  "server_info": {"name": "github-mcp-server", "version": "0.31.0", "protocol": "2025-06-18"},
  "instances": [
    {"seat": "backend-dev", "node": "node-a", "state": "running", "since": "2026-11-01T08:40:00Z",
     "restarts": 1, "tools": 42, "failure": null,
     "last_failure": {"class": "exited", "at": "2026-11-01T08:39:58Z", "node": "node-a",
                      "seat": "backend-dev"},
     "last_answer": "2026-11-01T09:02:11Z"}
  ],
  "instance_nodes": [{"node": "node-a", "answered": true, "count": 1}],
  "last_success": "2026-11-01T09:02:11Z",
  "last_failure": {"class": "exited", "at": "2026-11-01T08:39:58Z", "node": "node-a",
                   "seat": "backend-dev"},
  "resolved": {"auth": "integration", "runs_on": "engine_host",
               "timeouts": {"startup_seconds": 120, "request_seconds": 300,
                            "startup_default": true, "request_default": true},
               "binding": {"vendor": "github", "by": "recognised"}},
  "usage": {"since": "2026-10-26", "until": "2026-11-01", "days": 7, "elided": 0,
            "tools": [{"tool": "get_issue", "calls": 18, "failed": 1, "unavailable": 0,
                       "refused": 0, "total_ms": 7380, "last_at": "2026-11-01T09:02:11Z"}]}
}
```

### `POST /mcp-servers/{name}/retry`

Restarts one MCP server now, for the **Restart** action on its page under **Settings › MCP & tools**: every instance on every node, or, with a `seat`, that agent's instance on the node holding the seat. Decided by `tools.retry`, **an administrator's at any recency** and Ask Crewlet's only on the person's approval. It changes runtime state only: each instance starts again from the spec it already runs.

The body is empty to restart every instance, or `{"seat": "<handle>"}` for one agent's. The answer is `202 Accepted` with the request as recorded:

```json
{"server": "tracker", "seat": "", "at": "2026-11-01T09:05:00Z", "node": "node-a"}
```

**A stamp, not a command.** The request is one record in the coordination store, which every node watches; each node restarts every instance it runs whose state began **before** `at`: a serving instance's session ends and a fresh one starts at once, a down instance is tried now with its restart schedule started again, and an agent's instance whose first start failed gets a pass now. Only the node holding a named seat acts. The restart has happened on a node once its instances read a `since` after `at` in [the server's detail](#get-mcp-serversname); the same request heard twice, late, or after a node restarts restarts nothing more. The record goes when the configuration stops declaring the server or the seat.

| Status | `error` | When |
|---|---|---|
| `404` | `not_found` | The configuration declares no such server |
| `409` | `conflict` | The server is turned off (`enabled: false`), so nothing runs it |
| `409` | `seat_not_granted` | The seat is not granted the server |
| `400` | `invalid_body` | A `seat` named for a shared server (one instance for the company); or a body with a field the route does not read |
| `404` | `no_such_seat` | The organization has no agent seat by that handle |
| `503` | `unavailable` | The node could not record the request; ask again |

Every call, the guard's refusals included, is one `mcp_server_acted` in the runtime audit: who asked, which server, the seat if one, and how it ended, never anything the server is started with.

### `POST /mcp-servers/{name}/check`

Tests one MCP server where it runs, for the **Test** action on its page under **Settings › MCP & tools**. Each node asked opens its own connection exactly as it starts the server (same transport, launch, scrubbed environment and startup timeout), walks its stages, lists its tools and closes it. **A test never calls a tool**, and the running server keeps serving beside it. Decided by `tools.check`, **an administrator's at any recency** and Ask Crewlet's only on the person's approval: it changes no configuration and no credential.

A shared server is tested on every node holding a presence lease; the body is empty. A per-agent server runs as one agent with its credentials, so it is tested for one seat on the node holding it: the body is `{"seat": "<handle>"}`, and no other node tests it.

The answer is `200` with what each node found:

```json
{
  "server": "tracker", "seat": "", "draft": false,
  "at": "2026-11-01T09:05:00Z", "by": "jane.doe", "node": "node-a", "ok": true,
  "nodes": [
    {"node": "node-a", "answered": true, "reason": "", "ok": true,
     "steps": [{"stage": "launch", "state": "passed", "took_ms": 41, "detail": "the process started"},
               {"stage": "discover", "state": "passed", "took_ms": 182, "detail": "tracker-mcp 1.2.0, protocol 2026-07-28"},
               {"stage": "list", "state": "passed", "took_ms": 33, "detail": "2 tools"}],
     "failure": null,
     "server_info": {"name": "tracker-mcp", "version": "1.2.0", "protocol": "2026-07-28"},
     "tools": 2, "refused": 0, "took_ms": 270},
    {"node": "node-b", "answered": false, "reason": "did not answer within 4m15s", "ok": false,
     "steps": [], "failure": null, "server_info": null, "tools": 0, "refused": 0, "took_ms": 0}
  ],
  "server_info": {"name": "tracker-mcp", "version": "1.2.0", "protocol": "2026-07-28"},
  "tools": [{"name": "tracker_search", "raw": "search", "title": "", "description": "Searches issues.",
             "annotations": {"read_only": "yes", "destructive": "unknown", "idempotent": "unknown", "open_world": "unknown"},
             "risk": "read_only", "risk_declared": true, "external": true,
             "starting_level": "allow", "refused": ""}],
  "warnings": []
}
```

- `steps` are the stages a node walked, in order. A remote server walks `address`, `resolve`, `connect`, `tls`, `discover` and `list`; a local one `launch`, `discover` and `list`. Each `state` is `passed`, `failed`, `skipped` (no name to look up for an address written as one, no TLS for plain http) or `not_reached` (after the stage that failed). `detail` is what the stage found, or the failure's sentence for the stage that failed.
- `failure` is why the test stopped on a node: its `class`, one of the fourteen failure classes `/mcp-servers` reports, decided at the stage whose facts produced it (a lookup at `resolve`, a dial at `connect`, a certificate at `tls`, what the server answered at `discover`, a command that could not start or a process that exited before it answered at `launch`), and `said`. A server that answers and lists no tool it can be offered under is `ok`, with the class `empty_tools`.
- `tools` and `server_info` come from the first node that found the server serving: each tool as the engine would offer it (prefixed name, hints with the configuration's overrides, `risk` as `/mcp-servers/{name}` reads it), `starting_level` (the level it starts at when the server is added: `allow` for a tool asserted read-only, else `approve`), and `refused`, why it would not be offered under its name (`characters`, `too_long` or `builtin`). `warnings` say each refusal in a sentence.

**Never in an answer:** a header or variable value the server is started with (a server or process that repeats one has it withheld), an address with a credential in it, the server's instructions. Every sentence is redacted and bounded to 512 bytes on the node that wrote it.

**The latest test is kept.** It is recorded in the coordination store, one record per server, and [the server's detail](#get-mcp-serversname) answers it as `last_check` to every administrator on any node. A later test replaces it; the record goes when the configuration stops declaring the server.

| Status | `error` | When |
|---|---|---|
| `404` | `not_found` | The configuration declares no such server |
| `409` | `conflict` | The server is turned off, so nothing runs it to test (test its entry as a draft instead) |
| `409` | `seat_not_granted` | The seat is not granted the server |
| `400` | `invalid_body` | A `seat` named for a shared server, none named for a per-agent one, or a body with a field the route does not read |
| `404` | `no_such_seat` | The organization has no agent seat by that handle |
| `503` | `unavailable` | The node could not ask the fleet; ask again |

A node that does not answer within the test's budget (twice the server's startup timeout, plus fifteen seconds to close what it started) is named in `nodes` with why, never read as one that found nothing. One test of a server (and seat) runs at a time on a node: a test asked while one runs there is answered at once, on that node, that one is running, and starts nothing beside it. Every call, the guard's refusals included, is one `mcp_server_acted` with the action `check`.

### `POST /mcp-checks`

Tests a **draft** MCP server entry before it is saved, for the test step of the add and edit flows. The body is the entry as `PUT /config/mcp-servers/{name}` would take it, the seat for a per-agent one, and the values typed for its keys that are not stored yet:

```json
{"entity": {"name": "wiki", "transport": "http", "url": "https://wiki.example.com/mcp"},
 "seat": "", "values": {"Authorization": "Bearer <token>"}}
```

**`values`** holds what the server would be sent under each key, as [`PUT /mcp-servers/{name}/values/{key}`](#put-mcp-serversnamevalueskey) stores it once the entry is written. For the test each key reads the variable that route would store its value under in the company the draft makes (the key's own `${VAR}` where only it reads one, else `MCP_<SERVER>_<KEY>`), ahead of anything the store holds under that name. A key that route would refuse (one an integration fills for each agent, a name no header or variable can have, a derived name another field already reads, a variable past the 255 bytes a secret's name may be) is refused here with the same answer. Each value is trimmed and must be one line; together they hold at most 64 KiB (one stored value's bound), past which the answer is `413`. **A value is never written, recorded, logged or answered.** The entry and every value cross the broker sealed under the fleet's keyring, each bound to the one test. A key whose value is already stored needs no entry: the draft's `${VAR}` resolves it.

A draft runs what a write would (a command on the engine host, or an address dialled with the entry's values), so it is decided as that write, **`config.write` and `secrets.write` on top of `tools.check`**, before the body is read: a person who may not write the company and its secrets is refused `403` (`step_up_required` for a proof older than the step-up window) and nothing is tested. Ask Crewlet never runs one, since `secrets.write` is never its.

The entry is held to the configuration's own dry run, in the company it would join (a create for a new name, an edit for an existing one); an entry the dry run refuses is answered `422 validation_error` with the problems a write would get. An admitted draft is tested as the dry run left it, turned on whatever its `enabled` says, on the nodes the saved entry would run on, and answered as [`POST /mcp-servers/{name}/check`](#post-mcp-serversnamecheck) answers, with `"draft": true`. Tested for an agent (`seat`), it is started with what the saved entry would start that agent's instance with: the agent's own values, its unit's, and its own credential at every integration the entry reads, bound as the save will bind it. **A draft's test is never recorded**: the server's latest test is of the entry the company runs.

### `POST /mcp-probe`

Checks an address before an MCP server is added at it, for the address step of the add flow: what answers there, and how it is signed in to. The body is `{"url": "https://..."}`. The address is dialled as the server would be once added, a private one included, so it is decided as that write: **`config.write` on top of `tools.check`**, before the body is read. It resolves no secret and sends no credential.

```json
{
  "address": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp", "reachable": true,
  "check": {"node": "", "answered": true, "reason": "", "ok": false,
            "steps": [{"stage": "address", "state": "passed", "took_ms": 0, "detail": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp"},
                      {"stage": "discover", "state": "failed", "took_ms": 210, "detail": "..."}],
            "failure": {"class": "needs_sign_in", "said": "..."}, "server_info": {"name": "", "title": "", "version": "", "protocol": ""},
            "tools": 0, "refused": 0, "took_ms": 380},
  "auth": "oauth",
  "oauth": {"resource_metadata": "https://mcp.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp",
            "resource": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
            "authorization_servers": ["https://auth.example.com"], "issuer": "https://auth.example.com",
            "scopes": ["read", "write"], "client": "dcr", "pkce": true, "failure": null},
  "tools": null, "catalogue": "", "title": "", "vendor": ""
}
```

- `check` is the address's walk with nothing configured, as a node's test is answered.
- `auth` is the sign-in the server asks for: `none` where it lists its tools to no credential (`tools` counts them), `oauth` where it answers `401` with a Bearer challenge and publishes protected-resource metadata, `headers` where it refuses another way or publishes none, `""` where the check reached no answer to tell by. `reachable` is whether an MCP server answered at all: its handshake, or a refusal asking for a credential.
- `oauth` is what the server's sign-in metadata says: the protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728) at the address its challenge names, or at the well-known address on its own origin, and the metadata of the first authorization server it names (RFC 8414, or OpenID Connect discovery): its `issuer`, the `scopes`, how the engine would register as a client (`cimd` where it reads a client metadata document, `dcr` where it offers dynamic registration, `own` for a client an administrator registers), and whether it offers PKCE `S256`. `failure` is why the discovery stopped short.
- `catalogue`, `title` and `vendor` name the curated entry the address is, `""` where the curated catalogue does not know it.

**Whose address each request goes to.** The typed address is the operator's. Every other address the check reaches is one the server named, in its challenge or metadata, and is fetched only through the engine's public-address guard (ADR-0072) unless it is on the typed address's own origin, over https alone, following no redirect, reading at most 64 KiB, within ten seconds. An address the guard refuses ends the discovery with the class `blocked_address`: the server's sign-in points somewhere the engine does not follow. Metadata naming another issuer than the one asked for is not used. An address the configuration's own rule refuses (plain http to a public host, a user name or password in it) stops at the `address` stage, dialling nothing. Every call is one `mcp_server_acted` with the action `probe`, naming the address with its credentials withheld.
### `PUT /mcp-servers/{name}/values/{key}`

Stores one header of a remote server, or one variable of a local one, from the
server's page: what the server is sent under `key`, whole (`"Bearer <API
key>"`, as the curated catalogue's format says), as `{"value": "..."}`. The
value is sealed **write-only** in the fleet's secret store and the key reads it
through a `${VAR}`: no credential enters the company document and no route
answers the value again.

| Query | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seat=<handle>` | One seat's value of a per-agent server (`shared: false`), written into that seat's `mcp_env` block, which the engine lays over the server's own keys. Only a seat already granted the server takes one; storing never grants. Refused `400 invalid_query` for a shared server |
| `test=true\|false` | Test the value before storing it (the default). A per-agent server's value can only be tested as one of its seats, so without `seat` it is stored with `test=false` or refused `400 invalid_query` |
